43090473.titulo: Gut Microbiota Restructuring and Elizabethkingia Enrichment in Aedes albopictus Larvae Under Pyriproxyfen Exposure
43090473.autores: Xie LH, Xu SY, … Chen H (8 autores)
43090473.resumo: Reestruturação da microbiota intestinal de larvas de Aedes albopictus sob piriproxifeno, com enriquecimento de Elizabethkingia. (resumo a partir do título; abstract não lido)
43090473.resumo_original: Aedes albopictus transmits dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses, and its expanding range, together with widespread insecticide resistance, threatens the sustainability of chemical vector control. Pyriproxyfen (PPF) is an insect growth regulator used in mosquito control, but the relationship between gut bacteria and larval responses to PPF remains poorly characterized. We combined 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with culture-dependent isolation to characterize gut bacterial communities in Ae. albopictus following acute PPF exposure and identify candidates for functional investigation. The 24 h median lethal concentration (LC50) for the Fuzhou population was 10.27 mg/L. Community profiles were compared among Fuzhou larvae dying at 2× LC50, surviving at 5× LC50, and receiving solvent alone; solvent-treated Foshan laboratory larvae served as an external population reference. Bacterial richness and Shannon diversity were lower in both exposed Fuzhou groups than in the Fuzhou solvent-treated control, and community structure differed among the four groups (PERMANOVA, R2 = 0.797, p = 0.001). Elizabethkingia accounted for 35.0% of bacterial reads in survivors, compared with 22.8% in non-survivors and 7.6% in Fuzhou solvent-treated controls, with significantly higher relative abundance in survivors than in either comparison group. Culture-dependent isolation from survivors yielded 29 isolates representing nine genera, including three isolates assigned to Elizabethkingia anophelis by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Concordant sequencing and culture-based evidence, together with the recovery of viable isolates, positions Elizabethkingia as a tractable entry point into this question, opening a route to ask whether the larval microbiota can be managed to preserve the efficacy of pyriproxyfen-based control as resistance to other insecticide classes spreads.

resumo_blocos.racional: O regulador de crescimento de insetos piriproxifeno (PPF) é amplamente usado no controle larvário de Aedes albopictus, mas pouco se sabia sobre como a exposição aguda ao PPF reestrutura a microbiota bacteriana intestinal e se determinados táxons bacterianos associam-se à sobrevivência larval.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Sequenciamento de amplicons do gene 16S rRNA combinado ao isolamento bacteriano dependente de cultivo em larvas de Ae. albopictus da população de Fuzhou mortas a 2× CL50 (CL50 24 h = 10,27 mg/L), sobreviventes a 5× CL50 e controles tratados com solvente, tendo a linhagem laboratorial Foshan como referência externa.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A exposição ao PPF reduziu a riqueza bacteriana e a diversidade de Shannon em relação ao controle de Fuzhou e alterou significativamente a estrutura comunitária entre os quatro grupos (PERMANOVA, R2 = 0,797; p = 0,001). O gênero Elizabethkingia alcançou 35,0% das leituras bacterianas nos sobreviventes a 5× CL50, contra 22,8% nos não-sobreviventes a 2× CL50 e apenas 7,6% nos controles com solvente. O cultivo a partir de larvas sobreviventes recuperou 29 isolados de nove gêneros, incluindo três isolados identificados por 16S rRNA como Elizabethkingia anophelis.

43090472.titulo: Tetracycline Exposure Disrupts Gut Microbiota and Immune-Antioxidant Homeostasis in Honey Bees
43090472.autores: Hao M, Wang X, … Liu Y (7 autores)
43090472.resumo: Tetraciclina perturba a microbiota intestinal e a homeostase imune-antioxidante em abelhas. (resumo a partir do título; abstract não lido)
43090472.resumo_original: Antibiotic exposure can perturb the gut microbiota of honey bees, but its associations with host physiological responses remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the effects of tetracycline exposure on survival, locomotor activity, gut bacterial communities, and immune- and antioxidant-related gene expression in Apis mellifera workers maintained under controlled laboratory cage conditions. Tetracycline exposure at 100, 300, and 450 μg/mL reduced worker survival in a concentration-dependent manner, while 100 μg/mL increased daytime locomotor activity without affecting sucrose consumption. Tetracycline also altered gut bacterial community structure, with marked reductions in several core taxa, particularly Snodgrassella and Bartonella, whereas Commensalibacter, Lactobacillus Firm4 and Firm5 increased, especially at the highest concentration. Changes in immune- and antioxidant-related gene expression were more pronounced in the gut than in the head. Moreover, Snodgrassella abundance was positively correlated with Relish expression in the head and with Apidaecin and CAT expression in the gut. These findings demonstrate that tetracycline exposure reduces honey bee survival and is associated with coordinated alterations in gut bacterial communities and host physiological responses.

43090539.titulo: Dissecting the Lethal Mechanism of Silencing TcSP3 in Tetranychus cinnabarinus Eggs Reveals a Biosafety-Favorable RNAi Target
43090539.autores: Chen X, Zeng S, … Lu W (5 autores)
43090539.resumo: Silenciamento de TcSP3 em ovos de Tetranychus cinnabarinus como alvo de RNAi favorável à biossegurança. (resumo a partir do título; abstract não lido)
43090539.resumo_original: Serine proteases are essential for development and physiology in arthropods. We previously showed that RNAi-mediated silencing of the serine protease gene TcSP3 induces embryonic lethality in the carmine spider mite, Tetranychus cinnabarinus, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. Here, we adopted an integrated strategy-transcriptome sequencing, RT-qPCR validation, and gene-specific RNAi-to pursue two distinct but complementary objectives: (i) to map the downstream transcriptional response to TcSP3 silencing and thereby identify candidate RNAi targets and (ii) to functionally interrogate the leading candidate, TcHKB, in order to infer the lethal mechanism. We additionally performed a preliminary evaluation of the environmental biosafety of the resulting candidate dsTcHKB for RNAi-based mite management. TcSP3 silencing altered 495 genes (464 upregulated and 31 downregulated). Six downregulated candidate genes were validated; among these, silencing TcHKB resulted in the highest egg mortality (53.57%), accompanied by malformation and incomplete development, whereas silencing TcbHLH and Tcngn-1 caused 34.99% and 22.93% mortality. Sequence homology and domain prediction indicate that TcHKB encodes a Sp5-like transcription factor of the Sp/KLF family, suggesting that TcHKB may indirectly affect developmental signaling. The downregulation of TcHKB is therefore proposed as a possible, yet unverified, explanation for the observed embryonic lethality; direct measurements of Sp5, β-catenin, or Wnt pathway activity are still required to confirm this link. For translational application, we also conducted a preliminary biosafety evaluation of dsTcHKB. Under our tested conditions, sequence alignment showed no extensive homology between dsTcHKB and genes of the predatory mite N. barkeri, and direct bioassays detected no adverse effects on its survival, hatchability, or development; the dsRNA additionally degraded almost completely on cowpea leaves within three days. These initial observations address two specific risk aspects-environmental dissipation on cowpea leaves and non-target effects on N. barkeri-but do not yet establish general safety. This study suggests a plausible mechanism for TcSP3/TcHKB-mediated lethality and identifies TcHKB as a candidate RNAi target warranting further biosafety assessment.

43090463.titulo: BeetleFormer: A Sequence Transformer for Identifying Effective Double-Stranded RNAs in the Red Flour Beetle, Tribolium castaneum
43090463.autores: Xu J, Zhang W, … Yang J (5 autores)
43090463.resumo: BeetleFormer: transformer de sequência para prever dsRNAs eficazes em Tribolium castaneum. (resumo a partir do título; abstract não lido)
43090463.resumo_original: Selecting double-stranded ribonucleic acid (dsRNA) reagents remains a bottleneck in insect gene-function research and RNA interference (RNAi)-based pest management. We developed BeetleFormer to learn sequence patterns associated with RNAi screening outcomes in Tribolium castaneum. The model integrates multiscale convolutions, long-range attention, complementary-strand symmetry and sequence descriptors. Following previous dsRNA prescreening research, 14,821 iBeetle reagents meeting mortality or phenotype criteria were used as positives and 14,825 messenger RNA (mRNA) fragments as negative samples. Source genes and overlapping sequences were separated across training, validation and testing. On 6083 test sequences, BeetleFormer achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.978, accuracy 0.913 and Matthews correlation coefficient 0.831, compared with 0.888, 0.817 and 0.636 for an adapted convolutional-recurrent comparator. Ablations supported local processing and strand symmetry; AUC remained 0.976 after exact-length matching. External testing on 20 published dsRNAs and 20 mRNA negatives yielded AUC 0.928. Model interpretation revealed terminally concentrated sequence sensitivity and organized learned representations. These findings establish an improved sequence-based prescreen that turns genome-scale RNAi observations into candidate-selection evidence, supporting functional-genomics experiments and the development of RNAi-based pest control.

43090489.titulo: Functional Characterization of Prothoracicotropic Hormone in Larval Development and Diapause of Ostrinia furnacalis
43090489.autores: Cao S, Jia J, … Ma H (6 autores)
43090489.resumo: O neuropeptídeo PTTH regula desenvolvimento e diapausa em Ostrinia furnacalis; seu silenciamento reduz sinalização de insulina/IGF e reprograma metabolismo lipídico. (resumo a partir do título; abstract não lido)
43090489.resumo_original: Prothoracicotropic hormone (PTTH) is a secretory neuropeptide initiating insect metamorphosis via ecdysteroid synthesis. While the PTTH-ecdysone axis is well-established in development, its specific role in diapause regulation and the underlying mechanisms in agricultural pests like Ostrinia furnacalis are less understood. To address this, we identified O. furnacalis' PTTH gene (OfPTTH) and investigated its spatiotemporal expression and function using RNAi and 20-hydroxyecdysone (20E) rescue assays. Our findings show that OfPTTH expression was lowest during diapause, significantly increasing upon its termination, and exhibiting an extended developmental periodicity during diapause. OfPTTH-silencing was associated with reduced expression of ecdysone-signaling genes, leading to broad physiological disruptions including altered ecdysone and juvenile hormone signaling, inhibited insulin/IGF signaling, suppressed lipid metabolic reprogramming (triglyceride accumulation), and decreased heat shock protein expression. These events ultimately caused larval diapause-like developmental arrest, pupation failure, and mortality. Exogenous 20E treatment promoted pupation in OfPTTH-knockdown larvae and restored the expression of several downstream ecdysone-signaling genes, suggesting that impaired 20E signaling contributes to the observed developmental abnormalities. This study supports an important role of the PTTH-20E axis in O. furnacalis development and diapause-associated regulation and provides a basis for further evaluation of OfPTTH as a potential target for RNAi-based pest management.

43090495.titulo: Knockdown of ncm Induces Significant Mortality of Phyllotreta striolata
43090495.autores: Chen K, Ren H, … Chen M (9 autores)
43090495.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Knockdown of ncm Induces Significant Mortality of Phyllotreta striolata», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43090495.resumo_original: The striped flea beetle, Phyllotreta striolata, is one of the most destructive pests in Brassicaceae plants worldwide. RNA interference (RNAi) has been proven to be a promising alternative strategy for pest control, especially for P. striolata, since its larvae feed on roots and the adults feed on leaves. Gene ncm is critical for insect physiological process, as it is responsible for processing precursor mRNA into mature mRNA. In this study, we cloned and characterized the ncm gene (Psncm) from P. striolata. Additionally, we found silencing Psncm either by microinjection or oral delivery led to the high mortality of P. striolata adults. Moreover, the onset of feeding refusal was observed on day 3 in Psncm-silenced P. striolata. Finally, a total of 875 differentially expressed genes were identified in dsPsncm-injection treatment, among which 322 were upregulated and 553 were downregulated. Additionally, these genes were mainly clustered in "metabolism" and "organism systems" pathways. Consistent with the transcriptome analysis, metabolomics analysis revealed that silencing of Psncm was associated with significant alterations in multiple metabolic pathways. These results suggest that Psncm is a potential candidate for RNAi-based pest management, although further functional validation, field delivery, dsRNA stability, non-target safety, and resistance risk assessment are needed.

43088053.titulo: Structural and Compositional Characterization of a Human Adipose Allograft for Soft Tissue Volume Restoration
43088053.autores: Bouamar H, Fanniel V, … Hill S (8 autores)
43088053.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Structural and Compositional Characterization of a Human Adipose Allograft for Soft Tissue Volume Restoration», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43088053.resumo_original: Subcutaneous adipose tissue loss from trauma, congenital deformity, aging, or weight loss can compromise facial contour, symmetry, and soft-tissue support, making volume restoration a central target in soft-tissue reconstruction. Current approaches include autologous fat grafting, dermal fillers, and decellularized adipose matrices, each having distinct limitations related to tissue harvesting, material composition, durability, or absence of adipocyte structure. To address these limitations, dermaClaeTM was developed as a ready-to-use, minimally manipulated nonviable human structural adipose allograft for small volume applications in delicate areas, such as the face. This study characterizes the structural and compositional properties of dermaClae using histology, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and biochemical assays to evaluate tissue structure, composition, and extracellular matrix (ECM) components relevant to tissue integration and remodeling. Histological and SEM analyses demonstrated adipocytes surrounded by collagen-rich connective tissue. Adipocyte cross-sectional area demonstrated overlapping distributions with native adipose tissue. Total collagen, laminin α4, proteoglycans, and elastin levels were all measured in dermaClae at concentrations higher than native adipose tissue. Retained adipocyte structures contribute to tissue bulk, cushioning, and support, while the ECM provides a structural framework relevant to incorporation and remodeling. Together, these characteristics may position dermaClae as a potential natural alternative to current approaches for facial reconstruction.

43093728.titulo: Surface Engineering of Organosilica Nanoparticles Modulates Cellular Uptake, Cytotoxicity, and Mechanobiological Responses
43093728.autores: Mun EA, Zhaisanbayeva BA, … Khutoryanskiy VV (9 autores)
43093728.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Surface Engineering of Organosilica Nanoparticles Modulates Cellular Uptake, Cytotoxicity, and Mechanobiological Responses», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43093728.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: Surface chemistry is a major determinant of nanoparticle-cell interactions, yet their influence on mechanobiological properties of cells remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the cytotoxic and mechanobiological effects of thiolated and PEGylated organosilica nanoparticles and evaluated whether cortical stiffness could serve as a complementary measure of nanoparticle-cell interactions. Methods: We evaluated thiolated organosilica nanoparticles (Si NP-SH) and two PEGylated nanoparticles (Si NP-PEG750 and Si NP-PEG5000) in non-cancerous human pulmonary fibroblasts (HPF) and cancerous human pulmonary adenocarcinoma (A549) cells. We assessed cellular viability and nanoparticle uptake after exposure and used atomic force microscopy to measure cellular cortical stiffness. Additionally, nanoparticle effects on neuroblast proliferation and mitotic progression were examined in Drosophila melanogaster larval brain explants. Results: HPF cells were markedly less sensitive to all nanoparticle formulations across the tested concentration range, whereas A549 cells showed dose-dependent sensitivity, with thiolated nanoparticles producing the earliest and greatest reduction in viability. Despite a comparable uptake of Si NP-SH and Si NP-PEG750, the thiolated nanoparticles produced greater toxicity, whereas Si NP-PEG5000 showed lower uptake but intermediate toxicity. Atomic force microscopy measurements demonstrated significant cortical softening in Si NP-SH-treated A549 cells, while HPF cells were unaffected. All nanoparticles reduced Drosophila melanogaster neuroblast proliferation in a similar order: Si NP-SH > Si NP-PEG750 > Si NP-PEG5000. Conclusions: The biological activity of organosilica nanoparticles is predominantly dependent on accessibility and intracellular reactivity of surface thiols rather than uptake alone. PEGylation shields thiol reactivity, with higher PEG molecular weight additionally reducing nanoparticle uptake. The consistency of viability, uptake, cortical stiffness, and neuroblast proliferation identifies AFM-derived cortical stiffness as a valuable complementary measurement of nanoparticle-induced stress.

43090534.titulo: Effects of Oral and Volatile Peppermint Oil Exposure on Feeding and Hypopharyngeal Gland Development in Young Worker Honey Bees (Apis mellifera)
43090534.autores: Kim YH, Kim JM, … Oh D (7 autores)
43090534.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Effects of Oral and Volatile Peppermint Oil Exposure on Feeding and Hypopharyngeal Gland Development in Young Worker Honey Bees (Apis mellifera)», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43090534.resumo_original: Protein nutrition during early adulthood is closely associated with hypopharyngeal gland (HPG) development in worker honey bees, but whether peppermint oil (PO) influences this physiology and whether its effects depend on exposure route remain unclear. Newly emerged Apis mellifera workers were exposed for up to six days to dietary PO (0.05%, w/w), volatile PO (0.05% in paraffin oil, v/v), both routes, or control conditions. Protein-patty mass disappearance and recorded deaths were monitored daily, while body and head weight, HPG acinus area, feeding- and nutrient-associated gene expression in the brain and fat body, HPG mrjp1 expression, and MRJP1 protein abundance were assessed at designated sampling points. PO-exposed cages showed greater cumulative protein-patty mass disappearance and significantly altered feeding- and nutrient-associated gene expression, although individual molecular responses varied among exposure routes. All PO-treated groups had larger HPG acinus areas than controls on days 4 and 7; mrjp1 expression was significantly higher in PO-F on day 4 and in all PO-treated groups on day 7. MRJP1 protein abundance was also increased in all PO treatments. Volatile exposure showed numerically higher mortality on observation day 3, but cumulative mortality did not differ significantly from the control. These results indicate that dietary and volatile PO exposure were associated with changes in feeding-related measures and HPG development in young worker honey bees.

43076098.titulo: Gut microbiome stability and mycotoxin degradation confer aflatoxin B1 tolerance in Folsomia candida (Collembola)
43076098.autores: Wang K, Zhang Y, … Xu Y (8 autores)
43076098.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Gut microbiome stability and mycotoxin degradation confer aflatoxin B1 tolerance in Folsomia candida (Collembola)», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43076098.resumo_original:
Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a potent carcinogen that contaminates food and feed, causing significant economic losses and health problems in animals. Soil-dwelling arthropods such as Collembola often coexist with molds and are thought to tolerate toxic fungi, yet their responses to mycotoxins remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the effects of AFB1 on Folsomia candida. We found that AFB1 exposure caused dose-dependent increases in mortality, reductions in body size, and declines in reproductive output of this species. Remarkably, the growth retardation induced by AFB1 was largely alleviated upon removal of AFB1 from the diet. Analysis of gut microbial communities showed that high concentrations of AFB1 had little effect on overall community composition; the gut microbiota was dominated by the phyla Pseudomonadota and Bacillota and by the genera Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, and Enterobacter. Metagenomic profiling suggested that Wolbachia possesses the potential capability against AFB1. Furthermore, a large proportion of culturable gut bacterial isolates were found to be tolerant of AFB1 and could degrade it to varying degrees. Thus, while high AFB1 levels negatively affect F. candida's fitness, they do not perturb its gut bacterial community and its ability to degrade AFB1, indicating an adaptation of this host-microbiome system to AFB1 exposure.
Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a widespread mycotoxin that threatens food safety and animal health, but how soil animals tolerate AFB1 remains poorly understood. We show that the soil springtail F. candida is highly tolerant to AFB1 even though high doses reduce survival, growth, and reproduction. Notably, AFB1 exposure caused little change in gut microbial community structure. In addition, many gut bacterial isolates tolerated AFB1 and degraded it in vitro. These results suggest that microbiome stability and microbial detoxification capacity may help F. candida persist in mycotoxin-contaminated environments. Our study also highlights toxin-tolerant soil animals as a potential source of microorganisms and functions for aflatoxin biodegradation.

43096003.titulo: Defining the Diphyllin Pharmacophore for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral V-ATPase Inhibition by Structure-Guided Scaffold Modifications
43096003.autores: Elkabbany A, Sanford LM, … Davisson VJ (17 autores)
43096003.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Defining the Diphyllin Pharmacophore for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral V-ATPase Inhibition by Structure-Guided Scaffold Modifications», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43096003.resumo_original: The threat of emerging viral diseases presents a critical societal need for broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics. A key contribution to antiviral options would be a broad-spectrum agent that can treat a wide variety of viral diseases. Vacuolar H-ATPase (V-ATPase), a host proton pump critical for endosomal acidification, serves an essential role in facilitating the entry of multiple viruses. Diphyllin, a naturally occurring V-ATPase inhibitor, displays potent antiviral activity but is limited by suboptimal drug-like properties, including selectivity and metabolic instability. Molecular modeling enabled the identification of a conserved binding site on the V-ATPase a-subunit consisting of three distinct sub-pockets. Docking analyses of ninety-five known diphyllin derivatives demonstrated that active analogs effectively occupy all three subpockets, informing a structure-based design approach. A library of novel diphyllin analogs with modifications to a single-ring system showed 50-fold increases in potency for antiviral activity against Ebola, Venezuelan equine encephalitis, and Chikungunya viruses and exhibiting improvements in metabolic stability and permeability.

43093858.titulo: Are Viruses a Cause of Urinary Tract Infections? A Narrative Review
43093858.autores: Gebremedhin KB, Amogne W, … Eguale T (4 autores)
43093858.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Are Viruses a Cause of Urinary Tract Infections? A Narrative Review», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093858.resumo_original: Urinary tract infections (UTIs), often associated with the lower urinary tract, are a major public health problem. Traditionally, urine has been believed to be sterile in healthy individuals, but increasing evidence shows that the urinary tract may contain a variety of viruses even in healthy populations. Bacteria remain the major etiologic agents of UTIs, but growing evidence points to viruses as emerging causes. This narrative review focuses on six viruses: adenoviruses, cytomegalovirus (CMV), BK virus (human polyomavirus), severe acute respiratory syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), Zika virus, and West Nile virus. West Nile virus has been detected in urine without clear evidence of causing UTIs; however, the other five viruses reviewed in this narrative discuss have been associated with UTIs and may lead to various complications. Management of viral UTIs is mainly supportive, with reduced immunosuppression, symptom alleviation, prevention of complications, and monitoring of response to therapy. Key interventions include managing secondary bacterial infections, ensuring adequate hydration, using analgesics for pain and discomfort, and closely monitoring for treatment failure or recurrence. Effective prevention and control of viral infections also rely on broader public health strategies, including vaccination, sanitation, surveillance, early diagnosis, and appropriate treatment. Additional approaches may include prophylaxis, preemptive therapy, virus-specific treatments, and donor-recipient serostatus matching. Regular monitoring and careful adjustment of immunosuppressive therapy are also important, as no effective vaccine is available except for Ad4/Ad7 and SARS-CoV-2, and definitive preventive strategies are currently unavailable. Future research should focus on developing safe and effective antivirals and vaccines to prevent and treat viral UTIs and their complications.

43093103.titulo: California West Nile Virus Forecasting Challenge 2024
43093103.autores: Sánchez C HM, Danforth ME, … León TM (10 autores)
43093103.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «California West Nile Virus Forecasting Challenge 2024», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093103.resumo_original: West Nile virus (WNV) is the primary cause of mosquito-borne disease in California and the continental United States. Between 2003 (its year of introduction to California) and 2024, over 8200 symptomatic human cases, including 5083 severe neuroinvasive cases and 406 deaths, have been reported. In California, 52 out of 58 counties have had a reported WNV case. Following the example set by prior national WNV forecasting challenges, the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) launched the 2024 forecasting challenge with the aim of predicting symptomatic cases each month during the typical WNV season for a select group of high-burden counties in California: Placer, Sacramento, Solano, San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Fresno, Tulare, Kern, San Bernardino, Los Angeles, Orange, and Riverside. County-month predictions were solicited as probability bins and evaluated by the logarithmic score. The 2024 WNV season in California had low activity, with 131 cases statewide (85 in challenge counties), compared with a ten-year median of 334 cases statewide (236 cases in challenge counties). Overall, the ensemble outperformed all individual models, and machine learning models were the best-performing model class. Forecasts performed better for counties with lower historical variance in case activity.

43080537.titulo: Circular RNAs in metabolic reprogramming and therapy resistance in prostate cancer: emerging links to the tumor immune microenvironment
43080537.autores: Zhou P, Zhang F, … Song G (8 autores)
43080537.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Circular RNAs in metabolic reprogramming and therapy resistance in prostate cancer: emerging links to the tumor immune microenvironment», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43080537.resumo_original: Therapy resistance in prostate cancer can emerge at different disease stages; castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) is one clinically important state, and resistance to individual therapies may overlap but is not synonymous with CRPC. Metabolic reprogramming-including changes in glycolysis, de novo lipogenesis, glutamine metabolism, and mitochondrial homeostasis-has been implicated in prostate cancer progression and treatment resistance, although the strength of evidence varies across pathways and treatment settings. CircRNAs have been reported to modulate selected metabolic nodes in prostate cancer, although direct links between circRNA-associated metabolic changes and acquired therapy resistance are established only in a subset of studies. This review evaluates circRNAs as candidate regulators of selected metabolic processes in therapy-resistant prostate cancer. Mechanistically, individual circRNAs have been associated with selected metabolic changes through proposed miRNA-mediated interactions and, in some reports, peptide translation or protein scaffolding. These metabolic changes could, in principle, intersect with immunometabolic programmes such as lactate-associated suppression, lipid-linked macrophage states, and adenosine signalling; however, direct evidence that individual circRNAs control these immune-cell processes in CRPC remains limited, as detailed in the evidence tiers later in this review. Therapy-specific resistance networks are organised for enzalutamide/androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, PARP inhibitors and radiotherapy, distinguishing metabolism-dependent axes from signalling, mitotic, DNA-repair and exosome-propagated routes. Beyond mechanistic insights, circRNAs hold promise as non-invasive liquid-biopsy biomarkers and as druggable targets amenable to antisense oligonucleotide silencing, mimic delivery, and engineered circRNA vaccines. Major barriers to clinical translation include incomplete multi-therapy metabolic maps, sparse stage-resolved evidence across the hormone-sensitive→CRPC→neuroendocrine continuum, and unresolved delivery, safety, and regulatory challenges. Overall, current evidence supports circRNA-associated metabolic vulnerabilities as a promising preclinical research framework; however, circRNA-targeted metabolic interventions for therapy-resistant prostate cancer have not yet been clinically validated.

43090560.autores: Caetano NDS, Meireles BA, … Cassel M (4 autores)
43090560.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Evaluating the Insecticidal Potential of Solanum lycocarpum and Curatella americana Leaf Extracts: Histopathological Effects on Culex quinquefasciatus Larvae», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43090560.resumo_original: This study evaluated the larvicidal potential and histopathological impacts of ethanolic extracts from Solanum lycocarpum and Curatella americana against third-instar Culex quinquefasciatus larvae. Laboratory bioassays were conducted to assess mortality and behavioral effects. While no direct larval mortality occurred in this study, lethargy was observed three hours post exposure in treatments involving the highest concentrations (T7 and T8). After specimens were fixed in 70% ethanol, standard histological analysis revealed concentration-dependent changes across both plant extracts. Significant structural alterations were observed in the salivary glands, gastric caeca, Malpighian tubules, and the anterior, mid, and posterior intestines, with the most severe damage appearing to increase with higher extract concentrations. These disruptions affected tissues involved in feeding and development, potentially offering an indirect mechanism for vector control.

43076540.titulo: Modulation of MOF Catalytic Activity to Exploit Cystine Dependency for Immunometabolic Therapy
43076540.autores: Lv L, Xiang X, … Liu H (14 autores)
43076540.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Modulation of MOF Catalytic Activity to Exploit Cystine Dependency for Immunometabolic Therapy», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43076540.resumo_original: Tumor immunometabolism plays an important role in tumor progression and immune cell activity and is therefore critical to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy. Modulation of immunometabolism to boost cancer immunotherapy is mostly based on targeting tumor cell metabolism, which often fails to address the tumor-promoting functions maintained by stromal cells. In contrast, targeting a metabolic checkpoint shared by tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can potentially overcome this limitation but has been relatively underexplored. Herein, a locally delivered, ultrasound activatable nanocatalytic platform is reported for immunometabolic cancer therapy. The platform is composed of sulfasalazine and a gallium-modified Fe-TCPP metal-organic framework nanozyme codelivered in an oxidized sodium alginate-based hydrogel. Ultrasound-activated gallium-modified Fe-TCPP boosts electron transfer, peroxide activation, and reactive oxygen species production while disrupting iron balance. Simultaneously, sulfasalazine inhibits SLC7A11-mediated cystine uptake in CAFs and tumor cells, reducing matrix remodeling and weakening the tumor's antioxidant defense. This dual approach increases oxidative stress, reshapes the tumor microenvironment, induces immunogenic tumor cell death with ferroptotic traits, matures dendritic cells, and strengthens CD8+ T-cell responses. Consequently, it suppresses tumor growth in an immunocompetent osteosarcoma model and remains effective in a patient-derived OSCC xenograft model. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting shared SLC7A11-mediated cystine dependence integrates stromal remodeling, tumor redox disruption, and antitumor immune activation.

43090580.resumo_original: Municipal mosquito control programs depend on timely counts and species identification, yet these tasks take staff time, require scarce expertise, and are often handled in separate tools. We developed MOSAIC (Mosquito Observations and Surveillance using AI for Communities), a web platform bringing trap collections, photographs, counts, laboratory results, and expert review into a single record and turning them into weekly trap priorities. We evaluated it with the vector control program of Corpus Christi, Texas, USA. Counting uses classical computer vision (OpenCV) without a trained model; for identification, we compared multimodal large language models (LLMs) with a laboratory-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) and tested LLMs given a local species list, taxonomic knowledge, and labeled examples. OpenCV counts were within two mosquitoes of the operators' blind counts for 69% of 175 collections. On citizen-science photographs, the zero-shot LLM was correct on 89% of the genera it named but named a genus for 83% (overall accuracy 74%, versus 77% for the CNN). Across three runs, added knowledge and examples raised mean forced-choice species accuracy from 17 to 20% to 63-70%, but when abstention was allowed, the models named a species for only 23-49% of specimens. Automated tools can assist surveillance while experts confirm the outputs.

43093642.titulo: Characterization of the Gametocytocidal and Putative Transmission-Blocking Activity of Chlorotonil A Against Plasmodium falciparum
43093642.autores: Schäfer TM, de Carvalho LP, … Held J (16 autores)
43093642.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Characterization of the Gametocytocidal and Putative Transmission-Blocking Activity of Chlorotonil A Against Plasmodium falciparum», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43093642.resumo_original: Background: Chlorotonil A, a keto-macrolide produced by the myxobacterium Sorangium cellulosum, has potent antibiotic and antimalarial activities. Notably, chlorotonil A is active against both asexual and sexual blood-stage malaria parasites, making it a promising candidate for the development of an antimalarial treatment that also reduces parasite transmission to mosquitoes. Objectives: Here, we characterize the gametocytocidal and transmission-reducing activity of chlorotonil A. Methods and results: Using direct membrane feeding assays with Plasmodium falciparum isolates from a malaria-endemic area in Gabon, we show that chlorotonil A reduces oocyst infection prevalence and intensity in Anopheles gambiae (Kisumu) mosquitoes. Furthermore, we demonstrate that chlorotonil A is a particularly fast-acting gametocytocidal compound in vitro. Fluorescence and transmission electron microscopy revealed that chlorotonil A impairs membrane integrity and induces intracellular vacuolization after 6 h of drug exposure, with accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and intracellular acidification after 24 h. Conclusions: Our findings show that chlorotonil A has the potential for development as a dual-active antimalarial.

43094416.titulo: From low to high transmission: diversity-dependent responses of Plasmodium falciparum population structure to transmission intensity
43094416.autores: Suarez-Salazar D, Corredor-Espinel V, … Santos-Vega M (3 autores)
43094416.revista: Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci
43094416.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «From low to high transmission: diversity-dependent responses of Plasmodium falciparum population structure to transmission intensity», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43094416.resumo_original: Genetic surveillance is increasingly used to characterize malaria transmission, yet genetic patterns can respond nonlinearly to transmission intensity and depend on diversity already present in parasite populations. To isolate these effects from migration, selection, treatment and host immunity, we developed a neutral stochastic agent-based model of a closed human-mosquito transmission system integrating SEIS (susceptible-exposed-infectious-susceptible) epidemiological dynamics with neutral Plasmodium falciparum haplotypes and mosquito-stage recombination, without mutation or de novo allele generation. By independently varying human biting availability (amax) and initial genetic diversity (π0), we examined their joint effects on infection complexity, recombination and parasite population structure across a continuous transmission gradient. Infection prevalence and within-host infection complexity increased rapidly across low-to-intermediate transmission, whereas the effective recombination ratio and the number of recombinant haplotypes continued to increase across a broader range. Higher transmission was also associated with greater retention of human-stage parasite population genetic diversity (πH) and more even haplotype-frequency distributions, while initial genetic diversity constrained attainable genetic outcomes. Similar late-time population structures could be approached through different transient dynamics. Parasite population structure therefore reflects the interaction between transmission intensity and the genetic conditions on which transmission and recombination act, providing mechanistic expectations for interpreting malaria genetic surveillance patterns across heterogeneous transmission settings. This article is part of the theme issue 'Ecological and evolutionary interactions between parasites across scales'.

43093038.titulo: Investigating Lethality of Mayaro Virus, O'nyong-nyong Virus, Ross River Virus, and Una Virus in an Immunodeficient Murine Model
43093038.autores: Gardner CL, Pieterse L, … Burke CW (7 autores)
43093038.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Investigating Lethality of Mayaro Virus, O'nyong-nyong Virus, Ross River Virus, and Una Virus in an Immunodeficient Murine Model», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093038.resumo_original: Arthritogenic alphaviruses are mosquito-borne viruses characteristically associated with severe rheumatic disease and febrile illness. While this group of arboviruses house significant epidemic potential due to expanding competent vectors, host plasticity, and recombination events increasing infectivity, the median lethal dose (LD50) for many members remains limited or non-existent, thus restraining medical countermeasure (MCM) investigations. Mayaro virus (MAYV), o'nyong-nyong virus (ONNV), Una virus (UNAV), and Ross River virus (RRV) are four arthritogenic alphaviruses with epidemic potential. However, at the time of our study, no literature examining LD50 values for each virus in IFNAR-deficient mice, an effective model for characterizing disease severity and thus MCM potential, was available. In this study, we subcutaneously inoculated IFNAR-deficient mice with ranged doses of MAYV, ONNV, UNAV, or RRV to determine the LD50. However, we were unsuccessful upon finding complete lethality across all ranged doses for each virus. We further validated MCM potential in our MAYV model by prophylactically treating mice with neutralizing antibody (nAb) and examining clinical scores, weight loss, and survival rates. Our study serves as the first to examine the lethality of UNAV, MAYV, and RRV infection in an IFNAR-deficient mouse model and provides crucial lethal dose reference material for future MAYV, ONNV, UNAV, and RRV studies.

43093812.titulo: Antiviral Strategies Against Dengue Virus: Viral Targets, Host Pathways, and Chinese Herbal Medicines
43093812.autores: Liang Q, Liu K, … Shan C (4 autores)
43093812.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Antiviral Strategies Against Dengue Virus: Viral Targets, Host Pathways, and Chinese Herbal Medicines», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093812.resumo_original: Dengue is caused by four antigenically distinct dengue virus serotypes (DENV-1 to DENV-4) and remains a major global public health threat. It is endemic in more than 100 countries and territories, primarily in tropical and subtropical regions. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), approximately 390 million DENV infections occur annually, with nearly half of the world's population at risk of infection. Complex virus-host interactions and disease mechanisms continue to complicate antiviral development. No dengue-specific antiviral therapy has been approved. This review summarizes recent advances in anti-DENV therapeutics, including inhibitors targeting viral proteins, host factors, and virus-host interactions. In addition, it highlights the antiviral potential of Chinese herbal medicines and their bioactive compounds, and discusses priorities for their further development.

43092308.titulo: Long-Term Nitrogen and Phosphorus Control and Microbial Responses by Tea-Bag-Encapsulated MgO-Modified Biochar at the Sediment-Water Interface
43092308.autores: Ding Y, Chai B, … He L (12 autores)
43092308.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Long-Term Nitrogen and Phosphorus Control and Microbial Responses by Tea-Bag-Encapsulated MgO-Modified Biochar at the Sediment-Water Interface», no contexto de Polifosfato Inorgânico & Acidocalcisomas.
43092308.resumo_original: Internal phosphorus release from sediments is an important limiting factor in the remediation of eutrophic water bodies. Tea-bag-encapsulated MgO-modified biochar has advantages in phosphorus adsorption, microbial attachment, and convenient recovery, but its long-term phosphorus control effect and associated microbial responses at the sediment-water interface remain unclear. In this study, a 124-day sediment-water simulation experiment combined with metagenomic sequencing was conducted to evaluate its effects on nitrogen and phosphorus removal, water environmental changes, and microbial phosphorus-cycling functions. The results showed that the removal efficiencies of phosphate, total phosphorus, ammonia nitrogen, and total nitrogen in the treatment group reached 88%, 67%, 90%, and 40%, respectively. After application, the BET specific surface area of the material decreased from 47.85 to 20.18 m2/g, obvious surface deposits appeared, and phosphorus enrichment was detected, indicating that the material continuously participated in interfacial phosphorus fixation. Meanwhile, the relative abundances of Anaerolinea and Nitrospira increased from 5.71% to 10.08% and from 0.72% to 1.06%, respectively. Functional gene analysis showed that the relative abundances of genes related to phosphorus sensing, transport, and polyphosphate metabolism changed, suggesting that the functional potential related to phosphorus acquisition and storage was adjusted. Since this study was based on a small-scale long-term simulation system, the contribution of the material was mainly interpreted through the stage-specific differences between BC and BT, material characterization, and microbial functional responses, while the independent effects of time-varying factors such as temperature and redox conditions still require further controlled experiments. Overall, the sustained phosphorus control effect of tea-bag-encapsulated MgO-modified biochar was mainly associated with interfacial material fixation, microbial community changes, and adjustments in phosphorus cycling functional potential.

43090484.titulo: MAALEM-Btmosquito: A Novel Floating Granular Bti Formulation for Aedes aegypti Control in Domestic Water-Storage Containers
43090484.autores: Villegas A, Sanchez J, … Soberón M (11 autores)
43090484.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «MAALEM-Btmosquito: A Novel Floating Granular Bti Formulation for Aedes aegypti Control in Domestic Water-Storage Containers», no contexto de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas.
43090484.resumo_original: Integrated management of Aedes aegypti, the primary urban vector of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya, requires effective, environmentally safe larvicides with sufficient residual activity for operational use. We developed and evaluated MAALEM-Btmosquito, a novel floating granular formulation based on Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis (Bti), designed to maintain larvicidal activity under routine water use and partial water replacement in domestic water containers. Outdoor semi-field bioassays were conducted in 20 L buckets and 200 L drums under three water-replacement regimes (0%, 10%, and 50%). Groups of 25 late third- and early fourth-instar Ae. aegypti larvae were exposed at successive post-treatment intervals, and mortality was assessed at 24 and 48 h over 30 days. MAALEM-Btmosquito caused 100% mortality at 24 h on the first day and maintained >94.5% larval mortality throughout the study. Overall mean 24 h mortality across treatments was 98.8%, with treatment means ranging from 94.7% (95% CI, 91.9-96.5) to 99.7% (95% CI, 98.5-99.9). The greatest reduction in activity was observed in 20 L containers subjected to 50% water replacement. Operational performance was evaluated during three application cycles involving more than 700 households in Puente de Ixtla, Morelos, Mexico. The Breteau Index decreased by 72.6%, 64.6%, and 81.1%, while the mean egg count per ovitrap decreased from 93.2 ± 76.10 before the first MAALEM-Btmosquito application to 25.4 ± 20.44 eggs after completion of the field interventions. Because the community evaluation was conducted without a concurrent untreated control area, these field observations are associative and cannot be attributed solely to MAALEM-Btmosquito. Potential confounding factors include seasonality, rainfall, other vector-control activities, and household water-use behavior. Together with the controlled semi-field results, these findings support the potential of MAALEM-Btmosquito as a larvicide for integrated mosquito vector management.

43080261.titulo: Serum itaconate levels and treatment-related changes in polymyalgia rheumatica: a prospective observational study
43080261.autores: Li Z, Wu Y, … Wu M (7 autores)
43080261.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Serum itaconate levels and treatment-related changes in polymyalgia rheumatica: a prospective observational study», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43080261.resumo_original:
Itaconate (ITA) is an immunometabolic regulator, but its circulating levels and treatment-associated changes in polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) remain unclear. This study investigated serum ITA levels across treatment states and their longitudinal associations with inflammatory markers and glucocorticoid (GC) exposure.
This prospective observational study included 161 serum samples from 108 participants, comprising 20 healthy control (HC), 30 treatment-naïve (TN), and 111 treatment-exposed (TE) samples. Serum ITA was quantified by LC-MS/MS. Between-group differences were assessed using age- and sex-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Paired changes were evaluated in 11 patients, and longitudinal associations were examined across 42 TE-to-TE intervals from 27 patients using regression models with patient-clustered robust standard errors.
Adjusted geometric mean ITA concentrations were 4.170 ng/mL (95% CI, 3.132-5.553) in HC, 0.907 ng/mL (0.719-1.143) in TN, and 3.885 ng/mL (3.427-4.405) in TE. ITA levels were significantly lower in TN than in HC and TE (both P<0.001), whereas no significant difference was observed between TE and HC (P = 0.656). Among 11 paired patients, ITA increased in 10 at the first post-treatment follow-up, with median concentrations rising from 1.408 to 5.394 ng/mL (P = 0.0049). Across all 42 treated intervals, changes in ITA were not significantly associated with changes in ESR (P = 0.622). However, among 21 intervals involving abnormal ESR, an inverse association was observed after adjustment for concurrent GC dose changes (β=-0.601, 95% CI, -1.000 to -0.201; P = 0.006; Holm-adjusted P = 0.018).
Serum ITA was markedly reduced in TN PMR and increased following treatment initiation. Its exploratory inverse association with ESR changes in intervals involving abnormal ESR suggests treatment-associated immunometabolic variation that warrants further investigation.

43087672.titulo: Immune-Mediated Endothelial Injury in Cardiometabolic-Cardiovascular Disease
43087672.autores: Wang Q, Liu L, … Li Y (4 autores)
43087672.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Immune-Mediated Endothelial Injury in Cardiometabolic-Cardiovascular Disease», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43087672.resumo_original: Cardiometabolic disease, encompassing hypertension, type 2 diabetes, obesity, and dyslipidemia, is the predominant driver of cardiovascular disease (CVD) morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the vascular endothelium sits at the transition from metabolic derangement to overt cardiovascular events, serving as both sensor and transducer of metabolic injury. This review synthesizes evidence that aberrant immune responses act as contributory drivers of endothelial injury in cardiometabolic disease. These responses span innate pattern-recognition receptor activation, neutrophil-mediated cytotoxicity, monocyte/macrophage polarization imbalance, adaptive T- and B-cell dysregulation, and trained immunity. The inflammation they represent is therapeutically actionable at the level of cardiovascular events. Whether endothelial protection mediates that benefit has not been directly tested, and reverse causation and parallel metabolic-inflammatory loops are not excluded. We trace how the canonical innate sensing cascades (Toll-like receptor 4-nuclear factor κB, the NLRP3 inflammasome, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes) converge on endothelial activation. We then examine how oxidative stress at the immune-metabolic interface, including NADPH oxidase-derived reactive oxygen species, endothelial nitric oxide synthase uncoupling, mitochondrial damage-associated molecular pattern release, and oxidized phospholipid accumulation, amplifies this convergence. Finally, we describe how junctional disassembly, glycocalyx degradation, and endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition execute barrier disruption. We then assess mechanism-linked circulating biomarkers and multi-marker integration strategies, anchoring the framework in clinical trials that have established anti-inflammatory therapy in selected patient populations while the mechanistic steps linking these interventions to endothelial protection remain incompletely tested. We close by consolidating this evidence into a graded inventory that separates candidate circulating readouts from intervention and real-world evidence, and by marking where the mechanistic chain from pathway to readout to therapy remains unclosed. Whether these pathways can be translated into mechanism-informed risk stratification awaits prospective evidence and standardized measurement.

43077987.titulo: Dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia: a scoping review of program design, uptake, and safety surveillance
43077987.autores: Enriquez MGL, Villanueva-Uy LM, … Acuin MES (3 autores)
43077987.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia: a scoping review of program design, uptake, and safety surveillance», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43077987.resumo_original:
Dengue vaccine programs in Southeast Asia differ in target groups, delivery, financing, eligibility, and safety monitoring, and the evidence is scattered across peer-reviewed and grey literature.
To map evidence on dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia, focusing on program design, uptake, and safety surveillance, and to identify practical insights for future vaccination policies, implementation frameworks, and clinical guidelines in the region.
Scoping review.
Southeast Asia. Population Populations eligible for or receiving dengue vaccination.
The review followed JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. We searched PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane, Google Scholar, WPRIM, WHO IRIS, Google, and government and regulatory websites, and checked reference lists, for sources published from 2015 to 2026 on program design, uptake, or safety surveillance. Two reviewers screened records independently. Evidence was mapped by country and concept and synthesized narratively.
Database searches were last updated on September 8, 2026, and grey-literature and supplementary searches on November 1, 2026. Of 366 database records and 220 grey-literature links, 33 sources were included; a supplementary search added 12 (total 45). Evidence was found for six countries and none for Brunei, Cambodia, Lao PDR, Myanmar, or Timor-Leste. The Philippines ran a large, publicly funded, school-based CYD-TDV program; Indonesia combined private access with a provincial TAK-003 pilot; Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam relied mainly on private delivery. Safety surveillance was best documented in the Philippines, Malaysia, and Singapore. Uptake data were sparse: fewer than half of the >830,000 Filipino children given CYD-TDV completed three doses before the program was suspended, and the Indonesian pilot reported about 90% coverage. No uptake data were found for private-sector delivery. Nine sources were modeling or economic studies, which inform planning but do not document implementation.
Dengue vaccine implementation in Southeast Asia varies in delivery, financing, and safety monitoring, and is unevenly documented, especially for uptake. Standardized monitoring and reporting of real-world vaccination programs are needed.

43094982.titulo: Pathogen surveillance by agnostic high-throughput sequencing in sand flies collected in the country of Georgia
43094982.autores: Paskey AC, Thomas QK, … Bishop-Lilly KA (19 autores)
43094982.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Pathogen surveillance by agnostic high-throughput sequencing in sand flies collected in the country of Georgia», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43094982.resumo_original:
Sand flies are known vectors of human pathogens that cause acute febrile illness (AFI). Understanding the pathogen landscape within these insects is crucial for biosurveillance and prevention of infectious diseases in U.S forces deployed to regions where sand flies are present.
We used agnostic high-throughput sequencing to perform genomic surveillance for the presence of known human pathogens associated with AFI and novel relatives thereof in sand flies (Psychodidae: Phlebotominae) collected in the country of Georgia between August 2017 and August 2023. A total of 102 sand fly pools, containing 1-37 specimens each and in some cases sorted by sex, were homogenized. Of those, 86 produced Illumina RNA libraries suitable for sequencing. The resulting data were queried in an entirely pathogen agnostic manner: sequencing reads were processed through two bioinformatic pipelines, VirusSeeker 2.0 and MetaDetector, to perform quality control steps, de novo assembly, and a DIAMOND analysis on reads and assembled contigs. Manual analysis was performed to identify expected pathogens and any other pathogens of notable abundance. Results with similarity to pathogens of human or veterinary importance, as well as low confidence results represented by a low number of reads were also subjected to in-depth analysis.
This pathogen-agnostic assessment revealed both expected and unexpected results. We detected novel viruses consistent with insect vector viromes, including novel orthomyxoviruses that could merit further exploration and some vesiculovirus sequences that may represent endogenous viral elements. Although Leishmania was an expected finding, it was not detected with high confidence. A significant unexpected result was the detection of Rickettsia felis, a pathogen typically vectored by fleas and occasionally mosquitoes, in two separate pools, with 51% of the genome covered in one pool. Furthermore, we identified two distinct and complete novel phlebovirus genomes. Their genome divergence from previously known phleboviruses is so significant that they are not predicted to be amplified using any of the five published phlebovirus assays.
These results are achieved through a combination of agnostic sequencing and detailed bioinformatic analyses, enabling the detection of novel viruses and an expansion of our understanding of vector-borne disease ecology.

43077172.titulo: Redox-regulated immunomodulatory mechanisms of mycophenolate mofetil in a lupus-like disease
43077172.autores: Zhong J, Zhu W, … Liu B (6 autores)
43077172.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Redox-regulated immunomodulatory mechanisms of mycophenolate mofetil in a lupus-like disease», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43077172.resumo_original: Lupus-like autoimmune disease remains a severe, hard-to-manage complication after allogeneic immune cell transfer, with limited targeted therapies. While mycophenolate mofetil shows observable clinical benefit, its immunometabolic mechanisms in tissue-resident macrophages remain poorly defined. In this established murine lupus-like disease model, recipient mice received splenocytes from lupus-prone donors, with parallel comparisons between reactive oxygen species (ROS)-deficient, ROS-normal and conditional APOBEC3 knockout groups. We applied standardized in vivo mycophenolate mofetil dosing and ex vivo mycophenolic acid treatment, alongside high-resolution magnetic particle profiling, flow cytometry, ELISA, histology and RNA sequencing for systematic assessment. Mycophenolate mofetil significantly induced macrophage functional reprogramming, suppressed antigen-specific immune activation, lowered interferon-γ and IgG2b autoantibody levels, and alleviated pulmonary fibrosis, while APOBEC3-mediated cytosine deamination in macrophages was regulated by ROS signaling. These findings indicate that mycophenolate mofetil ameliorates lupus-like autoimmunity via ROS-dependent and independent DNA regulatory pathways, providing a new mechanistic basis for improving inflammation-directed immunomodulatory strategies.

43084220.titulo: Multistate Dengue Fever Outbreak in Sudan Amid Ongoing Conflict: A Descriptive Epidemiological Analysis
43084220.autores: Azhary A, Hajhamed NM, … Siddig EE (7 autores)
43084220.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Multistate Dengue Fever Outbreak in Sudan Amid Ongoing Conflict: A Descriptive Epidemiological Analysis», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43084220.resumo_original:
This study is a descriptive epidemiological analysis of a multistate dengue fever outbreak in Sudan during a period of intense armed conflict and mass displacement.
This study is an analysis of national surveillance data conducted using reports collected between August 2024 and July 2025. Variables, including case counts, fatalities, and internally displaced persons (IDPs) per state, were calculated and analyzed with R software 4.2.2 (Version 2025.05.1 + 513).
A total of 13,371 cases and 21 fatalities were reported across 10 states. Notably, Khartoum State, a conflict-affected region, recorded the highest number of cases (n = 8040), while Kassala reported the highest number of deaths (n = 9). Kassala State documented the highest number of dengue cases among IDPs (472), followed by Khartoum (69).
The findings highlight the need for strengthened dengue surveillance and vector control in conflict-affected settings, where disruption of health services may complicate outbreak prevention and response.
Not applicable.

43093691.titulo: Formulation of Glycerol-Based Emulsion Containing Myrica gale L. Essential Oil for Enhanced Repellent Activity
43093691.autores: Whyms SE, Kroll G, … Walsh JJ (7 autores)
43093691.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Formulation of Glycerol-Based Emulsion Containing Myrica gale L. Essential Oil for Enhanced Repellent Activity», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093691.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: Glycerol-based emulsions containing Myrica gale L. essential oils (EOs) were developed and evaluated for stability, volatilisation behaviour and in vivo mosquito repellent activity. Preliminary GC-MS characterisation of the oils demonstrated complex chemical profiles comprised mainly of a mixture of mono- and sesquiterpenes. Methods: Emulsions containing 10% oil were prepared at two surfactant concentrations (2.5 and 5%) and differing ratios of glycerol to water as the non-polar phase. The optimal system was determined to be 10% oil and 2.5% surfactant (i.e., cetearyl alcohol and cetearyl glucoside) in 100% glycerol as assessed over a 91-day storage period by changes in particle size, polydispersity and zeta potential. This formulation approach was subsequently applied to three proven insect repellent M. gale EOs. Volatilisation behaviour was investigated using headspace GC-MS analysis of selected marker compounds (α-pinene, camphene, β-pinene, myrcene, α-phellandrene, 3-carene, p-cymene, γ-terpinene). Results: M. gale-based emulsions demonstrated significantly improved volatilisation over time, compared with the EO coarsely dispersed in a lotion base. This enhanced partitioning behaviour correlated well with increased protection times observed in an arm-in-cage repellent assay against Aedes aegypti mosquitos. It was found that all formulated M.gale EOs, F_EO15M (CPT = 40.05 min, p = 0.032), F_EO21C (CPT = 42.023 min, p = 0.01) and F_EO15C (CPT = 99.478 min, p < 0.0001), performed significantly better than their non-formulated counterparts EO15M (CPT = 11.45 min), EO21C (CPT = 13.053 min) and EO15C (CPT = 33.02 min). Conclusion: This study describes for the first time an effective, topical M. gale-loaded emulsion for the improvement of insect repellent activity.

43096693.titulo: Unveiling skin mycobiome-immune dynamics: The role of fungi in trained immunity and immune reprogramming during skin diseases
43096693.autores: Riera-Leal L, Riera-Leal A, … Ortiz-García YM (7 autores)
43096693.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Unveiling skin mycobiome-immune dynamics: The role of fungi in trained immunity and immune reprogramming during skin diseases», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43096693.resumo_original: Human skin and mucosal surfaces harbor complex fungal communities, collectively termed the mycobiome, that can influence local and systemic immune homeostasis despite their relatively low abundance. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the composition and dynamics of cutaneous and mucosa-associated mycobiota at oral, nasal, and vaginal sites across the lifespan, highlighting Malassezia and Candida as dominant genera in specific niches. Age, anatomical site, hormonal status, barrier integrity, and environmental exposures shape these communities and their interactions with co-resident bacteria, archaea, and viruses. Particular emphasis is placed on fungal recognition and the mechanisms underlying trained innate immunity, while distinguishing experimental evidence from the incompletely defined effects of physiological colonization. Fungal components are recognized by receptors including Dectin-1, Dectin-2, Mincle, Langerin, Toll-like receptors, and NK cell receptors, activating pathways that coordinate antifungal defense. Experimental exposure to fungi or β-glucans can induce metabolic and epigenetic reprogramming in innate immune cells, involving PI3K-Akt-mTOR signaling, increased aerobic glycolysis, and altered chromatin states that support enhanced responses to subsequent challenges. Related antifungal pathways regulate cytokine production, Th17 responses, and inflammasome activation, with outcomes ranging from protective immunity to chronic inflammation and tissue damage, depending on the host and tissue context. Finally, we discuss fungal virulence strategies, interkingdom interactions, and their reported associations with inflammatory, infectious, and neoplastic diseases.

43093874.titulo: A Preliminary Virome Survey of Arctic and Sub-Arctic Tundra Mosquitoes (Aedes, Subgenus Ochlerotatus): Viral Diversity and Phylogenetic Affinities in Three Pooled Regional Samples
43093874.autores: Lee SY, Lee YM, … Chae N (6 autores)
43093874.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «A Preliminary Virome Survey of Arctic and Sub-Arctic Tundra Mosquitoes (Aedes, Subgenus Ochlerotatus): Viral Diversity and Phylogenetic Affinities in Three Pooled Regional Samples», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43093874.resumo_original: Rapid Arctic warming may increase mosquito abundance and alter host interactions, yet tundra mosquito-associated viral communities remain poorly characterized. We report viral sequences from pooled mosquitoes of three Arctic and sub-Arctic regions: Alaska (Aedes punctor group, n = 4), Canada (Ae. nigripes, n = 4), and Greenland (Ae. nigripes, n = 10). For each site, pooled specimens were sequenced from total nucleic acids and viral families were assigned only from amino-acid-level hits. Fourteen families were detected (7, 7, and 4 per pool), dominated by Iflaviridae, Narnaviridae, and Orthototiviridae (approximately 99%, 71%, and 93% of virus-assigned reads, respectively). Baculoviridae and Orthototiviridae were shared across all pools, though baculovirus may reflect environmental or dietary exposure rather than active infection. Maximum-likelihood phylogenies placed the recovered sequences within mosquito-associated lineages related to Fennoscandian relatives: a near-complete Alaskan iflavirus sequence (9850 bp) clustered with Finnish Pedersore iflaviruses, while Canadian and Greenlandic totiviruses and a narna-like virus were related to but divergent from Fennoscandian references. A Canadian chu-like virus-like sequence was the most divergent (27.9% amino-acid identity). These results link tundra mosquito-associated viral sequences to Fennoscandian lineages, some closely related but others substantially divergent. Despite single pooled libraries per region, this study offers an initial baseline for Arctic tundra mosquito viromes and underscores the need for future individually sequenced surveys under standardized protocols.

43090477.titulo: Forest Pest Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv11 with Intraspecific Classification Strategy
43090477.autores: Liang X, Xiang J, … Zou D (9 autores)
43090477.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Forest Pest Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv11 with Intraspecific Classification Strategy», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43090477.resumo_original: Forest pest detection has challenges such as the high similarity in appearance among different species, which leads to feature confusion. To address this issue, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv11 forest pest detection model with a fine-grained intraspecific classification strategy. The bottleneck of identification caused by the diversity of internal morphologies is effectively alleviated via constructing a dataset with adults, larvae, and nymphs, i.e., using intraspecific classification strategy. This model incorporates a CBA (Convolution-BatchNorm-AReLU) module, Scale-based Dynamic (SD) loss, and an Adaptively Spatial Feature Fusion (ASFF) module. The CBA module integrates an attention mechanism to dynamically adjust the gradient, which alleviates vanishing gradients and accelerates the convergence of model parameters. SD loss adaptively balances localization and scale loss based on a target scale, which reduces IoU fluctuations and enhances cross-scale robustness. Resolution conflicts and optimizing semantic alignment are alleviated by introducing the ASFF module to achieve learnable spatial multi-scale feature fusion. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv11 model outperforms existing methods, with Precision, Recall, AP50-90, and F1 score reaching 97.19%, 97.20%, 88.25%, and 97.17%, respectively. In practical applications, the proposed model can accurately capture subtle differences in the microscopic features of the same pest during different life cycles. This research project can accurately identify the types and occurrence stages of pests, match targeted control measures, avoid the use of excessive pesticides, and significantly reduce the cost of control and environmental pollution.

43086963.titulo: Anatomical transformation through the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition in megalopteran insects
43086963.autores: Zhao C, Huang M, … Liu X (9 autores)
43086963.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Anatomical transformation through the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition in megalopteran insects», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43086963.resumo_original:
The adaptation of aquatic insects to freshwater habitats is a key question for understanding insect evolution. Many aquatic insects undergo significant morphological and physiological changes during the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition. However, changes of internal anatomical structures and organs with the process of transformation have yet to be comprehensively investigated.
Here we document the anatomical transformations of the skeletal-muscular system, nervous system, digestive system, and tracheal system during the aquatic-terrestrial life-style transition in an aquatic insect species Protohermes xanthodes Navás, 1914 (Megaloptera: Corydalidae), using micro-CT and 3D reconstruction. Notably, unlike the rapid, concentrated breakdown of other organ systems, the tracheal system undergoes a prolonged, stepwise, and tightly orchestrated disintegration-reconstruction process during the major developmental stages. The digestive system is markedly modified but without complete disintegration across these stages. For predation and sensation under water, the larvae possess powerful mandibles and prothoracic muscles, and short but well-developed antennal nerves. In addition, the well-developed mesothoracic, metathoracic, and abdominal muscles at the filament base of the larvae enable underwater swimming.
This study provides new insights into the dynamic adaptations during the aquatic-terrestrial transition in Corydalidae (Megaloptera) and sheds light on coordinated evolution across multiple functional systems in response to environmental pressures.

43079461.titulo: Efficacy and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated plasmodium falciparum malaria in South Sudan: a multi-site therapeutic efficacy study, 2024-2025
43079461.autores: Ayuen DS, Dau AD, … Malual MD (9 autores)
43079461.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Efficacy and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated plasmodium falciparum malaria in South Sudan: a multi-site therapeutic efficacy study, 2024-2025», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43079461.resumo_original:
South Sudan has one of the highest malaria burdens per capita in Africa, and artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ) and artemether-lumefantrine (AL) are first- and second-line treatments for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria. However, despite the emergence of Artemisinin partial resistance (ART-R) and AL failure at some sites in the region, no therapeutic efficacy study (TES) has been conducted since the introduction of ASAQ and AL two decades ago. Our TES aimed to assess the efficacy of ASAQ and AL across four sites in South Sudan.
This study was conducted in Juba, Bor, Wau, and Yambio. Children aged 6 months to 59 months with microscopically confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum monoinfection were assigned to ASAQ or AL and followed for 28 days to assess treatment response. The primary endpoint was the Kaplan-Meier PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on Day 28. Day 3 parasite positivity was used as a measure of early treatment response.
We enrolled 390 children across all arms; 10.3% overall were lost to follow-up, ranging from 0% in Bor to 24.1% in Juba-ASAQ, and 350 (89.7%) were included in the per-protocol analysis. Kaplan-Meier uncorrected ACPR was: 96.2% (95% CI: 89.2-99.2) in Juba-AL, 95.6% (95% CI: 87.6-99.1) in Juba-ASAQ, 97.7% (95% CI: 92.6-99.7) in Bor (ASAQ) and 93.3% (95% CI: 86.1-97.5) in Yambio (AL). Kaplan-Meier PCR-corrected ACPR exceeded 90% in all sites except Wau: 98.7% (95% CI: 92.9-100.0) in Juba-AL, 100.0% (95% CI: 94.5-100.0) in Juba-ASAQ, 100.0% (95% CI: 95.8-100.0) in Bor (ASAQ) and 98.8% (95% CI: 93.5-100.0) in Yambio (AL). In Wau, only 34 participants were evaluable at Day 28, and no treatment failures were observed. Day 3 parasite positivity was elevated at Bor (13.8%), exceeding the WHO 10% threshold used as an indicator of suspected ART-R. No adverse events were reported.
ASAQ and AL remain highly efficacious against uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in South Sudan, supporting the continuation of the current treatment policy. The high Day 3 positivity rate at Bor warrants enhanced molecular surveillance and repeat efficacy monitoring. This study establishes a baseline for national TES surveillance.

43084107.titulo: The Genome Exposome Microbiome-Phenome (GEM-P): a conceptual framework for social bees
43084107.autores: Cutajar S, Alberoni D, … Mifsud D (4 autores)
43084107.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «The Genome Exposome Microbiome-Phenome (GEM-P): a conceptual framework for social bees», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43084107.resumo_original: The gut microbiome of social bees is a small, specific set of symbionts that contributes to nutrition, detoxification, immune function and behaviour, with effects on colony performance and resilience. In recent years, the field has expanded, but studies still analyse host genetics and environmental exposures separately and often rely on correlations between microbes and health traits. This makes it difficult to distinguish between instances in which microbiome differences primarily reflect host or environmental factors and instances in which they may contribute mechanistically to bee health. A key challenge is context dependence: similar microbiome shifts may be associated with different trait outcomes depending on life stage and task, exposure history, and colony transmission structure. We present the Genome Exposome Microbiome-Phenome (GEM-P) framework as an integrative organisational framework for social bees. GEM-P treats genome, lifetime exposures (exposome), and the gut microbiome as interacting components shaping phenotypes at both individual and colony scales. Phenotypes can, in turn, modify subsequent exposures and microbiome states. We use GEM-P to map evidence on genetic filtering, exposomal drivers, microbiome assembly and function, and phenotypic outcomes, and to highlight study designs that help distinguish among alternative biological pathways without requiring comprehensive multi-omics approaches. GEM-P provides a practical way to generate pathway-specific hypotheses and interpret microbiome-phenotype associations across contexts. KEY POINTS: • An integrative framework linking genome, exposome, gut microbiome, and phenome in social bees. • Highlights scale, timing, and social transmission as sources of context dependence. • Supports pathway-specific hypotheses and sampling designs that help distinguish alternative explanations for microbiome-phenotype associations.
