43090550.titulo: MiR-277 Drives Sexually Dimorphic Development in Ericerus pela Through Differential Regulation of Dlg1 and Lar
43090550.autores: Chen X, Ling X, … Chen H (7 autores)
43090550.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «MiR-277 Drives Sexually Dimorphic Development in Ericerus pela Through Differential Regulation of Dlg1 and Lar», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43090550.resumo_original: Insects exhibit diverse developmental strategies, yet the molecular basis of sexual dimorphism in metamorphosis remains largely elusive. The white wax scale insect Ericerus pela (hereafter, WWS) displays extreme sexual dimorphism: females undergo paurometamorphosis (four stages), while males undergo hyperpaurometamorphosis (five stages). Although miR-277 is highly expressed in both sexes, its functional role in this process was unknown. Here, we demonstrate that miR-277 drives sexually dimorphic development through differential regulation of two distinct targets. Combining gain- and loss-of-function assays, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and RNA interference, we show that miR-277 suppresses Discs large 1 (Dlg1) in females, disrupting cellular signaling and causing growth retardation and morphological abnormalities. In males, miR-277 inhibits tyrosine-protein phosphatase Lar (Lar), a receptor tyrosine phosphatase linked to nervous system development; knockdown of Lar severely impairs male metamorphosis but does not affect females. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized, sex-specific miRNA regulatory switch: miR-277 concurrently modulates a cell-growth pathway in females and a neurodevelopmental pathway in males, thereby generating divergent developmental outcomes. Our study provides the mechanistic insight into miRNA-mediated sexual dimorphism in insects and advances the understanding of how post-transcriptional regulators shape metamorphic diversity.

43090487.titulo: Broad-Scale Landscape Structure Shapes Anopheline Assemblages in an Amazonian Deforestation Frontier
43090487.autores: Santos TC, Ilacqua RC, … Laporta GZ (10 autores)
43090487.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Broad-Scale Landscape Structure Shapes Anopheline Assemblages in an Amazonian Deforestation Frontier», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43090487.resumo_original: Previous work in this Amazonian deforestation frontier identified a broad-scale landscape signal for malaria-vector abundance and infected-anopheline occurrence, generating the hypothesis that the anopheline assemblage itself may be organized by landscape structure. Here, we tested whether anopheline richness, total abundance, Nyssorhynchus darlingi abundance and multispecies assemblage structure are associated with landscape composition, configuration and spatial extent. We analyzed 365 anophelines from 22 landscapes and eight species using Bayesian count and hierarchical multispecies models. Predictors represented forest cover, secondary forest, water, exposed soil, forest configuration and river proximity across 3, 5 and 7 km2. The 7 km2 scale received the strongest support across responses. Forest cover consistently increased richness and community abundance, exposed soil reduced abundance-based responses, and forest edge density contributed to the best multispecies model. These findings indicate that broad-scale landscape structure organizes anopheline assemblages that may underlie malaria transmission in Amazonian frontier regions.

43084617.titulo: Aedes aegypti breeding patterns and arboviral risks influenced by complex social-climate dynamics in the semi-arid areas of Bouaké, central Côte d'Ivoire (West Africa)
43084617.autores: Dibo JDK, Touré M, … Zahouli JZB (12 autores)
43084617.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Aedes aegypti breeding patterns and arboviral risks influenced by complex social-climate dynamics in the semi-arid areas of Bouaké, central Côte d'Ivoire (West Africa)», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43084617.resumo_original:
Dengue (DEN) is rapidly expanding across yellow fever (YF)-endemic settings in Côte d'Ivoire (West Africa). However, data on how climate and social conditions influence local Aedes vector populations and disease transmission are still lacking, particularly in climatic transition zones. Thus, we assessed the driving effects of seasonality and social behaviours on Aedes aegypti occurrence and DEN and YF epidemic risks across variously urbanised landscapes in the semi-arid climate areas of Bouaké, central Côte d'Ivoire.
From September 2023 to August 2024, we sampled Aedes larvae and pupae in aquatic habitats among 3,600 households in urban, peri-urban and rural areas during rainy and dry seasons. We conducted a community-based survey to assess knowledge and practices related to potable water and solid waste management, mosquito breeding prevention and vector-borne disease risk in the households. Larval and pupal indices were compared between the study areas over behavioural and seasonal variations.
Ae. aegypti widely predominated across all study areas, with proportions > 99% (n = 64488). Larval breeding in aquatic habitats and related arboviral risks were driven by the local community behaviours and seasonality in all areas, and showed higher magnitude in the urban. DEN and YF epidemic risk indices exceeded the standard World Health Organisation (WHO) thresholds in all areas, with density figures of 6-9 in the urban and 4-8 in the peri-urban and rural areas. Out of 23,074 wet containers inspected, tires were the most productive pupal breeding grounds in the urban areas, while medium containers were the largest providers of pupae in the peri-urban and rural areas. Larval occurrences among household containers were associated with water storage practices and seasonal variations. Outdoor and discarded containers were more infested with Aedes larvae during rainy seasons. Domestic water-holding containers abundantly harboured larvae during dry seasons associated with longer water storage duration and frequent supply interruptions and drought. Unexpectedly, local community education and awareness of mosquito risks and DEN and YF causes were not translated into behavioural change for protective effect. Rainfall-behaviour cycles supported the strong presence of Ae. aegypti and high epidemic risks of DEN and YF year-round in all areas, with more pronounced effects in the urban areas.
In the semi-arid areas of Bouaké, the patterns of Ae. aegypti larval breeding among household water-holding containers are locally influenced by the complex and dynamic interactions between community behaviours and climate. Compensatory effects of rainfall-water storing dynamics sustain Ae. aegypti density figures and DEN and YF epidemic risks above the WHO-established thresholds over a year, mainly in the urban areas. Thus, community-driven awareness and vector control actions are required to attenuate climate impacts on arboviral epidemic risks in the semi-arid areas of Côte d'Ivoire and other West African countries.

43093831.titulo: Pathogenic Mechanisms of Japanese Encephalitis Virus Infection in Mammals
43093831.autores: Zhang S, Luo H, … Liang G (3 autores)
43093831.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Pathogenic Mechanisms of Japanese Encephalitis Virus Infection in Mammals», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43093831.resumo_original: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a mosquito-borne flavivirus and the leading cause of viral encephalitis in many regions of Asia. Owing to its pronounced neurotropism, JEV infection can result in severe neurological disease with high mortality, while 30-50% of survivors develop permanent neurological sequelae. Although substantial progress has been made over the past few decades, the molecular mechanisms underlying JEV infection, neuroinvasion, and host-mediated pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. In this review, we summarize recent advances in the understanding of JEV pathogenesis from both viral and host perspectives. We discuss the key events during JEV infection in mammalian hosts, including viral attachment and entry, replication and dissemination, viral determinants of virulence, blood-brain barrier penetration, and the mechanisms underlying central and peripheral nervous system injury. We further compare currently available experimental models for JEV research, including mouse models, porcine models, and human brain organoid systems, highlighting their respective applications, advantages, and limitations in investigating JEV pathogenesis. Collectively, this review provides an integrated overview of the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing JEV infection and neuropathogenesis, identifies current knowledge gaps, and discusses future research priorities that may facilitate the development of effective antiviral and neuroprotective strategies against Japanese encephalitis.

43090528.titulo: The Potassium Channel Gene BmTWK7 Contributes to Cocoon-Spinning Behavior in Bombyx mori
43090528.autores: Sun X, Tan Y, … Sima Y (9 autores)
43090528.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «The Potassium Channel Gene BmTWK7 Contributes to Cocoon-Spinning Behavior in Bombyx mori», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43090528.resumo_original: Potassium channels regulate membrane potential, cellular excitability, and neurotransmission, yet potential behavioral and physiological roles in the silkworm (Bombyx mori) remain unclear. Here, the roles of BmTWK7 (TWiK family of potassium channels protein 7), a gene encoding a two-pore-domain potassium (K2P) channel, were investigated using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout. BmTWK7 deficiency reduced the larval heart rate and altered dorsal vessel contraction patterns, supporting a regulatory role in cardiac function. BmTWK7-deficient larvae exhibited altered cocoon-spinning behavior, including a tendency toward an expanded wandering range, altered temporal patterns of spinning rate in males, higher cocooning positions, larger spinning areas, increased cocoon floss, and a higher frequency of incomplete cocoons. BmTWK7 deficiency was further associated with reduced head GABA levels, widespread downregulation of brain GABA-related genes, and increased brain Ca2+ fluorescence. Together, these findings support the role of BmTWK7 in regulating cocoon-spinning behavior and cardiac activity, while its deficiency was associated with altered GABAergic homeostasis and increased brain Ca2+ signals, highlighting broader roles of K2P channels in insect behavior and physiology.

43086712.titulo: Eight-year malaria trend in Estie District, Ethiopia: implications for malaria elimination
43086712.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Eight-year malaria trend in Estie District, Ethiopia: implications for malaria elimination», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43086712.resumo_original:
In Ethiopia, malaria is one of the leading health and socioeconomic problems even though significant numbers of malaria cases were reduced in the last two decades. The health facilities' retrospective studies offer valuable insights into how to carry out evidence-based interventions in particular areas and assess the effectiveness of ongoing malaria control initiatives. However, the trend of malaria prevalence has not been studied so far in the Estie locality; therefore, this study was designed to evaluate the eight-year trend of malaria in the Estie district, Ethiopia.
A retrospective study was conducted to determine the occurrence of malaria over the past eight years (2015-2022) from the peripheral blood smear examinations reported in the laboratory logbooks of the Mekane Eyesus hospital and health center, Ethiopia. To show the trends of infection rate patterns in months, years, sexes, age groups, residential settings, and seasons, descriptive statistics were used. Tables and figures were used to display results.
Of 49,215 clinically malaria-suspected individuals, only 15.6% (7674) microscopically confirmed malaria cases were reported in the district. The rate of infection was much higher in males (81.9%) and rural communities (71.3%) than females (18.1%) and urban communities (28.7%), respectively (p < 0.01). The most frequently identified Plasmodium species was Plasmodium falciparum (p < 0.01). The highest peak of malaria cases was recorded in age groups between 15 and 44 years in the autumn season (September, October, and November), which is considered the peak malaria transmission period in Ethiopia after the heavy rain in July and August.
Despite large fluctuations in malaria incidence over the last eight years, malaria has remained a public health problem in the research area. Malaria is particularly likely to reappear between 2021 and 2022, which is extremely concerning. Furthermore, in the study location, P. falciparum is the predominant species, followed by P. vivax in a rural population. As a result, the use of ongoing intervention strategies should be reviewed. Uninterrupted efforts and increased malaria control and prevention activities are critical to considerably lowering the malaria burden in the research area. Unless these issues are addressed, the country's goal of eradicating malaria would be significantly hampered.

43095939.titulo: Salicylamides as RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase Inhibitors with Antiviral Activity against West Nile and Zika Viruses
43095939.autores: Río ND, Rodríguez-Tacón Á, … Pérez-Pérez MJ (14 autores)
43095939.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Salicylamides as RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase Inhibitors with Antiviral Activity against West Nile and Zika Viruses», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43095939.resumo_original: Mosquito-transmitted orthoflaviviruses constitute an escalating global threat to public health, for which no approved antiviral therapies exist. Here, we identify the salicylanilide derivative S1 as a West Nile virus (WNV) RNA-dependent RNA-polymerase (RdRp) inhibitor. Chemical optimization of S1 yielded compound S7, which inhibited WNV RdRp activity and displayed antiviral efficacy in Vero cells (EC50 of 3.0 μM; CC50 > 100 μM). S7 and related analogues inhibited Zika virus (ZIKV) RdRp, and this enzymatic inhibition translated into antiviral activity in cell-based assays. Compared with niclosamide, as reference salicylanilide, compound S7 exerted lower impact on mitochondria, reduced cytotoxicity and no induction of apoptosis. Molecular modelling support binding within the polymerase N-pocket, with key contributing residues being highly conserved in both WNV and ZIKV polymerases. Site-directed mutagenesis further supported the importance of N-pocket residues for S7 binding. Therefore, the S7-scaffold constitutes a promising antiviral chemotype against orthoflaviviruses.

43091812.titulo: The Molecular Potassium Code: Extracellular K^+^ Sensing, Allosteric Ion Selectivity, KCC2 Thermodynamics, and the Dynamic Control of Neural Inhibition
43091812.autores: Dumitrescu D, Dumitru AV, … Rădoi MP (9 autores)
43091812.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «The Molecular Potassium Code: Extracellular K^+^ Sensing, Allosteric Ion Selectivity, KCC2 Thermodynamics, and the Dynamic Control of Neural Inhibition», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43091812.resumo_original: Neuronal excitability can be controlled by the level of potassium (K+) outside a neuron through both its effects on the cell membrane's electrical properties and its influence on ion transport across the membrane. Recent studies have also shown that certain ligand-gated ion-channel receptors can be modulated by the levels of K+ outside the neuron. Therefore, understanding how each mechanism contributes to the generation of inhibitory signals requires the ability to differentiate between them. This study represents a review that integrates evidence using various methods, including electrophysiology, structural studies, thermodynamics, and optical measurements, to propose a framework called the molecular potassium code that explains how neurons respond to varying levels of K+ in their environment. The framework describes three ways that neurons interact with changing levels of K+: how these changes shift their K+ equilibrium potential and membrane voltage; how they alter the thermodynamic driving force for KCC2-mediated cotransport of K+ and Cl-; and how receptor-dependent modulation occurs at specific receptors when documented. Changes in activation, desensitization, pharmacological sensitivity, and permeation characteristics have been measured in Drosophila DmAlka channels; however, the atomic details of K+ recognition by these channels remain unclear. Human GlyRα2 variants engineered or edited to allow for assessment of K+-associated responses under elevated K+ conditions did not provide sufficient evidence for physiological recruitment of these receptors in mammals. Additionally, the presence and function of astrocytes, as well as geometric factors such as size, shape, and orientation, affect local concentrations of K+. Therefore, the framework described here provides multiple approaches that scientists can use to measure and interpret different mechanisms contributing to the generation of inhibitory signals in the nervous system.

43093736.autores: Rishiq A, Birman I, … Golenser J (6 autores)
43093736.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Prevention of Experimental Severe Malaria», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43093736.resumo_original: Background: Severe malaria, including cerebral malaria and malaria-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome, remains associated with high mortality despite anti-plasmodial and supportive therapies. This study evaluates whether a drug combination can prevent severe malaria complications in a well-defined experimental model. The combination includes an anti-plasmodial artemisinin derivative, a tyrosine kinase inhibitor originally developed for anti-angiogenic cancer therapy, and the general immunosuppressant dexamethasone. Methods: C57BL/6 mice were infected with Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA sub1a strain). Disease progression was assessed using MRI, histology, and liver enzyme analysis and by monitoring parasitemia and survival. The drugs administered included the anti-plasmodial agent artemisone (Art), dexamethasone (Dex), a systemic immunosuppressant, and apatinib (Apa) and sunitinib, both angiogenesis inhibitors. Additional experiments were performed in infected Ncr1-deficient and Tigit-KO transgenic mice (which show decreased or increased activation of NK cells, respectively). Results: PbA infection in C57bl/6 mice induced mild cerebral pathology, severe pulmonary inflammation with edema and microhemorrhages, and elevated liver enzymes, followed by death within a week post-infection, despite relatively low parasitemia on the day of death. Early treatment with Art, starting two- or three days post-infection (PI), killed the parasites and led to complete recovery. Dex, Apa, and sunitinib, initiated at the same early time points PI, prevented acute mortality. However, about two weeks later, these mice developed high parasitemia and succumbed to the disease. Late treatment (starting five days PI) with the individual compounds was ineffective. In contrast, late combined treatment with Dex, Apa, and Art eliminated the plasmodia and rescued most mice. Infection of Ncr1-deficient or Tigit-KO mice resulted in rapidly fatal disease with a course similar to that in mice with the same genetic background, indicating that partial immunosuppression or immune enhancement is insufficient to inhibit malaria progression and that NK cells do not necessarily play a role in the pathology. Conclusions: Multi-target therapy using anti-plasmodial, immunomodulatory, and anti-angiogenic agents has the potential to prevent severe malaria complications and improve survival outcomes.

43090525.titulo: Exploratory Survey of Fungal Communities and Cultivable Yeasts Associated with Mosquito Larval Habitats in Italy
43090525.autores: Cappelli A, Damiani C, … Ricci I (6 autores)
43090525.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Exploratory Survey of Fungal Communities and Cultivable Yeasts Associated with Mosquito Larval Habitats in Italy», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43090525.resumo_original: Fungi represent recurrent components of mosquito-associated microbial communities, but the larval mycobiota remains far less documented than its bacterial counterpart. Here, we conducted an exploratory survey of fungal communities associated with mosquito larvae collected across central and north-eastern Italy during 2022 and 2023, collecting Aedes albopictus, Aedes koreicus and Culex pipiens larvae and related breeding waters. A subset of 16 larval pools and five water samples was analysed via ITS metabarcoding, while 23 samples were subjected to culture-dependent isolation. Metabarcoding revealed fungal assemblages dominated by Ascomycota and Basidiomycota and Rozellomycota sensu lato, with prominent yeast genera such as Wickerhamomyces, Kurtzmaniella, Candida, Rhodotorula and Metschnikowia. Cultivation yielded 21 yeast isolates assigned to seven distinct species: Candida parapsilosis, Metschnikowia pulcherrima, Barnettozyma californica, Schwanniomyces vanrijiae, Sporobolomyces roseus, Wickerhamomyces anomalus and Rhodotorula paludigena. Overlap between cultured yeast genera and metabarcoding profiles confirmed the complementary nature of the two approaches. This study documents fungal associations in three relevant mosquito species and provides, to our knowledge, the first ITS metabarcoding-based description of the mycobiota in field-collected Ae. koreicus larvae. Although the constrained sampling design precludes definitive inferences regarding host specificity or geographic patterns, the findings provide a baseline for larger studies of mosquito-associated fungal diversity.

43087033.titulo: Implications of the trade-offs between negative density-dependence and Allee effects for vector control
43087033.autores: Kipingu AM, Kiware S, … Viana M (5 autores)
43087033.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Implications of the trade-offs between negative density-dependence and Allee effects for vector control», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43087033.resumo_original:
Understanding population dynamics is fundamental for predicting species persistence and extinction, yet remains challenging because of the complex interplay among ecological, environmental, and anthropogenic factors. Population dynamics are regulated by intrinsic processes, such as negative density-dependence, driven by factors, including resource competition during larval development, and Allee effects, which can arise through mechanisms such as mate limitation at low population densities. While negative density-dependence is well-understood, Allee effects have received comparatively less attention despite important implications for conservation and population management. For disease vectors, both negative density-dependence and Allee effects can influence whether populations persist, rebound following control, or are driven to elimination. In malaria mosquitoes, negative density-dependence at the larval stages is well-known to regulate population growth, whereas Allee effects have not been empirically demonstrated, and their potential implications and interactions with negative density-dependence remain poorly understood. This study addresses this gap using a population simulation model to evaluate the trade-offs between negative density-dependence and potential mate-finding Allee effects and their implications for vector control. It is possible that, depending on the vector control strategy, Allee effects could become important at low densities and push populations closer to extinction.
A stochastic stage-structured population simulation model representing a simplified mosquito life cycle was developed. Negative density-dependence and mate-finding Allee effects were incorporated as processes affecting larval survival and total fecundity, respectively. Their effects were examined by varying the strength of both processes independently and jointly, under different vector control scenarios: control, sustained and shorter-term interventions (here, immolating larvicides) that reduced larval population.
When considered separately, neither negative density-dependence nor mate-finding Allee effects had a substantial long-term effect on population persistence, although negative density-dependence substantially altered equilibrium abundance. However, their combined effects accelerated population decline and increased the likelihood of extinction as the strength of both processes increased. Because Allee effects operate on low population abundances, sustained interventions were able to reduce mosquito populations to levels, where Allee effects became important, thereby increasing the probability of extinction. In contrast, short-term interventions led to population rebound, driven by negative density-dependence as formulated in the simulation.
Understanding less-studied regulatory processes such as Allee effects can support vector control by identifying stages of the vector life cycle that are either resilient or vulnerable to interventions. The results suggest that, if present, the mate-finding Allee effects and density-dependent resource competition considered in this study could potentially be leveraged to accelerate vector control and support the elimination of vector-borne diseases, such as malaria.

43079781.titulo: Indium Stress in Plants: Toxicity Mechanisms, Physiological Adaptation, and Emerging Mitigation Strategies
43079781.autores: Ali B, Rehman M, … Gan Y (6 autores)
43079781.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Indium Stress in Plants: Toxicity Mechanisms, Physiological Adaptation, and Emerging Mitigation Strategies», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43079781.resumo_original: Indium is widely used in high-tech industries and renewable energy applications; however, its increasing environmental release from industrial activities and electronic waste recycling poses a growing threat to agricultural ecosystems. In response to this growing challenge, this review comprehensively synthesizes the biogeochemical fate of indium and its phytotoxic effects, focusing on soil dynamics and root retention, physiological and molecular mechanisms of toxicity, and emerging mitigation strategies. In soils, indium exhibits remarkably low mobility and strong root retention, resulting in severe growth inhibition. It profoundly disrupts nutrient homeostasis, particularly that of phosphorus, magnesium, and iron, thereby triggering excessive production of reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (ROS/RNS). Consequently, indium toxicity induces lipid peroxidation, photosynthetic dysfunction, caspase-like programmed cell death, and premature cell-wall lignification. While multi-omics evidence reveals that plants attempt to counter this toxicity via phosphate-starvation signaling, autophagy, and antioxidant defenses, acute redox imbalance often overwhelms these intrinsic defense mechanisms. To contextualize these findings, we highlight indium's distinct biogeochemical behavior relative to other metal contaminants and technology-critical elements, thereby integrating systems-level insights into plant stress responses. Additionally, we evaluate promising mitigation strategies, emphasizing biochar amendments, root exudate regulation (e.g., flavonols), and beneficial nanomaterials, including silicon- and selenium-based materials, titanium dioxide nanoparticles, and emerging heteroatom-doped carbon dots, for enhancing plant resilience. Ultimately, we propose that the development and field validation of these targeted mitigation strategies will be essential for safeguarding sustainable crop productivity in indium-contaminated agroecosystems.

43088783.titulo: Reticulon-3 at the Interface of Hepatitis C and Dengue Virus Infection: Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Transfer and Emerging Antiviral Vulnerabilities
43088783.autores: Noumi T, Bitazar R, … Bukong TN (5 autores)
43088783.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Reticulon-3 at the Interface of Hepatitis C and Dengue Virus Infection: Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Transfer and Emerging Antiviral Vulnerabilities», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43088783.resumo_original: Positive-sense RNA viruses are commonly classified by genome organization, entry route, tissue tropism, and clinical syndrome, but these categories do not explain how viruses construct protected replication niches or route infectious material between cells. The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) provides a shared platform for viral translation, replication-organelle formation, membrane curvature, lipid remodeling, innate immune regulation, and vesicular trafficking. Within this framework, reticulon-3 (RTN3) has emerged as a candidate regulator linking ER-based RNA-virus replication to the generation of infectious extracellular-vesicle cargo. Hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV) provide complementary experimental settings for evaluating this model despite their distinct transmission routes, tissue tropisms, disease courses, and immune pathophysiology. HCV most clearly demonstrates that exosome-enriched fractions can transfer replication-competent viral RNA with defined host cofactors, whereas DENV provides an acute infection model for examining related transfer phenotypes. Both viruses nevertheless replicate within remodeled ER membranes and can transfer infection-competent material in a vesicle-associated form. Functional perturbation studies implicate RTN3 in the output of infection-associated vesicle preparations, but do not yet establish direct recognition of viral RNA or its incorporation into endosomal intraluminal vesicles. RTN3 can also restrict HCV replication through NS4B interactions, suggesting that its effects vary by endpoint and may reflect distinct functions at different stages of infection. Related membrane-remodeling and vesicle-associated processes in Zika virus, West Nile virus, enteroviruses, SARS-CoV-2, and hepatitis A virus illustrate broader exploitation of host membrane organization, but replication-membrane phenotypes and vesicle-associated dissemination in these systems do not establish an RTN3-dependent infectious EV pathway. In selected models, EV-enriched preparations contain protected viral cargo and transfer biological activity to recipient cells; neither particle enrichment nor infectivity alone resolves the carrier's identity. Advances in isolation and characterization, including density-gradient or size-exclusion separation, immunoaffinity selection, particle and marker profiling, membrane-protection assays, and recipient-cell infectivity testing, now permit more rigorous identification of defined vesicle populations, protected cargo, and biological activity. Nevertheless, RTN3 should not be considered a universal RNA-virus dependency, nor should extracellular-vesicle release be assumed to generate uniformly infectious populations. Instead, HCV and DENV support functional involvement of RTN3 in vesicle-associated output, while the molecular connection between ER organization and selective cargo enclosure remains unresolved. Defining these shared and virus-specific dependencies may reveal host-virus interfaces suitable for broad-spectrum or resistance-resilient intervention, provided that infection-selective reliance, a measurable therapeutic window, and preservation of essential host-cell functions can be demonstrated.

43085652.titulo: Enhanced Protection by Fluoride Varnish with Nano-Sized Sodium Trimetaphosphate Against Enamel Erosive Wear: An In Situ Study
43085652.autores: Paiva MF, Delbem ACB, … Pessan JP (10 autores)
43085652.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Enhanced Protection by Fluoride Varnish with Nano-Sized Sodium Trimetaphosphate Against Enamel Erosive Wear: An In Situ Study», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43085652.resumo_original:
To assess the effects of fluoride varnishes containing micrometric or nano-sized sodium trimetaphosphate (TMPmicro or TMPnano, respectively) on erosive tooth wear (ETW) in situ.
In this randomized, double-blind, crossover study, 14 participants wore palatal devices containing bovine enamel blocks (n=4/device), which received each of the four varnish treatments in separate experimental periods: Placebo (Pla - without F/TMP); 5% NaF (5NaF); 5NaF + 5% TMPmicro (5-TMPmicro); and 5NaF + 5% TMPnano (5-TMPnano). After 6 h of intraoral exposure and varnish removal, the blocks underwent four daily erosive challenges ex vivo for five days (ERO, 0.05 M citric acid, pH 3.2, 90 s), while two blocks were additionally subjected to abrasion by brushing (ERO+ABR). Profilometry, surface hardness (SH), cross-sectional hardness (ΔKHN) and computed X-ray micro tomography (gHAp × cm⁻³ × µm) were performed. Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA and Holm-Sidak's test (p<0.05).
ETW, integrated mineral loss and depth of mineral loss of the remaining eroded enamel showed a consistent treatment ranking under both conditions, with the greatest protection observed for 5-TMPnano, followed by 5-TMPmicro, 5NaF, and Pla. Compared with 5NaF, ETW was reduced by 20-22% with 5-TMPmicro and 40-50% with 5-TMPnano under ERO and ERO+ABR. A similar pattern was observed for hardness in depth (ΔKHN at 5-30 µm from the enamel surface), except between 5-TMPmicro and 5-TMPnano. Compared with 5NaF, SH loss was significantly lower for both TMP-containing varnishes under ERO, but only for 5-TMPnano under ERO+ABR.
F varnish supplemented with TMP significantly reduced ETW in situ, and nano-sized TMP provided additional protection.
The addition of TMP to 5% NaF varnishes, especially as nanoparticles, may enhance their protective effect against enamel erosive wear.

43086959.titulo: Transcriptomic analyses reveal how parasites exploit plasticity in caste and brain development of social wasps
43086959.autores: Vacca NA, Padilla-Choy V, … Uy FMK (4 autores)
43086959.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Transcriptomic analyses reveal how parasites exploit plasticity in caste and brain development of social wasps», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43086959.resumo_original:
The evolution of castes in social insects is one of the most spectacular examples of phenotypic plasticity. However, this adaptive plasticity could instead be exploited by parasites to develop an extended phenotype. We characterize the timing and molecular changes induced by enigmatic twisted-wing insects to manipulate developing social wasps. These parasites reprogram short-lived female workers into phenotypes that are long-lived like queens, while hindering ovary development and cooperative behavior. Using differential gene expression analyses across developmental stages of naturally infected and uninfected brood coupled with experimental infections, we uncovered that parasites manipulate the developmental plasticity that determines caste bias.
Parasite larvae infected most host larval instars. Across development, we identified 2341 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between uninfected workers and gynes (future queens), 529 DEGs between infected and uninfected workers, and 2672 DEGs between infected workers and uninfected gynes. However, robust differences in the number of DEGs were unique to each host stage. Specifically, candidate genes linked caste bias to insulin and juvenile hormone pathways, immune responses, and neural development. Controlling for the effect of nutrition and social interactions in development through our infection experiment revealed that the parasites consistently targeted caste bias and neural genes. Finally, infecting long-lived gyne brood that is not targeted in nature showed minimal manipulation.
Our findings reveal how stage-specific targeting of caste plasticity initiates the reprogramming of hosts towards the long-lived extended phenotype. We propose leveraging emerging host-parasite systems to unravel the molecular mechanisms underlying adaptive developmental plasticity.

43079707.titulo: Hemozoin-Targeting and Glutathione-Responsive Theranostic Prodrug Platform for Targeted Malaria Therapy
43079707.autores: Tayde D, Ali S, … Pramanik SK (4 autores)
43079707.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Hemozoin-Targeting and Glutathione-Responsive Theranostic Prodrug Platform for Targeted Malaria Therapy», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43079707.resumo_original: Malaria remains a major global health challenge, while the efficacy of artemisinin-based combination therapies is increasingly threatened by emerging resistance, treatment failure, and dose-limiting toxicity. Here, we report a stimulus-responsive antimalarial prodrug designed to exploit parasite-specific biochemical and physicochemical features. A hemozoin-targeting, reduction-responsive dihydroartemisinin (DHA) prodrug, DHA-SS-SmCp, was constructed by conjugating DHA to a luminescent Sm(DBM)3PHEN-NH2 complex through a glutathione (GSH)-cleavable disulfide linker. The prodrug spontaneously assembled into stable, monodisperse nanoparticles (534 ± 10 nm; PDI ≈ 0.084), enabling nanoparticle-mediated delivery and imaging. The reductive intracellular environment promotes disulfide cleavage and efficient DHA release, while the paramagnetic Sm complex facilitates association with hemozoin-rich parasite compartments. This integrated design provides both stimulus-responsive drug activation and parasite-associated imaging capabilities. In a Plasmodium yoelii N67-infected mouse model, DHA-SS-SmCp administered at 30 mg/kg DHA equivalent achieved complete parasite clearance, whereas free DHA at the same dose did not. By integrating redox-triggered activation, hemozoin affinity, luminescent imaging, and self-assembled nanodelivery, this study establishes a chemically programmed prodrug platform for selective antimalarial therapy and provides a framework for developing parasite-responsive therapeutics.

43080262.titulo: Bone turnover and phosphate metabolism in children with Prader-Willi syndrome: results from two tertiary centers
43080262.autores: Cheleș AD, Nicoară DM, … Mărginean O (9 autores)
43080262.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Bone turnover and phosphate metabolism in children with Prader-Willi syndrome: results from two tertiary centers», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43080262.resumo_original: Prader-Willi syndrome (PWS) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by impaired growth, altered body composition, and reduced bone mineral accrual. However, the relationships between skeletal maturation, bone turnover, and phosphate homeostasis during childhood remain insufficiently understood. This study explored bone turnover, somatotropic function, skeletal maturation, and phosphate metabolism in children with PWS compared with healthy peers. In this two-center retrospective case-control study, 40 children and adolescents with molecularly confirmed PWS and 40 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were evaluated between January 2016 and May 2026. Anthropometric measurements, bone age, somatotropic axis parameters, bone turnover markers, and indices of phosphate metabolism were analyzed using multivariable-adjusted models, correlation analyses, regression models, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses. Compared with controls, children with PWS showed a pattern of lower circulating bone turnover markers characterized by significantly lower osteocalcin, C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen, bone-specific alkaline phosphatase, and insulin-like growth factor I, together with a reduced molar insulin-like growth factor I/insulin-like growth factor-binding protein-3 ratio and delayed skeletal maturation. Phosphate metabolism was characterized by higher serum phosphorus, tubular reabsorption of phosphate, and tubular maximum reabsorption of phosphate per glomerular filtration rate, accompanied by lower fibroblast growth factor 23, ionized calcium, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D. Within the PWS group, bone turnover markers correlated with bone age. In exploratory analyses, growth hormone treatment status was not significantly associated with insulin-like growth factor I or major bone turnover markers; however, interpretation was limited by incomplete information regarding treatment dose, duration, age at initiation and adherence. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis identified bone age delay (AUC = 0.847) and bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (AUC = 0.842) as the strongest discriminators of PWS versus control status within the study population. Children and adolescents with PWS showed cross-sectional differences in skeletal maturation, bone turnover, and phosphate homeostasis compared with healthy controls. These findings should be considered exploratory and require confirmation in longitudinal studies incorporating detailed growth hormone exposure, bone density, and body composition assessments.

43090559.titulo: Combined Spinosad and Pyriproxyfen in Toxic Sugar Baits Enhances Suppression of Culex quinquefasciatus
43090559.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Combined Spinosad and Pyriproxyfen in Toxic Sugar Baits Enhances Suppression of Culex quinquefasciatus», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43090559.resumo_original: Combining insecticides with different biological activities may improve the effectiveness of toxic sugar baits (TSBs) for adult mosquito control. This study evaluated the lethal and sublethal effects of spinosad, pyriproxyfen, and their combination in TSBs against adult Culex quinquefasciatus. Concentration-response assays showed concentration-dependent mortality for both insecticides. Pyriproxyfen had lower LC50 estimates than spinosad, with values of 2.61 and 1.60 ppm for females and males, respectively, compared with 4.84 and 3.58 ppm for spinosad. Sublethal exposure to either insecticide reduced longevity, fecundity, and fertility, while adult size was unaffected. The combined treatment produced the greatest reductions in longevity, fecundity, and fertility compared with either insecticide alone. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining spinosad and pyriproxyfen in TSB formulations to enhance suppression of adult Cx. quinquefasciatus. Further studies are needed to investigate potential interactions between these insecticides and evaluate their combined effectiveness under field conditions.

43079943.titulo: Acupuncture Integration in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS): A Comprehensive Evidence-Based Review
43079943.autores: Yang W, Xu J, … Zheng Y (5 autores)
43079943.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Acupuncture Integration in Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS): A Comprehensive Evidence-Based Review», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43079943.resumo_original: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols have significantly improved perioperative outcomes; however, challenges including opioid-related adverse effects, postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV), delayed gastrointestinal recovery, and chronic post-surgical pain remain incompletely resolved. These limitations are closely linked to perioperative neuroimmune and autonomic dysregulation, which current pharmacologic strategies do not adequately address. This review examines acupuncture and acupoint-based stimulation modalities, including electroacupuncture and transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation, as adjunctive interventions within ERAS pathways. Current evidence suggests that these modalities may reduce postoperative pain and opioid consumption, decrease PONV incidence, and support gastrointestinal recovery in selected perioperative settings, with generally acceptable safety when delivered by trained practitioners. Mechanistic investigations suggest that these effects may involve modulation of spinal nociceptive processing, vagal anti-inflammatory pathways, and autonomic balance. Despite heterogeneity in study design and intervention protocols, the cumulative evidence supports the potential role of acupuncture as an adjunctive perioperative strategy, particularly for PONV and selected recovery outcomes. Acupuncture may serve as a mechanism-informed adjunct within ERAS pathways, with stronger conclusions requiring large, high-quality randomized controlled trials using standardized protocols and clinically meaningful endpoints.

43090087.titulo: From Bacterial Persistence to Granuloma Failure: Mechanisms of LTBI Reactivation as a Framework for Tuberculosis Prevention and Treatment
43090087.autores: Zhang L, Sun W, … Gong W (4 autores)
43090087.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «From Bacterial Persistence to Granuloma Failure: Mechanisms of LTBI Reactivation as a Framework for Tuberculosis Prevention and Treatment», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43090087.resumo_original: Latent tuberculosis infection constitutes the principal reservoir from which tuberculosis (TB) disease emerges, yet the molecular transition from durable containment to reactivation remains incompletely resolved. Reactivation is not a single bacterial "awakening" event or a nonspecific consequence of immunosuppression. Instead, we propose a hypothesis-generating threshold framework across an interconnected pathogen-host-microenvironment system. This narrative review integrates evidence on Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence and resuscitation programs, including metabolic remodeling, resuscitation-promoting factors, cell-wall turnover, and metal acquisition, with defects in adaptive and innate immunity, immunometabolic control, cytokine networks, aging, comorbid disease, and epigenetic regulation. We further examine the granuloma as a spatially heterogeneous ecosystem in which hypoxia, necrosis, vascular dysfunction, fibrosis, extracellular-vesicle communication, and intercellular crosstalk may influence bacterial control. Evidence from human longitudinal and cross-sectional studies is distinguished from non-human primate, other animal, in vitro, and cross-system evidence. The proposed balance between bacillary resuscitation potential and local containment capacity has not been prospectively validated in humans or defined by a numerical clinical cutoff. Pathogen-, host-, and lesion-directed approaches are therefore discussed as research priorities. They are not alternatives to recommended TB preventive treatment for eligible individuals or antimicrobial treatment of TB disease. Prospective human validation is required before the framework can inform biomarker-guided intervention or patient stratification.

43093833.titulo: Characterization of Pathogenic Features of Dengue Virus Serotypes 1-4 in the AG129 Mouse Model
43093833.autores: Cai C, Ding K, … Sun Q (12 autores)
43093833.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Characterization of Pathogenic Features of Dengue Virus Serotypes 1-4 in the AG129 Mouse Model», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093833.resumo_original: An AG129 mouse infection model with four DENV isolates was established to systematically characterize the early pathogenic phenotypes of these strains. DENV-1 caused 100% mortality by 15 dpi, with sustained viremia, widespread multi-organ injury, and persistent leukopenia. DENV-4 exhibited peak viremia at 4 dpi and unique neurovirulence, presenting exclusive hind-limb paralysis, severe pulmonary hemorrhage, and characteristic cerebral parenchymal lesions. DENV-2 and DENV-3 induced only transient mild viremia and focal tissue alterations without mortality. Hematological and biochemical alterations, as well as occasional splenic hemosiderin deposition, were noted among infected animals. This preclinical dataset offers insights into serotype-specific DENV pathogenesis and may aid future evaluation of broad-spectrum antivirals and tetravalent vaccine candidates.

43095935.titulo: Discovery of Indazole-Based Dual-Pharmacophore Inhibitors of Dengue and Zika Proteases as Promising Antivirals
43095935.autores: Singh SK, Potluri V, … Prasad PK (13 autores)
43095935.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Discovery of Indazole-Based Dual-Pharmacophore Inhibitors of Dengue and Zika Proteases as Promising Antivirals», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43095935.resumo_original: Flavivirus outbreaks caused by dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) remain a major global health challenge, with no FDA-approved antivirals available. Herein, we designed, synthesized, and evaluated indazole-based dual pharmacophore motifs targeting NS2B-NS3 serine proteases, essential for viral replication. Enzymatic assays revealed nanomolar to sub-micromolar potency, with strong selectivity over host serine proteases, minimizing off-target risks. Biophysical studies showed ligand-induced thermal stabilization, while kinetic and dialysis analyses confirmed a reversible, competitive, non-covalent inhibition mechanism. In DENV-infected Vero CCL-81 cells, several leads exhibited potent antiviral activity with low cytotoxicity. Notably, compound C8 demonstrated low-nanomolar enzyme inhibition against both viruses, translating to complete viral suppression in cells (EC50 = 0.5 μM) with a good selectivity index, underscoring its therapeutic potential. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported these findings, revealing key active-site interactions consistent with potency and specificity. Collectively, these results highlight indazole-based dual-pharmacophore inhibitors as promising anti-flaviviral leads.

43078339.titulo: Stochastic dynamics of a multi-stage dengue model with vaccination and saturated incidence rates
43078339.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Stochastic dynamics of a multi-stage dengue model with vaccination and saturated incidence rates», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43078339.resumo_original: Complex population movements and inherent disruptive environmental factors render it more challenging to analyse the pathogenic dengue virus. Research on epidemic mathematical frameworks may assist in protecting the economy and public health in addition to predicting the dengue epidemic's development pattern. Influenced by this, we discuss the six-dimensional ShVhIhRh-SvIv dengue stochastic epidemic model. For this stochastic system, we first verify the existence and uniqueness of a positive global solution. Next, we construct the suitable Lyapunov function to analyse the existence and uniqueness of a stationary distribution with ergodic features by Khasminskii's method. To investigate the statistical report for the existing stationary distribution by using a probability density function. This yields, the expression of the probability density function near quasi-endemic equilibrium of log-normal properties is solved by the Fokker-Planck equation. Furthermore, sufficient conditions are derived to eradicate and control the dengue transmission. Subsequently, numerical simulations are executed to validate the mathematical predictions, and the impact of environmental disturbances and key parameters on dengue transmission is taken into account as well.

43086879.titulo: Assessment of the coverage, use rate and physical integrity of long-lasting insecticide nets after scaling up of their distribution in Gujarat, India
43086879.autores: Baharia RK, Vadhel A, … Yadav CP (5 autores)
43086879.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Assessment of the coverage, use rate and physical integrity of long-lasting insecticide nets after scaling up of their distribution in Gujarat, India», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43086879.resumo_original:
Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (LLINs) are a key tool for control and elimination of malaria, by providing protection from the bite of infected mosquitoes. To support its malaria elimination goal by 2030, Gujarat distributed LLINs across 33 districts in 2019. However, sustained effectiveness depends on consistent use and proper maintenance.
A household-based cross-sectional survey was conducted in the Anand, Kutch, Panchmahal, and Surendranagar districts of the state of Gujarat in India. A Standard WHO questionnaire was used to assess LLIN coverage, usage, and maintenance. A total of 4719 households were surveyed. Net ownership, usage patterns, physical integrity (Hole size, washing and dry pattern), and maintenance practices were evaluated.
LLIN ownership was high (93.8%), but consistent usage was lower (51.9%). Seasonal variation in adherence was observed, with 86.5% of households using LLINs year-round and 91.8% using them while sleeping outdoors. Maintenance practices varied: 76.5% of households washed their nets regularly, but 51.6% dried them in direct sunlight, which may reduce their efficacy. Physical durability was compromised, with 27.3% of nets developing holes due to wear and misuse. Additionally, 23.6% of households repurposed LLINs for activities such as fishing or livestock protection.
Despite high coverage, gaps in consistent usage, proper care, and net durability remain challenges. Addressing these through community education, discouraging alternative net use, and improving sleeping conditions is essential to maximize the impact of LLINs. Strengthening behavioral interventions and maintenance practices will enhance LLIN effectiveness and contribute to Gujarat's malaria elimination efforts.

43085668.titulo: Recent advances in the glioma tumor microenvironment (TME): cellular interactions, signaling networks, and therapeutic opportunities
43085668.autores: Moqbel AQ, Ghani MU, … Ke X (7 autores)
43085668.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Recent advances in the glioma tumor microenvironment (TME): cellular interactions, signaling networks, and therapeutic opportunities», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43085668.resumo_original: Gliomas are treatment-resistant primary brain tumors, with glioblastoma (GBM) representing the most aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma. Their progression reflects the interplay between tumor-intrinsic alterations and the surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME). The TME comprises immune, stromal, vascular, and extracellular matrix (ECM) components, which together shape tumor growth, invasion, immune evasion, and treatment response. In GBM, tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), microglia, astrocytes, and endothelial cells interact with tumor cells through cytokine, chemokine, growth-factor, and extracellular-vesicle signaling, influencing tumor behavior and antitumor immunity. Hypoxia, vascular dysfunction, and ECM remodeling further shape this environment by altering tumor metabolism, angiogenesis, immune activity, and glioma-cell invasion. Molecular alterations, including EGFR activation, IDH mutations, BRAF alterations, and PTEN loss, also influence TME organization across glioma subtypes and contribute to differences in disease progression and treatment response. Despite advances in standard treatment, recurrence and therapeutic resistance remain major challenges, particularly in GBM. These challenges have driven interest in TME-directed strategies, including immunotherapy, anti-angiogenic therapy, metabolic interventions, vaccines, and myeloid-targeted approaches. Although several strategies have shown promise in preclinical models and clinical studies, their therapeutic efficacy remains variable. This review provides an integrated analysis of the glioma TME, with particular emphasis on GBM. We examine how immune, vascular, metabolic, ECM, and tumor-intrinsic factors interact to shape disease progression and treatment response. We also discuss emerging TME-targeted therapies and experimental models that deepen mechanistic understanding of glioma biology and may guide the development of more precise and effective treatments.

43092347.titulo: The Holobiont Bioreactor: Microbiome Dynamics, Biosafety Paradoxes, and Ecological Engineering in Black Soldier Fly Bioconversion
43092347.autores: Dabravolski SA, Pavshintsev VV, … Mitkin NA (6 autores)
43092347.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «The Holobiont Bioreactor: Microbiome Dynamics, Biosafety Paradoxes, and Ecological Engineering in Black Soldier Fly Bioconversion», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43092347.resumo_original: The black soldier fly (Hermetia illucens L.) has emerged as a cornerstone technology for the circular economy, valorising organic waste into high-value insect protein and biofertiliser. The efficiency, safety, and adaptability of this bioconversion process are fundamentally dictated by the complex interplay between the insect host and its gut microbiome, which together function as an integrated 'holobiont bioreactor'. This reactor is characterised by partially vertically transmitted core taxa and a dynamic, horizontally acquired microbial community. This review critically synthesises high-impact original research identified through a systematic literature search published predominantly between 2021 and 2026, incorporating foundational landmark studies, to provide a mechanistic overview of this holobiont's function. We first dissect the architecture of the BSFL microbiome, examining the 'nature vs. nurture' debate of egg-associated vertical inheritance versus horizontal acquisition and highlighting the critical, yet often overlooked, role of the fungal mycobiome. We then explore the larval gut as a spatio-temporally compartmentalised bioreactor, where extreme physicochemical gradients and host-microbe metabolic crosstalk drive nutrient extraction and immunity. A central focus is placed on the 'Bioremediation vs. Biosafety Paradox', wherein the system's capacity to degrade chemical xenobiotics and sanitise pathogens is contrasted with its propensity to amplify antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and bioaccumulate contaminants like heavy metals and microplastics under specific substrate and exposure conditions. Finally, we evaluate the frontier of microbiome engineering from the deployment of native probiotics and synthetic microbial consortia (SynComs) to enhance performance to the use of prebiotics for mitigating ammonia emissions. This synthesis reveals that while BSFL technology holds immense promise, its industrial maturation is constrained by significant methodological limitations in the current literature. We conclude by advocating for a field-wide shift towards integrated multi-omics and viability-based analytical frameworks to ensure the development of safe, efficient, and regulatory-compliant bioconversion systems.

43086905.titulo: Environmental indicators and large-scale climatic variability associated with malaria incidence in southeastern Iran: a 23-year negative binomial analysis
43086905.autores: Dehghan A, Rahimi M, … Hanafi-Bojd AA (6 autores)
43086905.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Environmental indicators and large-scale climatic variability associated with malaria incidence in southeastern Iran: a 23-year negative binomial analysis», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43086905.resumo_original:
Malaria transmission is influenced by climatic and environmental conditions, but the relative contributions of large-scale climate variability and local environmental factors remain unclear in southeastern Iran. We assessed associations between ENSO, remotely sensed environmental indicators, monsoon precipitation, and malaria incidence during 2001-2023.
Monthly malaria surveillance data from eight counties in southeastern Iran (2001-2023) were analyzed using a retrospective ecological longitudinal design. Predictors included Niño 3.4 ENSO, NDVI, NDWI, and LST, with candidate lags evaluated based on model fit, estimated effects, and epidemiological plausibility. The primary analysis used a negative binomial mixed-effects model (NB-GLMM) with a log link, population offset, calendar-month adjustment, a four-degree-of-freedom nonlinear temporal trend, and county-level random intercepts. A quadratic term for six-month lagged LST was included to assess nonlinearity. County-specific models and random-slope analyses were used to assess spatial heterogeneity, while monsoon precipitation was analyzed separately using cumulative June-September rainfall in Chabahar, Saravan, and Sarbaz.
In the final province-wide model, six-month lagged LST showed a significant nonlinear, U-shaped association with malaria incidence, with the estimated minimum occurring at approximately 0.32 standard deviations above the mean LST. ENSO (IRR = 1.01, 95% CI 0.95-1.08; p = 0.653), NDVI (IRR = 0.99, 95% CI 0.83-1.18; p = 0.888), and NDWI (IRR = 1.21, 95% CI 0.91-1.60; p = 0.192) were not independently associated with malaria incidence. County-specific analyses showed heterogeneous environmental associations, while formal random-slope analyses supported significant between-county heterogeneity for ENSO, NDVI, and NDWI but not LST. Monsoon-season precipitation was not significantly associated with annual malaria incidence in the analyzed counties. Environmental associations were substantially attenuated after adjustment for nonlinear long-term temporal variation.
Lagged LST showed a nonlinear province-wide association with malaria incidence, whereas ENSO, NDVI, and NDWI showed no independent associations. The attenuation of environmental associations after nonlinear temporal adjustment highlights the importance of accounting for long-term epidemiological trends. County-level heterogeneity indicates that environmental associations are context-dependent. The observed associations should not be interpreted as causal effects.

43092221.titulo: Plant-Mediated Silver Nanoparticles for Aedes aegypti Control: Larvicidal Efficacy and Mechanisms
43092221.autores: Seeniponnalagu S, Rajendran K, … Gurusamy D (5 autores)
43092221.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Plant-Mediated Silver Nanoparticles for Aedes aegypti Control: Larvicidal Efficacy and Mechanisms», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43092221.resumo_original: Aedes aegypti L. in Hasselquist (Diptera: Culicidae) is a major vector of dengue, chikungunya, Zika, and other arboviral diseases. Increasing insecticide resistance and environmental concerns highlight the need for sustainable vector-control strategies. Phytochemical-mediated silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) are promising bio-larvicidal agents because plant-derived metabolites contribute to nanoparticle formation, stabilization, and biological activity. This review provides a mechanistic and comparative assessment of green-synthesized AgNPs for A. aegypti control. It examines the roles of phytochemicals, including phenolics, flavonoids, terpenoids, and alkaloids, in nanoparticle synthesis and discusses how particle size, morphology, surface chemistry, and synthesis conditions influence larvicidal efficacy. Comparative analysis indicates that reported larvicidal activity varies with extract composition, nanoparticle characteristics, larval stage, exposure duration, and bioassay conditions, limiting direct comparisons of lethal concentrations across studies. Across the studies reviewed, plant-extract composition and synthesis-dependent nanoparticle characteristics emerge as important determinants of activity; however, their effects are difficult to separate from differences in larval stage, exposure duration, tested dose, and bioassay protocol. These methodological and material discrepancies elucidate the variability in reported lethal concentrations and the frequent unreliability of direct efficacy rankings across studies. Major toxicity mechanisms, including reactive oxygen species generation, oxidative stress, membrane disruption, enzyme inhibition, DNA damage, and apoptosis, are examined, with consideration of the distinction between experimentally demonstrated and proposed mechanisms in A. aegypti. The review also evaluates dose-response relationships and potential effects on non-target organisms and aquatic ecosystems. The contribution of plant metabolites to larvicidal activity and the relative roles of nanoparticles and released silver ions remain important research gaps. Challenges in standardization, reproducibility, scale-up, environmental safety, regulatory approval, and field validation are highlighted. Future research should prioritize harmonized synthesis and bioassay protocols, mechanistic validation, comprehensive ecological risk assessment, and field evaluation to support the responsible development of phytogenic AgNPs for mosquito control.

43092085.titulo: Protein Lactylation in Sepsis-Associated Acute Lung Injury: Evidence and Controversies
43092085.autores: Sun X, Zhang S, … Mao Z (5 autores)
43092085.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Protein Lactylation in Sepsis-Associated Acute Lung Injury: Evidence and Controversies», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43092085.resumo_original: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury/acute respiratory distress syndrome (SA-ALI/ARDS) is an important complication of sepsis involving disruption of the alveolar-capillary barrier and immunometabolic dysregulation. Lysine lactylation (Kla) may link metabolic states to transcriptional regulation and protein function. However, blood lactate, global Kla abundance, and the function of lactylation at specific sites are not interchangeable. This review organizes the evidence by cell type, histone and non-histone substrate, and modification site, and separately evaluates modification identification, functional perturbation, lung injury phenotypes in animal models, and observations in patients. Current studies do not show a uniform direction of effect: some lactylation events have been associated with glycocalyx degradation, ferroptosis, inflammatory amplification, and intercellular injury signaling, whereas other studies report protective feedback. Differences in models and levels of intervention limit direct comparisons. Evidence for context dependence is emerging, but dependencies on time, concentration, and disease stage have not been adequately validated. Histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) in patient samples provides a candidate biomarker signal; its independent clinical value and the efficacy of lactylation-targeted interventions remain to be established. Future work should prioritize cell- and site-specific causal validation and connect these studies with standardized assays in patient samples and external clinical validation.

43085676.titulo: Phosphorus concentration from low-phosphorus wastewater using embedded phosphorus removal biofillers coupled with anaerobic cyclic phosphorus release: performance evaluation and microbiological analysis
43085676.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Phosphorus concentration from low-phosphorus wastewater using embedded phosphorus removal biofillers coupled with anaerobic cyclic phosphorus release: performance evaluation and microbiological analysis», no contexto de Polifosfato Inorgânico & Acidocalcisomas.
43085676.resumo_original: To achieve high-concentration phosphorus (P) enrichment at low influent PO43--P concentrations while minimizing carbon source consumption, a reactor with embedded phosphorus removal biofillers (EBPAOs) was constructed in this study. Batch experiments were conducted to investigate the effect of the high-P solution formed by multiple anaerobic enrichment cycles on P release by EBPAOs. When the PO43--P concentration in the anaerobic P release liquid was below 200 mg/L, P release by EBPAOs was unaffected. As the PO43--P concentration increased, P release was gradually inhibited and nearly ceased at 400 mg/L. This is because the high P concentration weakened the transmembrane gradient of orthophosphate (ortho-P) and impeded its efflux, whereas the hydrolysis of intracellular polyphosphate (poly-P) remained unaffected. Under the coupled operation of aerobic continuous feeding (influent PO43--P 4 mg/L) and anaerobic P release cycling, the anaerobic phosphorus concentrate liquid (PCL) concentration reached 232.66 ± 1.20 mg/L after 13 cycles, achieving a concentration factor of 58.17, while the aerobic effluent PO43--P concentration was only 0.14 ± 0.06 mg/L. The relative abundance of Candidatus_Accumulibacter increased from 53.29% to 67.08%. Genes related to the pentose phosphate pathway were downregulated, whereas those related to the Embden-Meyerhof-Parnas pathway, polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) synthesis, and the tricarboxylic acid cycle were upregulated, enhancing PHA synthesis and adequate ATP supply. The ratio of anaerobic COD consumption to anaerobic P release (CODup/Prel) was 3.28 ± 0.03. These results indicate that this technology can achieve efficient P enrichment and stable P discharge control in low-P wastewater.

43084581.titulo: Effect of metformin on HIV reservoir, inflammation and cell differentiation in non-diabetic older people with HIV: a two-year placebo-controlled pilot trial (Metforaging)
43084581.autores: Gutiérrez-García L, Esteban-Cantos A, … Arribas JR (17 autores)
43084581.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Effect of metformin on HIV reservoir, inflammation and cell differentiation in non-diabetic older people with HIV: a two-year placebo-controlled pilot trial (Metforaging)», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43084581.resumo_original:
People with HIV (PWH) on long-term antiretroviral therapy (ART) exhibit persistent inflammation, immune activation, and a stable HIV reservoir, contributing to non-AIDS age-related comorbidities. Metformin, an indirect mTOR inhibitor with immunometabolic properties, is a candidate geroprotective agent. We assessed its long-term immunological and virological impact in non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥50 years.
Metforaging is a phase II, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in which 35 non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥ 50 years received metformin or placebo for 96 weeks. At baseline and week 96, we quantified blood T-cell, monocyte, B-cell and NK subsets, inflammation and immune checkpoint biomarkers, total HIV DNA, intact/defective proviruses, and cell-associated HIV RNA (CA-RNA). Between-group effects were estimated by baseline-adjusted ANCOVA.
At week 96, CD8+ TEMRA T cells increased with placebo but remained stable under metformin (adjusted mean difference -5.2%, 95% CI -8.5 to -2.0; p=0.003), with a modest increase in CD8+ effector memory T cells (p=0.044). No between-group differences were detected in soluble inflammation or immune checkpoint biomarkers, immune checkpoint mRNA expression, or HIV reservoir markers (total HIV DNA, intact and defective proviruses, CA-RNA).
In non-diabetic ART-suppressed PWH ≥50 years, 96 weeks of metformin appeared to attenuate CD8+ T-cell terminal differentiation with no between-group differences detected in systemic inflammation or the HIV reservoir. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant confirmation in larger, adequately powered trials.

43084128.titulo: Same cell or separate sections? Cross-method identity evidence in the telocyte and Cajal-like cell literature: a sampled meta-research survey
43084128.autores: Tudose RC, Varga I, … Rusu MC (3 autores)
43084128.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Same cell or separate sections? Cross-method identity evidence in the telocyte and Cajal-like cell literature: a sampled meta-research survey», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43084128.resumo_original: Telocytes and Cajal-like cells are identified by telopode ultrastructure or by markers and genetic labels read at light-microscope resolution; these identifications are equivalent only when they are joined in the same cell. We measured how often they join. From a metadata-defined frame of 908 records, a method-enriched census of the 18 whose abstracts declared an immunoelectron, correlative or volume-electron method and an equal-probability sample of 100 of the other 890 (87 obtained) were charted independently by two readers, the census by three. Each method-pair identity claim was classified as direct (same cell), population-level, inferred or unsupported. Readers mainly disagreed on immunolabelled cells showing the characteristic shape: depending on the reader, 25.6% or 55.3% of sampled papers reached a same-cell link. Because the marker draws the outline against which the shape is read, a post hoc rule set that pairing aside as co-registered but not independent, leaving 10.3% (8/78) and 15.8% (12/76; kappa, 0.54 between readings). At most two sampled papers made such a link at electron-microscope resolution and at most four reported numerical apertures; none of the 25 and 24 links pairing electron microscopy with light-level immunolabelling was direct; we found no extractable marker-versus-ultrastructure performance estimate among the charted papers. Seven census papers reached a direct electron-resolution link in the adopted file, four by immunoelectron labelling, so the link is technically feasible. In the sample, the bridge that makes a marker-defined population ultrastructurally defined was almost never built; reports should state the material pairing, the optics and the cell-level evidence.

43086511.titulo: Heterologous expression of recombinant dengue virus C-prM-E structural antigens from all four serotypes in the red microalga Porphyridium purpureum
43086511.autores: Utomo DIS, Bayu A, … Putra MY (9 autores)
43086511.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Heterologous expression of recombinant dengue virus C-prM-E structural antigens from all four serotypes in the red microalga Porphyridium purpureum», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43086511.resumo_original: The dengue virus (DENV) remains a significant global health threat, and the currently available vaccines exhibit concerns regarding safety, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness. Microalgae represent an innovative method for producing proteins that do not occur naturally. They are Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS), easily scalable, and capable of inducing post-translational modifications in eukaryotes. This study illustrates the effective heterologous expression of recombinant dengue virus capsid-premembrane-envelope (C-prM-E) structural antigen constructs representing all four DENV serotypes (DV1-DV4) in the red microalga Porphyridium purpureum through Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated transformation. Gene constructs containing capsid-premembrane-envelope (CprME) polyprotein fragments with C-terminal epitope tags were cloned into pCAMBIA1301 vectors and subsequently introduced into P. purpureum. PCR amplification confirmed the successful chromosomal integration of all four serotype constructs, yielding the anticipated 2.5-kb amplicons. The SDS-PAGE analysis revealed protein bands at around 85 kDa, consistent with the expected molecular weight of the processed CprME-derived proteins. We employed both anti-DENV-2 and anti-FLAG antibodies in a western blot assay to demonstrate that the recombinant antigens were identical and interacted with the immune system across all serotypes. These findings indicate that P. purpureum is an effective system for expressing DENV antigens, paving the path for the development of cost-effective, plant-derived dengue vaccine candidates. This microalgal platform may facilitate the large-scale production of tetravalent dengue vaccines, particularly in regions where dengue is prevalent and resources are scarce.

43093565.titulo: Mussel Biodeposits as a Qualitative Sentinel Proxy for Environmental Plastic Contamination in Freshwater Ecosystems
43093565.autores: Schirinzi GF, Geneselli I, … Ponti J (5 autores)
43093565.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Mussel Biodeposits as a Qualitative Sentinel Proxy for Environmental Plastic Contamination in Freshwater Ecosystems», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43093565.resumo_original: The identification of plastic particles below 10 µm in the environment is a challenge. Freshwater molluscs, widely used as model organisms for biomonitoring of water pollution, are able to filtrate large volume of water and naturally concentrate contaminants in their excretions. Based on this observation, this work aims to describe a method to collect and detect smaller plastic particles in feces and pseudofeces after animals' exposure to polyethylene terephthalate micro/nanoparticles, expected to be present in the environment at the end of its uncontrolled life cycle. Our findings, mainly based on Raman spectroscopy for polymer identification and electron microscopy, can be considered a qualitative to semi-quantitative proof of concept that can be further developed to build up a new system to collect plastics using molluscs, naturally exposed to environmental contaminants, without sacrificing them. In addition, the use of feces and pseudofeces of filtering organisms could be the solution to concentrate environmental plastics and confirm their presence.
