43095401.titulo: Potential roles of soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise in modulating the oral microbiome-host axis in obesity and diabetes: microbial dysbiosis, inflammation, and immunometabolic signaling
43095401.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Potential roles of soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise in modulating the oral microbiome-host axis in obesity and diabetes: microbial dysbiosis, inflammation, and immunometabolic signaling», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43095401.resumo_original: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are complex metabolic disorders increasingly associated with alterations in the oral microbiome, chronic low-grade inflammation, dysregulated immunometabolic signaling, and systemic metabolic dysfunction. Although regular exercise is a cornerstone intervention for improving metabolic health, interindividual variability in exercise responsiveness has prompted interest in complementary nutritional strategies. Emerging evidence suggests that soy proteins and soy-derived isoflavones may influence metabolic and immune pathways relevant to exercise adaptation, potentially involving microbial and host-mediated mechanisms. This narrative review synthesizes current experimental and clinical evidence regarding the potential roles of soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise in modulating the oral microbiome-host axis in obesity and diabetes. Particular attention is given to oral microbial dysbiosis, microbial metabolites, inflammatory and immune signaling, insulin resistance, glucose and lipid metabolism, vascular dysfunction, and systemic immunometabolic responses. We distinguish direct evidence from the oral microbiome from indirect evidence derived from the gut microbiome, systemic metabolic studies, and preclinical models. Although some findings suggest convergence of soy-derived bioactives and exercise on overlapping microbial and host pathways, such convergence should not be interpreted as experimentally established synergy. The potential contribution of microbial biotransformation of soy isoflavones and subsequent microbial-host interactions is also considered as an emerging, but incompletely characterized, mechanism linking dietary bioactives with systemic metabolic health. Overall, the available evidence supports a hypothesis-generating framework in which soy proteins, isoflavones, and exercise may contribute to complementary modulation of microbial ecology and host immunometabolic signaling; however, direct human evidence linking these interventions to oral microbiome changes remains extremely limited. Most mechanistic evidence derives from gut microbiome research, systemic metabolic outcomes, and preclinical models and therefore cannot be directly extrapolated to the oral microbiome-host axis. Further well-controlled human studies are needed to determine whether combined soy and exercise interventions can reproducibly modify oral microbial communities and whether such changes are associated with clinically meaningful metabolic outcomes in obesity and T2DM.

43093804.titulo: An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment
43093804.autores: Othayoth J, Bist JS, … Bist P (3 autores)
43093804.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «An Atlas of Antiviral Therapeutic Outcomes: How Viral Biology Shapes the Reach of Treatment», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43093804.resumo_original: Antiviral inhibition does not produce a single therapeutic endpoint: some infections can be cured after finite treatment, others require durable suppression, and others remain difficult to influence because the actionable phase is brief or anatomically inaccessible. These different outcomes reflect the biological state that preserves infection or permits return, the time during which a drug-sensitive process remains causally important, the anatomical space in which consequential virus or viral material resides, and the capacity of viral populations to evolve under therapeutic pressure. Here, we examine these relationships across curable, suppressible, latent, acute, neuroinvasive, and post-acute viral infections. Comparisons among HCV, HIV-1, HBV, HSV, influenza, RSV, dengue, SARS-CoV-2, Ebola virus, CHIKV, and other systems show how persistence architecture, diagnostic timing, tissue pharmacology, host context, and resistance can determine whether antiviral activity translates into virological cure, durable suppression, recurrence control, prevention, or incomplete therapeutic control. Human challenge studies, clinical programs with discordant outcomes, and resistance studies further illustrate where mechanistic activity and therapeutic sufficiency diverge. Across these examples, antiviral outcome depends ultimately on whether treatment can intercept the biological state that determines the subsequent fate of infection.

43077757.titulo: Nanotechnology-enabled modulation of immune cell ferroptosis for empowering cancer immunotherapy
43077757.autores: Zhou T, Guo S, … Li M (5 autores)
43077757.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Nanotechnology-enabled modulation of immune cell ferroptosis for empowering cancer immunotherapy», no contexto de Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor.
43077757.resumo_original: Ferroptosis has emerged as a promising strategy to overcome therapy resistance and reshape the tumor-immune microenvironment. Beyond direct tumor killing capabilities, ferroptosis functions as a context-dependent immunometabolic regulator, capable of enhancing antitumor immunity through immunogenic cell death while also impairing immune effector functions under excessive oxidative stress. However, research has predominantly centered on tumor-cell ferroptosis, while its roles in regulating the fate and function of key immune cells remain less explored, including tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), dendritic cells (DCs), T cells, and natural killer (NK) cells. Here, we review recent advances in nanomaterial-enabled ferroptosis regulation that enable coordinated modulation across tumor and immune compartments. We emphasize the coordinated roles of lipid metabolic reprogramming and iron homeostasis in establishing cell-type-specific susceptibility to ferroptosis, thereby contributing to heterogeneous immune responses within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Drawing on recent evidence of the context-dependent effects of nanomaterial-mediated ferroptosis on immune responses, we critically discuss material design strategies that enable cell-selective targeting and spatiotemporal control, aiming to promoting ferroptosis in tumor and immunosuppressive cells while protecting antitumor immune cells. Collectively, this review establishes a mechanistic framework connecting immune-cell ferroptosis with nanomedicine design and highlights key directions for developing more precise and durable ferroptosis-based cancer immunotherapies.

43092355.titulo: Short-Term Climate Variability and Its Association with Dengue Transmission in the Southern United States
43092355.autores: Bowles T, Deshpande G, … Oni T (4 autores)
43092355.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Short-Term Climate Variability and Its Association with Dengue Transmission in the Southern United States», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43092355.resumo_original: Dengue fever has re-emerged in parts of the Southern United States (U.S.), raising concerns about how short-term climate variability may influence transmission risk. This ecological study evaluates whether changes in mean annual temperature and total annual precipitation between 2020 and 2024 were associated with shifts in dengue incidence across seven Southern U.S. states. Dengue case data were obtained from CDC ArboNET, and climate data from NOAA monitoring systems. Incidence rates were standardized using U.S. Census population estimates, and associations were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation and longitudinal mixed-effects models. All study states experienced increases in mean annual temperature over the five-year period, while precipitation patterns varied. Dengue incidence rose across all states, with Florida showing the most substantial increase. Moderate correlations were observed between temperature change and dengue incidence (rs = 0.54) and between precipitation change and dengue incidence (rs = 0.71), though neither reached statistical significance. Longitudinal mixed-effects models identified a statistically significant positive association between temperature and both cumulative incidence and locally acquired incidence. These findings suggest that modest short-term climate shifts may be associated with variations in dengue dynamics in the Southern U.S., underscoring the need for expanded surveillance and longer-term analyses to better characterize these emerging vector-borne disease risks.

43094462.titulo: A genomic toolkit for surveillance and elimination of the principal malaria vectors in Southeast Asia
43094462.autores: Dennis TPW, Vantaux A, … St Laurent B (17 autores)
43094462.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «A genomic toolkit for surveillance and elimination of the principal malaria vectors in Southeast Asia», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43094462.resumo_original: While substantial progress has been made toward malaria elimination in Southeast Asia, major challenges remain. The principal mosquito vectors, Anopheles dirus and Anopheles minimus, inhabit diverse ecological niches and exhibit a wide range of behavioural and physiological insecticide resistance phenotypes, complicating vector control efforts. In Africa, genomic surveillance has transformed our understanding of vector evolution and resistance, supported by open-access tools and data. Comparable resources for Southeast Asian vectors remain limited. Here, we release Adir1.0, a curated, analysis-ready catalog of 540 An. dirus whole-genome sequences, accessible for interactive cloud-based analysis via the malariagen-data-python application programming interface (API). Alongside, we provide an updated Amin1.0 API to enhance functionality and usability, enabling integrated analyses across historical and new datasets. We demonstrate these resources by performing the first exploratory population genomic analysis of An. dirus from Bangladesh, Thailand, and Cambodia, revealing population structure, candidate regions of physiological resistance, and genomic structural variation. Together, these resources provide a foundation for genomic surveillance studies to inform vector control and malaria elimination strategies in Southeast Asia.

43092558.titulo: Expanding Kelch13 Artemisinin Resistance Markers Are Associated with Higher Malaria Incidence in Uganda
43092558.autores: van Wyk S, Gwasupika J, … Barnes KI (8 autores)
43092558.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Expanding Kelch13 Artemisinin Resistance Markers Are Associated with Higher Malaria Incidence in Uganda», no contexto de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão.
43092558.resumo_original: Artemisinin partial resistance (ART-R)-associated Plasmodium falciparum Kelch13 mutations are expanding across Africa. However, their population-level consequences remain poorly understood, particularly in settings of moderate-to-high malaria transmission. We investigated associations between Kelch13 and partner drug mutation prevalence and monthly confirmed malaria incidence across 16 Ugandan districts from 2017 to 2022, using integrated molecular, epidemiological, climatic, malaria-control, and antimalarial resistance data and negative binomial regression. Combined prevalence of WHO-validated and candidate Kelch13 mutations increased over the study period. Each 10-percentage-point increase in Kelch13 prevalence was associated with a 13.1% higher incidence after multivariable adjustment (aIRR, 1.131; 95% CI, 1.090-1.174). Furthermore, each 10-percentage-point increase in pfcrt K76T prevalence was associated with a 24.2% higher malaria incidence. As expected, ITN distribution ≥ 80%, IRS coverage ≥ 90%, and higher altitude were associated with lower incidence, whereas temperatures of 25-30 °C, relative humidity of 60-80%, and higher precipitation were associated with higher incidence. The persistence of these associations after adjustment suggests that expanding ART-R-associated parasite populations are independently associated with malaria incidence. The relationship may be bidirectional. These findings support interpreting ART-R within its ecological and intervention context and integrating molecular, epidemiological, and malaria-control surveillance to safeguard antimalarial efficacy.

43090536.titulo: Development of a Calreticulin-Based Endogenous Control for Use in Culex restuans RT-qPCR Assays in Massachusetts
43090536.autores: Stamborski N, Rich CM, … Rich SM (6 autores)
43090536.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Development of a Calreticulin-Based Endogenous Control for Use in Culex restuans RT-qPCR Assays in Massachusetts», no contexto de Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi.
43090536.resumo_original: Hematophagous arthropods and associated pathogens are becoming more prevalent globally. With limited treatment options, prevention is the top priority to reduce disease. Reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) has emerged as a standard detection method for many laboratories, but it has several drawbacks. Degraded sample quality, failed RNA preparations, and the presence of reaction inhibitors can lead to false negative results, introducing the need for a positive control. Existing control methods rely on adding exogenous nucleotides during amplification reactions, which may not reflect the quality of the sample. Incorporating assays to detect endogenous mosquito mRNA transcripts provides assurance that sample quality is sufficient for the downstream amplification of pathogen RNA. In the present study, we applied the Rapid Amplification of cDNA Ends (RACE) technique to obtain a full-length calreticulin cDNA sequence from the Culex restuans mosquito, collected in Massachusetts, USA. We then used the newly discovered cDNA sequence to design primers and probes spanning the first exon-exon junction of the calreticulin gene, which allowed for specific and accurate RNA transcript detection in an RT-qPCR assay. This assay detected the presence of calreticulin transcripts in extracted pools of mosquito RNA. This approach may be further developed to include other relevant mosquito species and, with extensive validation, may have potential for use as an endogenous control in arbovirus surveillance.

43095601.titulo: Caffeine Prolongs Survivability and Significantly Modulates Cytokine Levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-18 and IL-10 in Plasmodium berghei ANKA-infected ICR Mice
43095601.autores: Noriman AZ, Mohd Abdul Razak MR, … Hassan WRM (6 autores)
43095601.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Caffeine Prolongs Survivability and Significantly Modulates Cytokine Levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-18 and IL-10 in Plasmodium berghei ANKA-infected ICR Mice», no contexto de Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação.
43095601.resumo_original: Caffeine, a bioactive compound in Theobroma cacao, exhibits various pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory properties. Malaria is an inflammatory-related disease caused by Plasmodium spp. Severe infection of this disease can cause cerebral malaria, which is characterised by neuroinflammation. An in vitro study of caffeine suggested that it possesses anti-malarial properties. However, caffeine's potential in both anti-malarial and cytokine-modulating properties through in vivo have yet to be explored. This study investigated the anti-malarial and cytokine-modulating effects of caffeine in P. berghei ANKA-infected ICR mice. Anti-malarial activity of caffeine at 5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg body weight was given via intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection, and the chemosuppressive percentage (percentage of parasitaemia inhibition) was calculated based on Peter and Robinsons's study in 1992. In addition, the cytokine-modulating effect was determined using the ELISA method. Chemosuppressive test at 5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg and 20 mg/kg b.w. of caffeine in the P. berghei ANKA-infected ICR mice exhibited 64.18 ± 9.17, 39.93 ± 5.63 and 21.86 ± 5.57%, respectively. Notably, the lowest concentration, 5 mg/kg b.w. of caffeine was able to prolong significantly (p < 0.05) the survivability of malaria-infected ICR mice for 17 days as compared to infected mice (12 days). This effective dose of caffeine revealed a significant reduction in cytokine levels of TNF-α, IFN-γ, IL-18 and IL-10 by 1.08-, 1.12-, 1.12- and 1.15-folds, respectively, as compared to malaria-infected mice. Collectively, 5 mg/kg b.w. of caffeine exhibited good chemosuppressive, modulated levels of inflammatory cytokines and prolonged survivability of P. berghei ANKA-infected ICR mice. Hence, caffeine can be a plausible candidate for the development of anti-malarial therapeutic drugs.

43090502.titulo: Genome-Wide Characterization of ABCG Transporters Involved in Anthranilic Diamide Insecticide Tolerance in Spodoptera exigua (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)
43090502.autores: You C, Duan R, … Ji X (8 autores)
43090502.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Genome-Wide Characterization of ABCG Transporters Involved in Anthranilic Diamide Insecticide Tolerance in Spodoptera exigua (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae)», no contexto de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas.
43090502.resumo_original: The beet armyworm, Spodoptera exigua (Hübner), has developed pronounced resistance to nearly all major classes of insecticides, posing a persistent threat to global agricultural productivity. The ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters, particularly members of the G subfamily, mediate the transmembrane efflux of xenobiotics and are increasingly implicated in insecticide tolerance, but the functional roles of the ABCG subfamily in S. exigua remain poorly understood. In this study, we identified 17 SeABCG genes and systematically characterized their spatiotemporal expression patterns and insecticide-responsive profiles. Most SeABCGs were broadly expressed across developmental stages and tissues, although with notable quantitative variation. Among the insecticide-responsive candidates, SeABCG3, SeABCG8, and SeABCG10 were significantly upregulated after treatment with cyantraniliprole and chlorantraniliprole and were highly expressed in detoxification tissues; these three genes were therefore selected for functional studies. Functional characterization through RNAi confirmed that SeABCG3, SeABCG8, and SeABCG10 contribute to tolerance against cyantraniliprole and chlorantraniliprole. Furthermore, molecular docking results revealed that SeABCG3, SeABCG8, and SeABCG10 exhibit potential binding affinity for both cyantraniliprole and chlorantraniliprole. These findings provide the first functional characterization of ABCG transporters in S. exigua and identify SeABCGs as crucial factors contributing to tolerance to anthranilic diamide insecticides.

43093725.titulo: Visualizing Disintegration Pathways of Orally Disintegrating Tablets in Water and Thickened Media Using Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-Ray CT
43093725.autores: Noji M, Fujita Y, … Harada T (6 autores)
43093725.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Visualizing Disintegration Pathways of Orally Disintegrating Tablets in Water and Thickened Media Using Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-Ray CT», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43093725.resumo_original: Background/Objectives: Orally disintegrating tablets (ODTs) are often used for patients with dysphagia; however, their co-administration with "thickened water" in clinical settings can delay disintegration and potentially reduce therapeutic efficacy. While wicking networks formed by superdisintegrants facilitate rapid disintegration, we hypothesized that viscous polymers in thickened water cause "pore clogging" within these networks. Although conventional macroscopic evaluations have demonstrated this delay, direct visualization of the underlying microstructural changes remains unexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to elucidate the microstructural mechanisms of disintegration delay. Methods: Simplified model ODTs containing either a wicking-type (crospovidone [CP]) or a swelling-type (sodium starch glycolate [SSG]) disintegrant were prepared. Their microstructures and disintegration behaviors were evaluated by cryogenic focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (Cryo-FIB-SEM), three-dimensional (3D) X-ray computed tomography (CT), and disintegration tests under simulated gastric conditions (pH 1.2). Results: Cryo-FIB-SEM revealed that CP-containing tablets formed numerous channel-like pores that promoted capillary action upon contact with water, whereas SSG-containing tablets formed larger, isolated macropores. X-ray CT analysis demonstrated distinct low-density regions associated with penetration-induced structural changes in both formulations. In CP-containing tablets, these regions extended throughout the channel network, whereas in SSG-containing tablets they were largely confined to the tablet surface. Consequently, the disintegration of CP-containing tablets in simulated gastric fluid was significantly delayed compared to that of SSG-containing tablets. Conclusions: The findings are consistent with a pore-clogging mechanism in which penetration of a viscous medium interferes with the liquid transport pathways responsible for rapid tablet disintegration. Combined Cryo-FIB-SEM and X-ray CT imaging provided direct morphological evidence of disintegrant-dependent structural responses in viscous media and offers a new framework for mechanistic investigation of tablet disintegration processes.

43090552.titulo: Transient Suppression of Head CYP9Q3 Transcripts Is Associated with Thiacloprid and Tau-Fluvalinate Susceptibility in Apis mellifera
43090552.autores: Katsavou E, Vlogiannitis S, … Vontas J (12 autores)
43090552.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Transient Suppression of Head CYP9Q3 Transcripts Is Associated with Thiacloprid and Tau-Fluvalinate Susceptibility in Apis mellifera», no contexto de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem.
43090552.resumo_original: Neonicotinoid toxicity to honeybees varies among active ingredients, with the insects being tolerant to thiacloprid but sensitive to imidacloprid. The selective toxicity has been hypothesized to be due to differences in metabolic detoxification by cytochrome P450s. In vitro experiments revealed that CYP9Q3 efficiently metabolises thiacloprid but not imidacloprid, consistent with the toxicity data. Honeybee tolerance to tau-fluvalinate, a pyrethroid acaricide used against Varroa destructor, has also been linked to P450-mediated detoxification. To address the role of CYP9Q3 in vivo in Apis mellifera, we used an RNA interference approach based on double-stranded RNA delivery through the median ocellus of adults to transiently suppress expression of CYP9Q3 in the head. Following confirmation of CYP9Q3 suppression by qPCR, fixed-dose topical bioassays were conducted with the neonicotinoids imidacloprid and thiacloprid and the pyrethroid tau-fluvalinate. Suppression of CYP9Q3 was associated with increased mortality following exposure to thiacloprid and tau-fluvalinate, whereas no increase was observed with imidacloprid. These findings provide in vivo functional evidence supporting the role of CYP9Q3 in honeybee tolerance to thiacloprid and tau-fluvalinate. The RNAi approach offers a valuable tool for investigating the functions of cytochrome P450 enzymes and other genes expressed in the honey bee head that are involved in insecticide susceptibility.

43090026.titulo: Intrinsic Variations in Stress Resistance and Host-Microbiome Interactions Influence Neurodegenerative Disease-Associated Phenotypes in Drosophila Models
43090026.autores: Yue X, Dulac A, … Birman S (5 autores)
43090026.resumo: Variação intrínseca de resistência ao estresse e interações hospedeiro–microbioma modulam fenótipos de neurodegeneração em Drosophila. (resumo a partir do título; abstract não lido)
43090026.resumo_original: Drosophila is widely used to model human diseases, including metabolic and neurological disorders such as Parkinson's disease (PD). Disease-induced changes in locomotion and stress resistance are typically assessed against healthy control flies, such as the white-eyed strain w1118, used as a reference for normal physiology and behavior. We compared two independent w1118 lines and found striking differences in their susceptibility to oxidative stress induced by the PD risk factor paraquat and nutrient starvation. Axenic rearing increased oxidative stress resistance in the susceptible line but not the resistant one, without affecting starvation resistance. We found that the stress-sensitive line had higher levels of Clostridiales bacteria and the endosymbiont Wolbachia in its gut microbiota and lower immune effector expression (antimicrobial peptides, lysozymes) in the head and gut. In a genetic PD model, the stress-resistant background strongly attenuated the locomotor defects mediated by the pan-neuronal expression of human mutant α-synuclein but not when expression was restricted to the dopaminergic neurons of the protocerebral anterior medial (PAM) cluster. These findings implicate the microbiome and immune effectors as modifiers of PD penetrance and suggest that accounting for such hidden variability could increase consistency in neurodegenerative disease modeling in Drosophila.

43092405.titulo: Lachnospiraceae and the Host Immune System: Mechanisms, Disease Associations and Precision-Oriented Intervention
43092405.autores: Mao D, Yang Q, … Ji H (8 autores)
43092405.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Lachnospiraceae and the Host Immune System: Mechanisms, Disease Associations and Precision-Oriented Intervention», no contexto de Vigilância Bibliográfica Geral.
43092405.resumo_original: The family Lachnospiraceae is among the most abundant obligately anaerobic taxa in the healthy human gut. Its core function-fermentation of dietary fibre to produce short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), chiefly butyrate-makes it a key node linking diet, the microbiota and host immunity. Altered Lachnospiraceae abundance is associated with inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer and autoimmune conditions, but the underlying molecular layers, causal structure and intra-family heterogeneity have yet to be integrated. This review addresses a single question: how do Lachnospiraceae shape and constrain host immunity? It first summarises the family's taxonomy, metabolism and ecology, and then examines the relevant mechanisms along four partly overlapping axes of immune crosstalk: the mucosal barrier and epithelial innate immunity, metabolite-mediated immune signalling, immune sensing of bacterial structural components and the shaping of adaptive immunity, together with a fifth, prospective and still exploratory layer of immune tolerance and trained immunity, which is presented as an open question rather than as an established mechanism. Four features distinguish this review from earlier overviews of the family: an explicit evidence hierarchy applied claim by claim; strict separation of findings obtained for Lachnospiraceae from those obtained for related taxa; explicit grading of intervention studies according to whether the family was manipulated, depleted or merely measured; and restriction of the trained-immunity layer to an open question. Associations with immune-related diseases are then assessed by disease category, followed by culturomics, genetic tools, live biotherapeutic products (LBPs) and polysaccharide-based, precision-oriented interventions. The central conclusion is that the immunological effects of Lachnospiraceae are strongly strain-specific and disease-context-dependent; family-level associations therefore cannot be extrapolated directly to strain-level causal effects.

43080508.titulo: Amino acid metabolic checkpoints in microglia: emerging regulators of Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis
43080508.autores: Xu F, Li H, … Zhang M (3 autores)
43080508.resumo: Estudo voltado à caracterização mecanística e funcional abordada em «Amino acid metabolic checkpoints in microglia: emerging regulators of Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis», no contexto de Vigilância Bibliográfica Geral.
43080508.resumo_original: Microglial immunometabolic reprogramming is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but amino acid metabolism has received less integrated attention than glucose and lipid metabolism. This Mini Review examines tryptophan-kynurenine, arginine, and glutamine pathways because they connect amino acid flux or amino acid-derived metabolites with microglial redox control, inflammatory signaling, mitochondrial function, and amyloid handling. We use the term amino acid metabolic checkpoints narrowly for a molecular regulatory node that has a demonstrable link to amino acid availability, transport, metabolic flux, or an amino acid-derived ligand and whose perturbation changes a defined microglial function. Broad domains such as mitochondrial fitness and phagolysosomal competence are treated as functional outputs rather than checkpoints. The glutamine-NLRP3 literature illustrates why directionality and experimental context are essential: glutaminase inhibition can promote mitophagy and suppress NLRP3 activation, whereas NLRP3 loss or chronic pharmacological inhibition increases glutamine/glutamate-related metabolism, mitochondrial activity, and Aβ clearance. These findings support bidirectional coupling rather than a simple model in which glutaminolysis is uniformly pathogenic. Evidence for tryptophan- and arginine-related nodes is biologically compelling but more heterogeneous in cell type and disease context. A checkpoint framework that explicitly grades direct versus indirect evidence may therefore help prioritize cell- and stage-specific immunometabolic intervention in AD.

43077510.titulo: Immunometabolic basis of glutamine supplementation as a potential host-directed therapy for tuberculosis.
43077510.autores: Jiang Q, Dikdan RJ, … Shi L (14 autores)
43077510.revista: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
43077510.resumo: Em camundongos com TB, metabolômica dirigida e transcriptoma mostram que o controle agudo vem com ativação de mTORC1, glutaminólise, glicólise e metabolismo de arginina e serina; a infecção crônica reduz mTORC1, aumenta o catabolismo de BCAA e baixa a glutamina. Glutamina oral restaurou aminoácidos pulmonares, reforçou mTORC1 e reduziu moderadamente carga bacteriana e lesão; dados humanos reanalisados mostram queda de glutamina circulante na progressão.
43077510.resumo_original: Undernutrition is the leading risk factor for tuberculosis susceptibility, severity, and poor treatment outcome. Nutritional immunology and immunometabolism frame how nutrient availability and metabolism shape host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) infection. By integrating targeted metabolomics and transcriptional profiling in a murine tuberculosis model, we defined immunometabolic programs underlying the transition from acute to chronic infection. Immune control of Mtb during acute infection was accompanied by robust activation of immune and metabolic programs, including mTORC1-associated signaling, glutaminolysis, glycolysis, arginine metabolism, and serine one-carbon metabolism, thereby highlighting the importance of amino acid metabolism and mitochondrial function in antimicrobial immunity. In contrast, chronic infection was characterized by reduced immune activation and mTORC1-associated signaling, increased branched-chain amino acid catabolism, and altered amino acid profiles, with leucine and glutamine among the discriminating metabolites. These findings suggest that reduced glutamine availability during chronic infection may increase reliance on leucine oxidative catabolism to sustain mitochondrial metabolism during nutrient stress, potentially limiting leucine availability for mTORC1-associated anabolic metabolism and immune activation. Oral glutamine supplementation restored amino acid homeostasis, including lung leucine abundance, enhanced mTORC1-associated signaling and central metabolic programs, moderately reduced bacterial burden and lung pathology, and mitigated infection-associated wasting. Reanalysis of published human metabolomics datasets further demonstrated reduced circulating glutamine levels during progression to active tuberculosis, supporting conservation of glutamine metabolic dysregulation across host species. Collectively, our findings identify a potential glutamine-leucine metabolic axis linking nutrient availability with immunometabolic competence and provide a mechanistic rationale for evaluating glutamine supplementation as a host-directed strategy for tuberculosis.

resumo_blocos.racional: A desnutrição figura como o principal fator de risco para suscetibilidade, gravidade clínica e desfecho terapêutico desfavorável na tuberculose (TB). Sob a ótica da imunologia nutricional e do imunometabolismo, os autores investigaram como a disponibilidade de aminoácidos e o metabolismo mitocondrial moldam a defesa do hospedeiro durante a transição da infecção aguda para a infecção crônica por Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Integração de metabolômica direcionada e perfilamento transcricional em modelo murino de tuberculose, comparando fases aguda e crônica da infecção. Realizaram suplementação oral de glutamina in vivo para avaliar homeostase de aminoácidos pulmonares, sinalização anabólica e desfechos microbiológicos, além da reanálise de conjuntos de dados metabolômicos humanos publicados durante a progressão para TB ativa.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O controle imune na fase aguda acompanhou-se de robusta ativação da sinalização associada a mTORC1, glutaminólise, glicólise, metabolismo de arginina e metabolismo de um carbono via serina. Na fase crônica, observaram-se queda na ativação imune e em mTORC1 e aumento do catabolismo de aminoácidos de cadeia ramificada, destacando leucina e glutamina como metabólitos discriminantes — sugerindo que a escassez de glutamina redireciona a leucina para oxidação mitocondrial e limita o anabolismo mediado por mTORC1. A suplementação oral de glutamina restaurou os níveis pulmonares de leucina, reativou mTORC1, reduziu moderadamente a carga bacteriana e a patologia pulmonar, mitigou a perda ponderal e refletiu a queda de glutamina circulante vista em coortes humanas.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Fornece um eixo mecanístico glutamina-leucina-mTORC1 diretamente transferível às investigações de imunometabolismo do hospedeiro no LUCHM, conectando restrição ou desbalanço nutricional à competência antimicrobiana e à preservação tecidual.

43063265.titulo: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
43063265.autores: Su T, Liu S, … Zhou ZH (5 autores)
43063265.resumo: Estrutura por crio-EM do complexo Saglin–SGS4 de Anopheles gambiae: SGS4 e SGS5 ligam Saglin e outras proteínas SG1 em extratos de glândula salivar; Saglin forma homodímero por coiled-coil e pontes dissulfeto.
43063265.resumo_original: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

resumo_blocos.racional: A transmissão bem-sucedida da malária por mosquitos Anopheles exige o desenvolvimento do Plasmodium no intestino médio seguido pela invasão das glândulas salivares pelos esporozoítos. Embora proteínas salivares como Saglin e as proteínas de superfície de glândula salivar SGS4 e SGS5 já fossem implicadas nessa etapa, a ausência completa de estruturas tridimensionais nativas impedia decifrar a mecânica molecular dessa interação.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores realizaram fracionamento bioquímico e análises por espectrometria de massas diretamente a partir de extratos nativos de glândulas salivares de Anopheles gambiae para mapear parceiros de ligação endógenos. Em seguida, resolveram por criomicroscopia eletrônica (cryo-EM) a estrutura em alta resolução do complexo nativo Saglin-SGS4 e conduziram análises estruturais comparativas entre diferentes complexos da família SG1 (salivary gland 1) com proteínas SGS.
resumo_blocos.resultados: As análises proteômicas demonstraram que SGS4 e SGS5 de Anopheles gambiae associam-se diretamente a Saglin e a outros membros da família SG1 nos extratos salivares. A estrutura por cryo-EM revelou que a Saglin forma homodímeros estabilizados por interações coiled-coil e pontes dissulfeto, acoplando-se longitudinalmente à subunidade SGS4. A comparação entre complexos SG1-SGS evidenciou uma arquitetura conservada nas proteínas SG1 combinada à plasticidade conformacional das proteínas SGS para acomodar parceiros SG1 de comprimentos distintos.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Revela pela primeira vez a arquitetura molecular nativa de complexos proteicos da glândula salivar de Anopheles que facilitam a invasão por esporozoítos, fornecendo alvos estruturais precisos para estratégias de bloqueio de transmissão baseadas no vetor acompanhadas pelo programa de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium no LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Investigar por modelagem estrutural e imunomarcação se ortólogos de SG1 e SGS em Anopheles aquasalis conservam a interface coiled-coil/dissulfeto descrita para Saglin-SGS4 e se anticorpos dirigidos a essa fenda longitudinal reduzem a carga de esporozoítos salivares.

43072377.titulo: A gut-brain axis for aversive interoception drives innate and anticipatory emesis in Drosophila
43072377.autores: Karunakaran R, Choudhary P, … Das G (9 autores)
43072377.resumo: Em Drosophila, toxina ingerida lesa enterócitos do intestino médio, que geram ROS; o canal TrpA1 de células enteroendócrinas detecta o ROS e libera neuropeptídeos, que atuam em neurônios serotoninérgicos e dopaminérgicos e chegam aos corpos pedunculados. O circuito produz êmese inata e memória aversiva que antecipa a êmese.
43072377.resumo_original: The gut-brain pathways that transmit negative signals to the brain, influencing bodily functions and behavior, are not fully understood. We have identified a gut-brain axis in Drosophila that detects toxin-induced gut damage and triggers innate and learned, anticipatory emesis. Ingested toxins induce the midgut enterocytes to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). ROS are detected by TrpA1 channels in enteroendocrine cells, resulting in the release of neuropeptides that signal gastric malaise. We also find evidence for midgut and ROS-independent mechanisms of toxin detection. Gut-derived neuropeptides act on brain serotonergic and dopaminergic neurons, which then communicate with the brain's sensory integration and memory centers, the mushroom bodies (MBs). This circuit enables vomiting and facilitates the formation of aversive memories. We find that the persistent activity of dopaminergic neurons mediates aversive reinforcement. Such activity lends itself to pairing the gut-derived malaise signal with odor representations in the MBs, enabling the flies to learn that the paired odor predicts toxin ingestion and to exhibit anticipatory emesis. Many components of this interoceptive pathway are likely conserved, providing a genetic model for exploring how aversive gut-brain communication influences metabolism, feeding, stress responses, and neurodegeneration.

resumo_blocos.racional: Os circuitos enteroceptivos do eixo intestino-cérebro capazes de detectar dano epitelial agudo induzido por toxinas ingeridas e convertê-lo em respostas comportamentais defensivas imediatas e memória aversiva permaneciam pouco elucidados em insetos. O estudo buscou mapear como o estresse oxidativo intestinal se traduz em comando neuroendócrino central e aprendizado antecipatório.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Utilizando linhagens genéticas de Drosophila melanogaster submetidas à ingestão controlada de toxinas luminais, os autores combinaram ensaios comportamentais de êmese inata e condicionamento olfativo antecipatório com manipulação genética de enterócitos, células enteroendócrinas expressando canais TrpA1 e circuitos aminérgicos centrais. A sinalização de espécies reativas de oxigênio (ROS), liberação de neuropeptídeos intestinais e atividade persistente de neurônios serotonérgicos e dopaminérgicos conectados aos corpos pedunculados (mushroom bodies) foram dissecadas funcionalmente.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Toxinas ingeridas induzem enterócitos do intestino médio a produzir espécies reativas de oxigênio (ROS), que são detectadas por canais TrpA1 em células enteroendócrinas — paralelamente a vias independentes de ROS — disparando a secreção de neuropeptídeos sinalizadores de mal-estar gástrico. Esses neuropeptídeos ativam neurônios serotonérgicos e dopaminérgicos cerebrais projetados aos corpos pedunculados, promovendo êmese defensiva imediata. A atividade persistente dos neurônios dopaminérgicos atua como reforço aversivo que associa o sinal visceral a odores pareados, gerando êmese antecipatória aprendida.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta diretamente a geração de ROS por enterócitos no intestino médio à ativação de canais TrpA1 enteroendócrinos e sinalização neuropeptídica central, oferecendo um arcabouço mecanístico valioso para entender como o estresse oxidativo induzido por hemo e lipídios peroxidados no repasto HFHS altera o comportamento alimentar e pós-prandial em Aedes aegypti no LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Testar em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti se a sobrecarga de ROS intestinal após repasto com sangue HFHS ativa canais TrpA1 enteroendócrinos e modifica a resposta olfativa ou aversão alimentar em repastos subsequentes.

43078841.titulo: Increasing dengue outbreaks in temperate Brazil are associated with Aedes aegypti invasion and infestation levels.
43078841.autores: Bermann TL, Barbosa DAM, … da Luz Wallau G (30 autores)
43078841.resumo: Integra dados entomológicos, epidemiológicos e ambientais de 2015 a 2023 no Rio Grande do Sul com 665 novos genomas de DENV: Aedes aegypti se expandiu pelos municípios, quase metade superou 20 casos/100 mil hab. em 2023 e as linhagens virais persistem localmente entre anos, com duas regiões como polos de dispersão.
43078841.resumo_original: Dengue fever, caused by dengue virus (DENV), is one of the most significant mosquito-borne diseases globally, with increasing risk due to the expansion of Aedes vectors into subtropical and temperate zones. Brazil accounted for 70% of dengue cases reported worldwide in 2024, and the virus has recently become endemic in the southernmost state of Rio Grande do Sul. Here, we integrate entomological, epidemiological and environmental data and generate complementary genomic data to investigate DENV dynamics in Southern Brazil from 2015 to 2023. During this period, Aedes aegypti expanded across state municipalities, with a marked increase in dengue cases from 2020 onward. Nearly half of the municipalities surpassed the incidence threshold of ≥20 cases per 100,000 residents per year by 2023, indicating endemic transmission. Genomic analysis of 665 new DENV genomes is consistent with the local persistence of viral lineages across years, driving seasonal outbreaks. Moreover, Northwest and Metropolitan regions are identified as key hubs for viral spread within the Rio Grande do Sul state. These findings highlight the north-to-south expansion of dengue into temperate regions, emphasizing the urgent need for intensification of vector control and surveillance in newly endemic areas to mitigate dengue burden in a mostly naive human population.

resumo_blocos.racional: Em 2024, o Brasil concentrou 70% dos casos mundiais de dengue, com expansão alarmante do vírus da dengue (DENV) e de vetores Aedes para zonas subtropicais e temperadas, tornando a doença recentemente endêmica no Rio Grande do Sul. O estudo buscou reconstruir como a invasão e os níveis de infestação de Aedes aegypti impulsionaram a dinâmica epidemiológica e genômica da transmissão em clima temperado entre 2015 e 2023.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Integração de séries históricas entomológicas, epidemiológicas e ambientais do Rio Grande do Sul (2015–2023) combinada à geração e análise genômica de 665 novos genomas de DENV para rastrear persistência viral interanual e rotas de dispersão intermunicipal.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A expansão territorial de Aedes aegypti pelos municípios gaúchos foi acompanhada por acentuada escalada de casos a partir de 2020, levando quase metade dos municípios a ultrapassar o limiar de endemicidade de pelo menos 20 casos por 100.000 habitantes/ano em 2023. A análise filogenômica dos 665 genomas demonstrou persistência local contínua de linhagens virais ao longo de múltiplos anos sustentando surtos sazonais, identificando as regiões Noroeste e Metropolitana como principais polos de disseminação viral intraestadual em uma população humana majoritariamente naïf.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Contextualiza a expansão meridional de Aedes aegypti e da persistência endêmica de DENV no Brasil em áreas temperadas, reforçando a necessidade de correlacionar competência vetorial e tolerância térmica/metabólica em populações brasileiras acompanhadas pelo LUCHM.

43066088.titulo: Metabolic profiling of brain and cerebrospinal fluid in cerebral malaria
43066088.autores: Sachdeva C, Forster R, … Daily JP (12 autores)
43066088.resumo: Metabolômica não direcionada de cérebro de camundongos com malária cerebral experimental e de cérebro e LCR de crianças com CM e coma não malárico: ECM altera energia e aminoácidos (ácidos pipecólico e lático); cérebro humano CM×NMC difere pouco; ácido glicérico sobe no LCR de CM.
43066088.resumo_original: Cerebral malaria (CM), a severe neurological complication of Plasmodium falciparum infection, is a common cause of pediatric mortality and long-term cognitive impairment in endemic regions. The mechanisms driving CM-associated coma and neuropathology are not fully understood. We performed untargeted metabolomic profiling of brain tissue from experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) mouse models and brain autopsy tissue and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples from children with CM and non-malarial coma (NMC). ECM brain samples exhibited significant metabolic alterations, including differences in energy metabolism and amino acids and elevated pipecolic and lactic acids. In contrast, CM and NMC brain metabolomes showed limited differences. CSF metabolomes from cohorts in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Malawi showed elevated glyceric acid in CM compared with NMC. Together, these findings highlight metabolic perturbations in CM across species and sample types and identify glyceric acid as a potential CSF biomarker.

resumo_blocos.racional: A malária cerebral causada por Plasmodium falciparum permanece entre as principais causas de letalidade pediátrica e sequelas neurocognitivas duradouras, mas os distúrbios metabólicos neuroquímicos que sustentam o coma malárico em comparação a comas não maláricos e ao modelo murino ainda eram pouco caracterizados.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores executaram perfilamento metabolômico não direcionado (untargeted metabolomics) comparando parênquima cerebral de camundongos com malária cerebral experimental (ECM) frente a tecido cerebral de autópsia e amostras pareadas de líquido cefalorraquidiano (LCR) obtidas de coortes pediátricas com malária cerebral (CM) versus coma não malárico (NMC) na República Democrática do Congo e no Maláui.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O tecido cerebral murino na ECM apresentou remodelamento metabólico pronunciado em vias bioenergéticas e de aminoácidos, destacando-se o acúmulo significativo de ácido pipecólico e ácido lático. Em contraste, o metaboloma post-mortem do parênquima cerebral humano diferiu pouco entre CM e NMC, mas o metaboloma do líquor nas duas coortes africanas revelou elevação consistente de ácido glicérico nos pacientes com malária cerebral em relação ao coma não malárico.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece um mapa comparativo direto entre o modelo murino de malária cerebral experimental (como o sistema PbA/C57BL/6J operado no LUCHM) e a doença pediátrica humana, posicionando os ácidos pipecólico, lático e especialmente o ácido glicérico liquórico como marcadores translacionais de disfunção bioenergética e barreira hematoencefálica.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Dosar lactato, ácido pipecólico e ácido glicérico no córtex e no líquor cisternal de camundongos C57BL/6J infectados com PbA nos dias 4 a 6 pós-infecção, correlacionando seus níveis à quebra de claudina-5 e ativação microglial.

43063246.titulo: Biostable insect kinin mimetics in either blood or sugar meals deter feeding in the mosquito Aedes aegypti (L.)
43063246.resumo: Seis miméticos biostáveis de cinina reduzem o comportamento alimentar de fêmeas de Ae. aegypti; 1728, IK-Aib-19 e IK-Aib-20 cortam o volume de sangue ingerido em 95%, 51% e 63%; antagonista de receptor reverte parcialmente o efeito.
43063246.resumo_original: In insects, kinins (leucokinins) regulate diverse physiological processes. Previously we found kinin mimetic 1728 elicits aversive behavioral responses in Aedes aegypti female mosquitoes of flying-, walking- or jumping away when offered in sucrose. The feeding effects of six insect kinin analogues with different EC50 on the recombinant mosquito kinin receptor, and containing aminoisobutyric acid (Aib) (1728, 1729, IK-Aib-12, IK-Aib-19, and IK-Aib-20) or β3-Pro (1460) for increased biostability, were investigated when offered in sugar or blood meals. We used a high-resolution, high-throughput feeding behaviors analysis device, the flyPAD, adapted for mosquitoes. Analogues 1728, IK-Aib-19, and IK-Aib-20 (1 mM) decreased the feeding behaviors towards both meals resulting in a reduction in sucrose volume ingested of 95%, 92%, and 33%, respectively, and reduced the volume of blood ingested by 95, 51 and 63%, respectively. Analogue IK-Aib-12 reduced blood volume ingested by 78%, having no effect on feeding behaviors towards sugar. Mimetics1728 and 1729 (1 mM) reduced the feeding behaviors towards blood, and the blood volume ingested by 95% and 91%, respectively. Analogues modulated feeding behaviors by mainly reducing the number of sips, feeding bursts, and activity bouts. Analogue 1728 reduced sugar volume ingested by 95% and its aversive behavioral effects were partially reversed by co-administration of a synthetic small molecule kinin receptor antagonist (SACC-0048555) that we discovered, as expected. However, the sugar volume ingested was still reduced by 73%. Co-administration of 1728 with suramin, a G protein decoupler, in contrast, restored both normal feeding behaviors and volume ingested. These results agreed with our previous finding that 1728 directly shuts down the sugar sensory neuron in the labella signaling through the kinin receptor, a GPCR.

resumo_blocos.racional: As cininas de insetos (leucocininas) regulam balanço hidrossalino e comportamento alimentar via receptores acoplados à proteína G (GPCRs), mas peptídeos nativos sofrem degradação proteolítica rápida. O estudo avaliou se análogos sintéticos biostáveis de cinina adicionados a refeições açucaradas ou sanguíneas bloqueiam a ingestão em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Seis análogos biostáveis de cinina com diferentes valores de EC50 frente ao receptor recombinante de cinina de mosquito — contendo ácido aminoisobutírico (Aib: 1728, 1729, IK-Aib-12, IK-Aib-19 e IK-Aib-20) ou β3-prolina (1460) — foram ofertados a 1 mM em sacarose ou repasto sanguíneo para fêmeas de Aedes aegypti. A microestrutura fina da alimentação (número de goles/sips, rajadas de alimentação e surtos de atividade) foi quantificada na plataforma de alta resolução flyPAD adaptada para mosquitos, seguida de ensaios farmacológicos de resgate com o antagonista sintético SACC-0048555 e com suramina (desacoplador de proteína G).
resumo_blocos.resultados: A 1 mM, os análogos 1728, IK-Aib-19 e IK-Aib-20 reduziram o volume ingerido de sacarose em 95%, 92% e 33% e cortaram o volume de sangue ingerido em 95%, 51% e 63%, respectivamente, enquanto o análogo 1729 reduziu o repasto sanguíneo em 91% e o IK-Aib-12 inibiu seletivamente a ingestão de sangue em 78% sem afetar o açúcar. A inibição decorreu da queda acentuada no número de goles e rajadas alimentares. Enquanto o antagonista do receptor de cinina SACC-0048555 reverteu parcialmente a aversão ao 1728 (mantendo 73% de redução de volume), a co-administração com suramina restaurou integralmente o comportamento e o volume ingerido, confirmando silenciamento de neurônios gustativos da labela via GPCR.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Traz ferramentas farmacológicas seletivas (como IK-Aib-12, específico para repasto sanguíneo, e 1728/1729) e métricas comportamentais de alta resolução para dissecar regulação pós-ingestão e sinalização por leucocininas em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti no insetário do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Utilizar análogos seletivos da via de cininas ou modulação de Lkr para testar se o fracionamento forçado do volume de repasto sanguíneo atenua o pico de hemo livre e a peroxidação lipídica intestinal em Aedes alimentadas com sangue HFHS.

43062890.titulo: Blood-derived dietary protein promotes sleep in the mosquito Aedes aegypti
43062890.autores: Zhang J, Tsujimoto H, … Keene AC (5 autores)
43062890.resumo: Proteína dietética do sangue (BSA sozinho reproduz o efeito) aumenta o sono de Aedes aegypti por vários dias após o repasto, além da fase de busca de hospedeiro; o receptor de leucocinina (Lkr) também foi testado por RNAi.
43062890.resumo_original: Sleep is a ubiquitous, yet highly variable, behavior across species. The duration and timing of sleep are influenced by ecological demands and dietary context. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, a blood-feeding insect with specialized nutritional requirements, the relationship between feeding and sleep remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how blood-derived dietary protein influences sleep regulation. Using postural analysis, videography, and arousal-threshold assays, we established that immobility bouts of ≥10 min reliably define sleep in A. aegypti. Mosquitoes lacking the circadian clock gene cycle still maintained daily sleep rhythms but exhibited reduced sleep duration and heightened overall activity. Infrared activity monitoring revealed that blood-fed females showed a marked increase in sleep beginning immediately after feeding and persisting for several days, accompanied by reduced locomotor activity. Notably, this sleep elevation lasted well beyond the cessation of previously reported host-seeking phases, raising the possibility of distinct phases of opportunistic vs. targeted host pursuit. To determine the dietary basis of this effect, we tested mosquitoes fed a bovine serum albumin (BSA)-based diet. BSA feeding alone was sufficient to mimic the sleep-promoting and activity-reducing effects of blood, suggesting dietary protein is a major nutritional regulator. Moreover, RNAi-mediated knockdown of the leucokinin receptor (Lkr), which has previously been associated with fluid homeostasis and feeding behavior, resulted in enhanced sleep and reduced activity, implicating mosquito LK signaling in the modulation of postprandial sleep. Together, these findings demonstrate that blood-derived proteins drive sustained increases in sleep and reductions in locomotor activity in A. aegypti. This work positions A. aegypti as a model for dissecting nutrient-specific regulation of sleep and highlights potential adaptive functions of protein-induced quiescence, such as energy conservation and predator avoidance. More broadly, it provides insight into how specialized diets shape the neural and behavioral architecture of sleep.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora o sono seja profundamente moldado pelo contexto ecológico e nutricional, a relação entre hematofagia e regulação do sono em Aedes aegypti permanecia indefinida. Os autores investigaram se o repasto sanguíneo e especificamente seu componente proteico induzem estados prolongados de sono pós-prandial no vetor.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Combinando análise postural, videografia, ensaios de limiar de despertar (arousal-threshold) e monitoramento infravermelho contínuo de atividade locomotora em fêmeas de Aedes aegypti (incluindo mutantes do gene de relógio circadiano cycle), os autores validaram episódios de imobilidade ≥ 10 minutos como critério operacional de sono. Para isolar o gatilho nutricional e molecular, compararam sangue total a uma dieta artificial purificada de albumina sérica bovina (BSA) e realizaram silenciamento por RNAi do receptor de leucocinina (Lkr).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Mutantes de cycle mantiveram ritmos diários de sono, porém com menor duração total e hiperatividade basal. Em fêmeas selvagens, o repasto sanguíneo disparou aumento acentuado do sono e queda locomotora imediatamente após a alimentação, persistindo por vários dias — muito além da janela clássica de supressão de busca por hospedeiro. A ingestão isolada de BSA reproduziu integralmente o aumento sustentado de sono induzido pelo sangue, demonstrando que a proteína dietética é o regulador nutricional primário, enquanto o knockdown por RNAi de Lkr elevou o sono e reduziu a locomoção, implicando a via da leucocinina na modulação pós-prandial.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Repasto Sanguíneo HFHS & Metabolismo do Vetor' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta diretamente nutrição pós-repasto, sinalização do receptor de leucocinina (Lkr) via RNAi e conservação energética em Aedes aegypti, abrindo uma variável comportamental inédita para os estudos de dieta HFHS (rica em lipídios/glicose versus proteína) conduzidos no LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Monitorar em actímetros infravermelhos se fêmeas de Aedes aegypti alimentadas com sangue de camundongos obesos (HFHS) exibem alteração na duração da quiescência pós-prandial de ≥ 10 min e na expressão de Lkr em relação ao repasto controle.

43072483.titulo: Convergent evolution of bt resistance in insects: Receptor mutations, non-receptor mechanisms and polygenic adaptation
43072483.autores: Balaji A, Balakrishnan N, … Raghu R (5 autores)
43072483.resumo: Revisão que reúne mecanismos de resistência a Bt em insetos-praga: mutações em receptores (ABC, caderina, APN, ALP), mecanismos fora do receptor (ativação e sequestro da toxina, efeitos da microbiota) e arquitetura poligênica (variação de número de cópias em Helicoverpa zea), mais resistência a Vip3.
43072483.resumo_original: The extensive cultivation of transgenic Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) crops has constituted one of the largest human-mediated evolutionary selection experiments in modern agriculture. Although resistance is often attributed to specific management failures, accumulating global evidence shows that Bt-resistant populations repeatedly emerge across diverse agroecosystems and unrelated insect taxa, through comparable ecological conditions and a constrained set of adaptive mechanisms, indicating a central role for convergent evolution. This review integrates ecological, molecular and genomic perspectives into a single evolutionary framework. It argues that Bt resistance evolves through partially predictable trajectories shaped by convergent ecological pressures and constrained molecular pathways. At the ecological level, recurrent pressures such as prolonged Bt exposure, suboptimal toxin expression, inadequate refuge implementation and continuous host availability generate similar selection regimes in unrelated insect taxa. At the molecular level, convergence is most evident in receptor-gene modifications within ATP-binding cassette transporters, cadherins, aminopeptidases N and alkaline phosphatases, alongside non-receptor processes affecting toxin activation, sequestration and Bt susceptibility, including microbiota-associated effects. Genomic studies further demonstrate that resistance is not always explained by single major-effect mutations but can involve multilocus and polygenic architectures, as demonstrated by copy-number variation and standing quantitative-trait variation in Helicoverpa zea. The review also examines resistance to Vip3 toxins, considering reported genetic mechanisms and implications for Bt pyramids. These findings show how ecological pressures channel adaptation into a constrained set of molecular pathways, while diverse genetic architectures expand the evolutionary routes available to pest populations. We also discuss what molecular convergence means for resistance monitoring and management, and where the constraint may fail.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora o surgimento de populações de insetos resistentes a culturas transgênicas expressando toxinas de Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) seja frequentemente atribuído a falhas isoladas de manejo local, evidências globais mostram evolução repetida da resistência em táxons distantes sob pressões seletivas equivalentes. O trabalho sintetiza um modelo evolutivo unificado integrando ecologia, vias moleculares restritas e arquitetura genômica poligênica.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão integrativa de estudos ecológicos, bioquímicos e genômicos populacionais sobre evolução convergente de resistência a toxinas Cry e Vip3 de Bacillus thuringiensis em lepidópteros e coleópteros-praga (incluindo Helicoverpa zea). Foram comparados regimes de seleção em campo (exposição prolongada, subdosagem tecidual e refúgio insuficiente), alterações em famílias de receptores de borda em escova, vias não ligadas a receptores e mapeamentos genômicos de variação de número de cópias (CNV) e locos quantitativos.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A síntese demonstra forte convergência molecular em quatro classes canônicas de receptores do intestino médio — transportadores ABC (como ABCC2), caderinas, aminopeptidases N (APN) e fosfatases alcalinas (ALP) — coexistindo com mecanismos não receptores de ativação proteolítica alterada, sequestro luminal de toxina e modulação pela microbiota intestinal. Revela ainda que, além de mutações monogênicas de grande efeito, a resistência em campo envolve arquiteturas poligênicas e variação de número de cópias (como documentado em Helicoverpa zea), além de mecanismos genéticos distintos frente a toxinas Vip3 em pirâmides Bt.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Incide diretamente no programa de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas do LUCHM em Spodoptera frugiperda e Anticarsia gemmatalis, reforçando a necessidade de monitorar simultaneamente receptores ABCC2/APN/ALP, integridade da matriz peritrófica, proteases luminais e contribuição de simbiontes bacterianos como Enterococcus mundtii.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Cruzar ensaios de susceptibilidade a toxinas Cry em larvas de Spodoptera frugiperda e Anticarsia gemmatalis com depleção/reconstituição de simbiontes intestinais para separar resistência mediada por receptores ABCC2 de mecanismos luminais dependentes da microbiota.

43079132.titulo: Volume Electron Microscopy of Cortical Organoids: Methods for Region Identification, Connectome Reconstruction, and Organelle Segmentation.
43079132.autores: Dallere S, Mattioni A, … Boido M (9 autores)
43079132.resumo: Fluxo de trabalho de vEM em organoides corticais humanos: CLEM, mosaico SEM de grande área, FIB-SEM e validação por TEM. Dos dois protocolos de inclusão comparados, DeFelipe e Fairén/Cano-Astorga permite segmentar sinapses e traçar neuritos; Deerinck dá mais contraste de membrana, mas limita a visualização da densidade pós-sináptica.
43079132.resumo_original: Volume electron microscopy (vEM) has become a powerful tool for 3D ultrastructural analysis of neural circuits, yet its application to human brain organoids remains limited, particularly for connectomic studies. Here, we established a comprehensive and scalable workflow for applying vEM to human cortical organoids, integrating correlative light and electron microscopy, large-area SEM (scanning electron microscopy) mosaic imaging, focused ion beam-SEM (FIB-SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) validation. By systematically comparing two embedding protocols in use, we demonstrated that the DeFelipe and Fairén (1993); Cano-Astorga et al. (2024a) method provides optimal compatibility with toluidine blue-stained semithin sectioning and enables reliable synapse segmentation and neurite tracing. In contrast, the Deerinck's protocol (2010) offers enhanced membrane contrast but limits postsynaptic density visualization. Using FIB-SEM imaging of peripheral, neuropil-like regions of cortical organoids, we achieved accurate 3D reconstruction of synapses, neurites and intracellular organelles, enabling quantitative assessment of synaptic apposition surfaces, neurite trajectories, and organelle distribution across defined cellular compartments. Together, our results demonstrate for the first time the feasibility of micro-connectomic reconstruction in human cortical organoids at nanometer resolution. This methodological framework expands the applicability of vEM to organoid systems and provides a robust foundation for future studies of human brain development, disease modeling, and therapeutic evaluation at the synaptic and subcellular level.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora a microscopia eletrônica de volume (vEM) seja referência para reconstrução ultraestrutural 3D de circuitos neurais, sua aplicação a organoides corticais humanos permanece limitada por desafios de identificação regional e preservação sináptica. Os autores desenvolveram um fluxo escalável para viabilizar estudos microconectômicos e segmentação de organelas em organoides cerebrais humanos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Fluxo multimodal integrando microscopia correlativa óptica e eletrônica (CLEM), imageamento em mosaico por MEV de grande área (large-area SEM), microscopia eletrônica de varredura com feixe de íons focalizado (FIB-SEM) e validação por microscopia eletrônica de transmissão (TEM). Compararam sistematicamente os protocolos de inclusão de DeFelipe & Fairén (1993)/Cano-Astorga et al. (2024a) e de Deerinck (2010) em regiões periféricas tipo neurópilo de organoides corticais.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O protocolo de DeFelipe & Fairén/Cano-Astorga apresentou compatibilidade superior com cortes semifinos corados com azul de toluidina e permitiu segmentação confiável de sinapses e rastreamento de neuritos, enquanto o protocolo de Deerinck aumentou o contraste de membranas porém limitou a visualização da densidade pós-sináptica. Por meio de FIB-SEM em resolução nanométrica, reconstruíram em 3D sinapses, trajetórias de neuritos e organelas intracelulares, quantificando superfícies de aposição sináptica e distribuição subcelular de organelas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Fornece parâmetros diretos de escolha de protocolo de inclusão (OTO/Deerinck vs. preservação de densidades sinápticas) e fluxo CLEM + mosaico SEM + FIB-SEM altamente transferíveis aos projetos de ultraestrutura 3D do LUCHM no CENABIO/UFRJ.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Comparar o protocolo de Cano-Astorga com o OTO clássico em amostras de cérebro murino com malária cerebral por PbA e de intestino médio de Aedes aegypti para otimizar simultaneamente contraste de organelas/contactomas e estruturas de junção.

43079774.titulo: Extracellular Polyphosphate at the Host-Pathogen Interface: Emerging Roles in Virulence and Therapeutic Opportunity.
43079774.autores: Tennakoon A, Shrestha SK, Rijal R (3 autores)
43079774.resumo: Revisão sobre polifosfato extracelular na interface hospedeiro-patógeno: o polyP bacteriano de cadeia longa é em geral imunossupressor (prejudica a maturação do fagossomo, reprograma macrófagos, reduz a morte por complemento e a atividade de neutrófilos), enquanto o polyP curto do hospedeiro é pró-coagulante e inflamatório.
43079774.resumo_original: Polyphosphate (polyP) is a conserved linear polymer of orthophosphate residues linked by phosphoanhydride bonds. Although polyP has long been studied for its intracellular roles in phosphate storage, energy metabolism, and stress adaptation, growing evidence indicates that extracellular polyP also influences host-pathogen interactions. In a subset of well-characterized bacterial systems, including mycobacteria and Neisseria species, extracellular or surface-associated polyP has been directly linked to impaired phagosome maturation, altered macrophage activation, reduced complement-mediated killing, and reduced neutrophil antimicrobial activity, whereas in other pathogens, polyP supports virulence primarily via intracellular mechanisms. PolyP chain length governs biological activity: long-chain bacterial polyP is largely immunosuppressive, whereas short-chain host polyP promotes procoagulant and inflammatory signaling, although context dictates specific outcomes. Here, we examine models of polyP externalization, detail how extracellular polyP impairs phagosome maturation, reprograms macrophages, and inhibits complement, evaluate interbacterial and probiotic barrier functions, and consider therapeutic opportunities targeting polyP metabolism.

resumo_blocos.racional: O polifosfato inorgânico (poliP) — polímero linear de resíduos de ortofosfato unidos por ligações fosfoanidrido — é classicamente estudado por suas funções intracelulares em reserva de fosfato, bioenergética e adaptação ao estresse. Esta revisão analisa evidências crescentes de que o poliP extracelular e associado à superfície atua como modulador direto de virulência e evasão imune na interface patógeno-hospedeiro.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão mecanística integrando modelos de externalização de poliP e dados funcionais em sistemas bacterianos bem caracterizados, como micobactérias e espécies de Neisseria, comparando efeitos dependentes do comprimento de cadeia entre poliP bacteriano de cadeia longa e poliP de cadeia curta derivado do hospedeiro.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O poliP extracelular ou de superfície bacteriana promove comprometimento da maturação do fagossomo, reprogramação/alteração da ativação de macrófagos, redução da lise mediada pelo sistema complemento e queda da atividade antimicrobiana de neutrófilos. Evidências comparativas mostram que o tamanho da cadeia dita o desfecho biológico: poliP bacteriano de cadeia longa exerce efeito majoritariamente imunossupressor, ao passo que poliP curto do hospedeiro estimula sinalização pró-coagulante e inflamatória de forma dependente do contexto, abrindo também frentes sobre barreiras probióticas e alvos terapêuticos no metabolismo de poliP.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Polifosfato Inorgânico & Acidocalcisomas' do LUCHM.

43082089.titulo: Sulfakinin Signaling Regulates Feeding and Energy Homeostasis in Hyphantria cunea: A Viable Target for Oral RNAi-Based Pest Control.
43082089.autores: Qi Q, Zhang J, … Cao C (7 autores)
43082089.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082089.resumo: Em Hyphantria cunea, o eixo sulfakinina (SK)/receptor (SKR) varia com o estado nutricional; silenciá-lo altera a homeostase energética, aumenta o consumo, esgota reservas, reduz a tolerância ao estresse e prejudica a reprodução. dsRNA produzido em bactéria e dado por via oral induziu RNAi, mortalidade larval e atraso de desenvolvimento.
43082089.resumo_original: Hyphantria cunea is a globally important pest of agricultural and forest ecosystems, owing its invasiveness to starvation tolerance, high feeding activity, and rapid reproduction. Neuropeptide signaling systems play a central role in regulating these key physiological processes. This study characterized the Sulfakinin (SK)/Sulfakinin receptor (SKR) pathway in H. cuneaand evaluated its potential for pest management. SK and SKR expression was influenced by nutritional status. Silencing SK or SKR disrupted energy homeostasis, increased food consumption, depleted energy reserves, reduced stress tolerance, and severely impaired reproduction. Conversely, SK peptide injection suppressed feeding during the early treatment period and significantly limited larval weight gain at 48-72 h. Furthermore, oral delivery of bacterially produced dsRNA targeting SK or SKR induced RNAi responses, resulting in increased larval mortality and delayed development. Collectively, these findings highlight the SK/SKR signaling pathway as a promising molecular target for sustainable RNAi-based strategies to control H. cunea.

resumo_blocos.racional: A praga invasora agrícola e florestal Hyphantria cunea destaca-se por elevada tolerância ao jejum, intensa atividade alimentar e rápida reprodução, processos coordenados por sistemas neuropeptidérgicos. Os autores caracterizaram a via da sulfacinina (SK) e seu receptor (SKR) como reguladora da homeostase energética e alvo molecular para controle baseado em RNAi oral.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Análise transcricional de SK e SKR sob diferentes estados nutricionais, ensaios de perda de função por silenciamento gênico de SK ou SKR, injeção de peptídeo sintético de SK avaliando consumo alimentar e ganho de peso larval em 48–72 h, além de entrega oral de dsRNA produzido em bactérias direcionado a SK ou SKR.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A expressão de SK e SKR respondeu diretamente ao estado nutricional. O silenciamento de SK ou SKR desregulou a homeostase energética, elevou o consumo alimentar, depletou reservas energéticas, reduziu a tolerância ao estresse e prejudicou severamente a reprodução; inversamente, a injeção do peptídeo SK suprimiu a alimentação no período inicial e restringiu significativamente o ganho de massa larval entre 48 e 72 h. A entrega oral de dsRNA bacteriano anti-SK ou anti-SKR desencadeou resposta de RNAi efetiva, elevando a mortalidade larval e atrasando o desenvolvimento.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece um paralelo direto para os programas de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas e eixo neuropeptidérgico em lepidópteros do LUCHM (Spodoptera frugiperda e Anticarsia gemmatalis), validando dsRNA bacteriano oral contra receptores neuropeptidérgicos.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Mapear ortólogos de sulfacinina/SKR em Spodoptera frugiperda e testar se o silenciamento oral prejudica a integridade metabólica intestinal ou potencializa a letalidade de protoxinas Cry/Vip3 de Bacillus thuringiensis.
