10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.titulo: A standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay with spatially defined bite areas
10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.autores: Miot EF, Medkour H, … Pompon J (10 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.resumo: Preprint: ensaio padronizado de transmissão mosquito-camundongo com áreas de picada definidas (Miot, Pompon); abstract não lido, só o título.
10.64898/2026.11.19.767790.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne viruses initiate infection in the skin, where interactions between viral particles, host cells, and mosquito saliva can influence early infection and subsequent viral dissemination. Investigating these events requires methods that link mosquito exposure to the precise site of inoculation. However, identifying individual bite sites during subsequent tissue collection remains a practical challenge in mosquito-to-mouse transmission models. Here, we describe a standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay that facilitates the localization of mosquito bite sites and targeted tissue sampling. The method combines a custom 3D-printed feeding device, individual mosquito exposure, and perforated adhesive tape to define the biting area and mark identified bite sites for subsequent collection. We demonstrate the application of this protocol using West Nile virus (WNV) and Dengue virus (DENV)-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes with C57BL/6J mice and A129 Ifnar1-/- mice, respectively. All infected mosquitoes successfully blood-fed within 20 min of exposure. After three infected-mosquito bites, mice developed clinical signs from approximately day 6 post-bite, with mortality occurring between days 8 and 10 for WNV, while disease onset occurred at 4 days post bite and most of the mice recovered by day 10 for DENV. To investigate early WNV viral kinetics in skin, WNV genomic RNA was quantified in biopsies collected at marked bite sites and the draining inguinal lymph nodes. Viral RNA was detected in both tissues as early as 1 h post-bite, and RNA levels increased significantly at 24 h post-bite. This protocol provides a practical approach for identifying mosquito bite sites and investigating early tissue-level events following vector-mediated transmission. With appropriate validation, the protocol can be adapted to other vector pathogen host systems and downstream analyses.

resumo_blocos.racional: A transmissão de arbovírus inicia-se na derme, onde partículas virais, células residentes do hospedeiro e fatores salivares do mosquito interagem nos primeiros minutos pós-picada. Contudo, localizar com precisão milimétrica o ponto exato de inoculação individual para biópsia tecidual precoce seguia sendo um entrave técnico nos modelos mosquito-camundongo.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Desenvolveu-se um protocolo padronizado de transmissão mosquito-para-camundongo combinando um dispositivo de alimentação impresso em 3D, exposição individualizada de mosquitos e fita adesiva perfurada que delimita a janela cutânea de picada e marca cada ponto de repasto. O método foi validado expondo camundongos C57BL/6J e A129 Ifnar1-/- a três fêmeas de Aedes aegypti infectadas respectivamente com vírus do Nilo Ocidental (WNV) ou Dengue (DENV), seguido de quantificação de RNA genômico viral em biópsias cutâneas demarcadas e linfonodos inguinais drenantes em 1 h e 24 h pós-picada.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Todas as fêmeas infectadas realizaram repasto sanguíneo completo em até 20 minutos de exposição controlada. Após três picadas infectantes, camundongos C57BL/6J desenvolveram sinais clínicos de WNV por volta do dia 6 e mortalidade entre os dias 8 e 10, enquanto camundongos A129 Ifnar1-/- apresentaram início clínico de DENV no dia 4 com recuperação majoritária até o dia 10. O RNA genômico de WNV já foi detectado tanto na biópsia cutânea demarcada quanto no linfonodo inguinal drenante em apenas 1 hora pós-picada, elevando-se significativamente em 24 horas.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Imunidade de Vetores & RNAi' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Protocolo de baixo custo (impressão 3D + máscara adesiva perfurada) imediatamente adaptável ao biotério C57BL/6J e insetário do LUCHM tanto para arbovírus quanto para rastrear a deposição dérmica de esporozoítos de Plasmodium berghei ANKA e proteínas salivares.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Fabricar em impressora 3D o adaptador de área delimitada para comparar a cinética cutânea (1 h vs 24 h) e o infiltrado inflamatório dérmico após picada de fêmeas de Aedes criadas sob dieta padrão versus HFHS.

43069274.titulo: A synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complex organizes photoreceptor neurotransmission
43069274.autores: Wang F, Zhao W, … Zhang J (13 autores)
43069274.resumo: FIB-SEM e eletrofisiologia revelam complexos mitocôndria–fita–vesícula sináptica em fotorreceptores: rodopsina de bastonete com par 1:1 megamitocôndria–fita; desmonte do complexo precede a perda funcional na degeneração (Nat Commun).
43069274.resumo_original: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. In a retinal degeneration model, the sMRVc progressively disassembles before functional decline, with fragmented mitochondria, detached ribbons, and dispersed vesicles. We also identify non-ribbon release sites selectively targeting horizontal cells. These findings establish the sMRVc as a conserved structural-metabolic module whose subtype-specific organization reflects distinct visual demands and whose integrity is essential for synaptic health.

resumo_blocos.racional: Sinapses de fotorreceptores dependem da cooperação estreita entre mitocôndrias, fitas sinápticas (synaptic ribbons) e vesículas para sustentar liberação contínua de neurotransmissores, mas a organização tridimensional nanoscópica desses elementos em módulos bioenergéticos funcionais entre bastonetes e cones permanecia obscura.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores empregaram microscopia eletrônica de varredura com feixe de íons focalizado (FIB-SEM) combinada a registros eletrofisiológicos em retina de mamíferos, reconstruindo em 3D terminais de bastonetes (rod spherules) e pedículos de cones. Avaliaram ainda a perturbação genética da proteína de ancoragem mitocondrial sintafilina (syntaphilin) e acompanharam a integridade ultraestrutural do complexo em um modelo de degeneração retiniana antes do declínio funcional.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A reconstrução por FIB-SEM revelou complexos sinápticos mitocôndria-fita-vesícula (sMRVcs) com arquiteturas subtipo-específicas: esférulas de bastonetes exibem pareamento estrito 1:1 entre uma única megamitocôndria e uma fita sináptica para sustentar liberação contínua de glutamato no escuro, ao passo que pedículos de cones abrigam múltiplos sMRVcs distribuídos, além de sítios de liberação não associados à fita voltados a células horizontais. A deleção de sintafilina alterou a razão para 2:1 nos bastonetes ao recrutar mitocôndrias extras junto à fita e potencializou a transmissão sináptica, enquanto na degeneração retiniana a desmontagem do sMRVc (fragmentação mitocondrial e destacamento da fita) precedeu a perda funcional.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Exemplifica o poder analítico do FIB-SEM para quantificar acoplamento físico-metabólico e estequiometria organelar em escala nanométrica, servindo de referência metodológica direta para os projetos de contactoma mitocôndria-organela no CENABIO/LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Aplicar métricas equivalentes de distância de ancoragem e razão estequiométrica em volumes FIB-SEM do CENABIO para quantificar o acoplamento entre mitocôndrias, gotas lipídicas e retículo no epitélio intestinal de Aedes aegypti.

10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.titulo: The ACDC domains of AP2-O3 and FD3 contribute to protein interactions and ookinete development
10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.autores: Tang J, Liu B, … Li Z (7 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.resumo: Preprint: domínios ACDC de AP2-O3 e FD3 e o desenvolvimento do oocineto de Plasmodium.
10.64898/2026.11.19.767835.resumo_original: The Apicomplexan AP2 (ApiAP2) family of transcription factors are key regulators of Plasmodium spp. parasite development. In addition to containing AP2 DNA-binding domains, nine ApiAP2 proteins also encode an apicomplexan-specific ACDC domain whose function remains largely unknown. Here, we dissect the biological role of the ACDC domain from two female-specific regulators, AP2-O3 and FD3, using the rodent malaria model Plasmodium yoelii and the human malaria parasite P. falciparum. In Plasmodium yoelii, deletion of the ACDC domain preserved AP2-O3 and FD3 protein presence and nuclear localization without significantly affecting asexual growth or gametocyte production. However, deletion of these domains impaired the gametocyte-to-ookinete transition, reducing ookinete conversion efficiency. Proteomic and biochemical studies indicate that the AP2-O3 ACDC domain interacts with FD3, while the FD3 ACDC domain preferentially associates with full-length FD3. Transcriptomic data showed that over 80% of transcripts that increased after FD3 ACDC deletion were also higher following AP2-O3 loss, with female gametocyte marker expression largely unchanged. In Plasmodium falciparum, removing the FD3 ACDC domain did not affect female lineage-specific expression of FD3, nuclear localization of FD3, or the asexual growth and gametocyte maturation of parasites. Leveraging the high sequence conservation of ACDC domains across the Plasmodium genus, we conducted structure-based virtual screening of 283 compounds targeting the predicted PfAP2-O3 and PfFD3 ACDC interaction interface. Seven compounds ranked among the top candidate inhibitors for both domains, and the highest-priority ligand for each domain was further evaluated by molecular dynamics simulations. Collectively, our findings support a role for ACDC domains in ApiAP2 protein interactions and identify candidate compounds for future experimental evaluation as potential transmission-blocking leads.

resumo_blocos.racional: Fatores de transcrição da família ApiAP2 governam transições críticas do ciclo de Plasmodium, e nove deles possuem na extremidade um domínio exclusivo de apicomplexas denominado ACDC cuja função bioquímica era desconhecida. O estudo investigou o papel do domínio ACDC nos reguladores específicos da linhagem feminina AP2-O3 e FD3 durante o desenvolvimento sexual e formação de oocinetos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Utilizando edição genética nos modelos murino Plasmodium yoelii e humano Plasmodium falciparum, os autores deletaram seletivamente os domínios ACDC de AP2-O3 e FD3 avaliando expressão, localização nuclear, crescimento assexuado, gametocitogênese e eficiência de conversão de gametócitos em oocinetos. Complementaram a análise com ensaios proteômicos/bioquímicos de interação proteica, RNA-seq comparativo e triagem virtual baseada em estrutura de 283 compostos contra a interface predita PfAP2-O3/PfFD3 seguida de dinâmica molecular.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Em P. yoelii e P. falciparum, a deleção do domínio ACDC preservou a expressão e a localização nuclear de AP2-O3 e FD3 sem afetar a replicação sanguínea assexuada nem a produção de gametócitos, mas bloqueou severamente a transição gametócito-oocineto em P. yoelii. Ensaios bioquímicos mostraram que o domínio ACDC de AP2-O3 interage com FD3 e o ACDC de FD3 promove autoassociação, com mais de 80% de sobreposição nos transcritos desregulados após perda de ambos. A triagem virtual de 283 moléculas identificou sete candidatos prioritários capazes de alvejar ambos os domínios ACDC conservados.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Identifica uma interface proteína-proteína altamente conservada (domínio ACDC em AP2-O3/FD3) indispensável para a maturação do oocineto no intestino do mosquito, oferecendo novos alvos químicos de bloqueio de transmissão alinhados à frente de Plasmodium do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar experimentalmente se inibidores candidatos da interface ACDC bloqueiam a conversão ex vivo de gametócitos em oocinetos de Plasmodium berghei ANKA e impedem a travessia do epitélio intestinal do vetor.

43077712.titulo: Natural Infection Induces Antibodies Targeting Pfs230 Domains D1M and D7D8 with Potential for Malaria Transmission Blocking.
43077712.autores: Harju T, Cao Y, Kumar N (3 autores)
43077712.resumo: Anticorpos naturais contra os domínios D1M e D7D8 de Pfs230 (candidato a vacina de bloqueio de transmissão) foram correlacionados em sorologia de Zimbábue (n = 301) e Tailândia (n = 44).
43077712.resumo_original: The natural immunogenicity of domain 1 (D1M) and domains 7 and 8 (D7D8) in Plasmodium falciparum transmission-blocking vaccine (TBV) candidate Pfs230 is assessed. Antibody reactivity by ELISA using endemic human sera from Zimbabwe (n = 301) and Thailand (n = 44) was evaluated. Regression analyses revealed significant positive correlations between responses to both domains. A 1-log increase in Pfs230-D1M reactivity predicted a 0.43- to 0.87-log increase in Pfs230-D7D8 reactivity across cohorts. Furthermore, Pfs230-D1M positivity increased the odds of Pfs230-D7D8 positivity by 59% to 89%. These data demonstrate that both Pfs230-D1M and Pfs230-D7D8 are highly immunogenic during natural infection, validating their potential as strong TBV candidates.

resumo_blocos.racional: A proteína de superfície de gametócitos/gametas Pfs230 é um dos principais candidatos a vacina de bloqueio de transmissão (TBV) contra Plasmodium falciparum, mas a imunogenicidade natural comparativa de regiões específicas da molécula em áreas endêmicas precisa ser quantificada. O trabalho avaliou respostas de anticorpos humanos contra o domínio 1 (D1M) e os domínios 7 e 8 (D7D8) de Pfs230.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Ensaios imunoenzimáticos (ELISA) utilizando soros humanos de áreas endêmicas para malária no Zimbábue (n = 301) e na Tailândia (n = 44), seguidos de análises de regressão para mensurar correlação quantitativa e razão de chances entre reatividade a Pfs230-D1M e Pfs230-D7D8.
resumo_blocos.resultados: As análises de regressão revelaram correlações positivas significativas entre os títulos contra ambos os domínios nas duas coortes geográficas. Cada incremento de 1 log na reatividade a Pfs230-D1M previu aumento de 0,43 a 0,87 log na reatividade a Pfs230-D7D8, e a soropositividade para Pfs230-D1M elevou em 59% a 89% a chance de positividade para Pfs230-D7D8, confirmando que ambos os domínios são altamente imunogênicos durante a infecção natural.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Reforça a priorização de epítopos combinados ou específicos de Pfs230 (D1M e D7D8) no programa de Biologia Celular de Plasmodium & Bloqueio de Transmissão do LUCHM, validando imunogenicidade natural em populações humanas distintas.

43079506.titulo: A national geocoded inventory of Aedes mosquitoes in Kenya: integrating published, archival, and digital sources across 124 years.
43079506.autores: Muchiri SK, Mwangi LW, … Snow RW (8 autores)
43079506.resumo: Inventário nacional geocodificado de Aedes no Quênia, integrando fontes publicadas, de arquivo e digitais.
43079506.resumo_original:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV), transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes, represent growing public health threats in Kenya and across sub-Saharan Africa. In the absence of licensed vaccines for either disease in Africa, targeted vector control remains the primary prevention strategy, making accurate knowledge of Aedes species distributions essential. Global inventories of Aedes species are severely under-representative for Kenya, with existing repositories documenting fewer than 200 unique locations. No comprehensive, geocoded national inventory integrating published, unpublished, and digital sources has previously been assembled.
Three complementary approaches were used to assemble a national geocoded inventory of Aedes species in Kenya including (i) a systematic review of peer-reviewed literature, theses, and conference abstracts; (ii) digitisation of unpublished archival reports from the Ministry of Health, Division of Insect-Borne/Vector-Borne Diseases (DIBD/DVBD), regional and municipal councils; and (iii) cross-referencing with Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and Walter Reed Biosystematics Unit's (WRBU) VectorMap repositories. Data were extracted using a standardised template, de-duplicated, and geocoded using Global Positioning System (GPS) coordinates, Google Earth, or census enumeration area shapefiles. Aedes species were classified as principal or possible secondary vectors based on confirmed field detection and, for the principal vector, an established role in transmission during dengue and chikungunya outbreaks reported in Kenya.
A total of 1,802 time-site records were identified across 855 unique locations between 1901 and 2024, documenting 104 Aedes species. Unpublished archival records contributed 51% of all records, with peer-reviewed articles accounting for 43%. The principal vector, Aedes aegypti was the most widely documented species, reported at 522 unique locations. Eight possible secondary vectors with confirmed DENV and/or CHIKV detection were documented, with Aedes mcintoshi, Ae. ochraceus, and Ae. tricholabis the most frequently recorded. Geographic coverage was concentrated along the coast and western Kenya, with notable surveillance gaps in northern and northeastern regions.
This inventory represents the most comprehensive geocoded database of Aedes mosquito species ever assembled for Kenya, substantially exceeding the coverage of existing global repositories. It provides an essential empirical foundation for disease and vector surveillance, ecological niche modelling (ENM) and sub-national targeting of vector control interventions in Kenya.

resumo_blocos.racional: Na ausência de vacinas amplamente licenciadas contra dengue e chikungunya na África, o controle vetorial direcionado depende criticamente de mapas precisos de ocorrência de mosquitos Aedes. Até então, repositórios globais sub-representavam severamente o Quênia, registrando menos de 200 localidades únicas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Integração de três fontes complementares entre 1901 e 2024: (i) revisão sistemática de literatura revisada por pares, teses e resumos de congressos; (ii) digitalização de relatórios arquivísticos inéditos do Ministério da Saúde queniano (DIBD/DVBD) e conselhos regionais/municipais; e (iii) cruzamento com GBIF e VectorMap (WRBU). Os registros foram padronizados, deduplicados e geocodificados via GPS, Google Earth ou malhas censitárias, classificando vetores principais e potenciais secundários pela detecção confirmada de DENV e/ou CHIKV.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Foram consolidados 1.802 registros espaço-temporais em 855 localidades únicas, documentando 104 espécies de Aedes, com 51% dos dados oriundos de arquivos inéditos e 43% de artigos publicados. resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Fornece base empírica de referência para modelagem de nicho ecológico e seleção de espécies secundárias de Aedes (como Ae. mcintoshi e Ae. ochraceus) com detecção viral natural, relevante para estudos comparativos de competência vetorial no LUCHM.

43081930.titulo: Developmental site type, larval productivity, and insecticide susceptibility of Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
43081930.autores: Zongo S, Toe HK, … Namountougou M (12 autores)
43081930.resumo: Tipo de criadouro, produtividade larval e suscetibilidade a inseticida de Aedes aegypti.
43081930.resumo_original: Arboviral diseases, including dengue and chikungunya, are increasing in sub-Saharan Africa. This study assessed Aedes aegypti larval productivity across three container types and examined associations with abiotic parameters and insecticide resistance patterns in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso. From July to September 2024, a semi-field experiment was conducted at the Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme. Tires, terracotta jars, and buckets were exposed outdoors for natural colonization. Larval abundance and six abiotic parameters (pH, temperature, salinity, conductivity, total dissolved solids, and redox potential) were recorded over 11 rounds. Susceptibility bioassays were performed on emerging Ae. aegypti adults using deltamethrin (0.03%), bendiocarb (0.2%), and malathion (1.5%). A total of 14,020 larvae were collected, of which 93.13% were Ae. aegypti. Tires (mean = 83.3 ± 10.8 larvae/container) and terracotta jars (mean = 50.7 ± 7.4 larvae/container) harbored significantly more larvae than buckets (mean = 22.5 ± 3.3 larvae/container); tires and jars did not differ significantly. Generalized linear mixed model analysis showed no significant effect of abiotic parameters, while container type was strongly associated with abundance. Ae. aegypti populations were resistant to deltamethrin in all container types (mortality 5.2%-17.9%) and to malathion in both tested container types (mortality 88.4%-88.8%). For bendiocarb, populations were resistant in plastic buckets (85.3% mortality), showed suspected resistance in tires (91.6%), and were susceptible in terracotta jars (98.6%). Vector control should prioritize the management of tires and terracotta jars, and widespread pyrethroid resistance highlights the need for alternative tools.

resumo_blocos.racional: O avanço das arboviroses na África Subsaariana exige compreender quais tipos de criadouros sustentam maior produtividade larval de Aedes aegypti e como os adultos emergentes respondem aos inseticidas em uso. O estudo avaliou produtividade larval, parâmetros físico-químicos da água e resistência a inseticidas em Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Experimento em semicampo no Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme (julho a setembro de 2024, 11 rodadas) expondo pneus, potes de terracota e baldes plásticos à colonização natural. Mediram-se abundância larval e seis parâmetros abióticos (pH, temperatura, salinidade, condutividade, sólidos totais dissolvidos e potencial redox) analisados por modelos lineares mistos generalizados (GLMM), além de bioensaios de suscetibilidade em adultos emergentes com deltametrina (0,03%), bendiocarbe (0,2%) e malationa (1,5%).
resumo_blocos.resultados: Coletaram-se 14.020 larvas (93,13% de Ae. aegypti), com produtividade significativamente maior em pneus (média 83,3 ± 10,8 larvas/recipiente) e potes de terracota (50,7 ± 7,4) do que em baldes (22,5 ± 3,3), sem efeito significativo dos parâmetros abióticos no GLMM. Os adultos exibiram forte resistência à deltametrina em todos os criadouros (mortalidade de 5,2% a 17,9%) e resistência à malationa nos dois tipos testados (88,4%–88,8%); para bendiocarbe, houve resistência em baldes (85,3%), resistência suspeita em pneus (91,6%) e suscetibilidade em potes de terracota (98,6%).

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Demonstra que o tipo de criadouro (pneus e terracota) condiciona não apenas a densidade larval, mas também variações na suscetibilidade fenotípica de adultos emergentes a carbamatos, reforçando a necessidade de controle larvário e alternativas aos piretroides.

43083712.titulo: Down-Regulation of eIF3L Is Associated with Decreased Susceptibility of Helicoverpa armigera to Cry1Ac.
43083712.autores: Li N, Zhang C, … Liang G (8 autores)
43083712.resumo: A queda de eIF3L se associou a menor suscetibilidade de Helicoverpa armigera a Cry1Ac e afeta a expressão dos receptores CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3.
43083712.resumo_original: Large-scale cultivation of transgenic Bt crops has led to target pest resistance to Bt proteins, especially Cry1Ac. Under persistent selection pressure, Helicoverpa armigera has evolved resistance to Bt proteins in both laboratory and field populations, highlighting an urgent need to comprehensively elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying pest Bt resistance. Previous studies have confirmed that the eukaryotic translation initiation factor eIF2 plays a critical role in regulating Bt resistance. Our prior RNA-seq data showed significant differences in the expression level of eIF3L between susceptible and Cry1Ac-resistant strains of H. armigera. In this study, we further observed that the mRNA level of eIF3L was significantly reduced in larvae surviving Cry1Ac exposure. More importantly, heterologous expression of eIF3L increased the susceptibility of Sf9 cells to Cry1Ac. Consistently, knockdown of eIF3L was associated with reduced mortality in H. armigera larvae exposed to Cry1Ac. Together, our in vivo and in vitro results suggest that eIF3L is involved in Cry1Ac toxicity. Furthermore, eIF3L affects the expression of the Cry1Ac receptor genes CAD, ABCC2, and ABCC3. Collectively, these results indicate that down-regulation of eIF3L is associated with decreased susceptibility of H. armigera to Cry1Ac, providing novel insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying insect resistance to Bt proteins.

resumo_blocos.racional: O cultivo extensivo de culturas transgênicas Bt selecionou resistência à toxina Cry1Ac em populações de campo e laboratório de Helicoverpa armigera. Após identificar expressão diferencial do fator de iniciação traducional eIF3L em dados prévios de RNA-seq entre linhagens suscetíveis e resistentes, os autores investigaram o papel funcional de eIF3L na toxicidade de Cry1Ac.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Quantificação de mRNA de eIF3L em larvas de H. armigera sobreviventes à exposição a Cry1Ac, expressão heteróloga de eIF3L em células Sf9 (Spodoptera frugiperda) desafiadas com Cry1Ac, silenciamento gênico (knockdown) de eIF3L in vivo em larvas expostas à toxina e análise de expressão dos genes receptores CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Os transcritos de eIF3L mostraram-se significativamente reduzidos nas larvas sobreviventes ao tratamento com Cry1Ac. A expressão heteróloga de eIF3L aumentou a suscetibilidade das células Sf9 à Cry1Ac, enquanto o knockdown de eIF3L reduziu a mortalidade das larvas de H. armigera expostas à toxina. Adicionalmente, eIF3L modulou a expressão dos receptores de Cry1Ac CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3, ligando a maquinaria de tradução à densidade de receptores de toxina na membrana intestinal.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Revela um mecanismo pós-transcricional/traducional (via eIF3L) controlando múltiplos receptores clássicos de Cry1Ac (CAD, ABCC2 e ABCC3), de interesse imediato para o programa de Controle de Pragas & Bioinseticidas do LUCHM em lepidópteros-praga.

43082033.titulo: Trained immunity in sepsis from immune reprogramming to precision immunotherapy.
43082033.autores: Liu N, Gan T, … Wang Z (5 autores)
43082033.resumo: Revisão sobre imunidade treinada em sepse, da reprogramação imune à imunoterapia de precisão.
43082033.resumo_original: Sepsis represents a severe systemic inflammatory response to infection, with complex immune dysregulation at the core of its pathophysiology. Conventional therapies remain limited to effectively modulate immune status while controlling infection, contributing to high mortality rates and severe long-term complications.In recent years, trained immunity,a form of innate immune memory, has demonstrated novel potential for regulating immune responses through metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic regulation. This narrative review integrates mechanistic and translational evidence on trained immunity in sepsis, with particular emphasis on key signalling pathways, their contributions to immune dysregulation, and potential biomarkers. It further discusses emerging precision immunotherapy strategies.Targeting trained immunity and assesses their opportunities and challenges in clinical translation, with particular emphasis on personalised treatment design and safety evaluation.Finally, we consider the application prospects of trained immunity in the long-term chronic inflammation and immune dysfunction associated with sepsis. However, direct clinical evidence remains limited, and validated biomarkers for identifying trained immune states in patients with sepsis are currently lacking. Future multidisciplinary studies are therefore needed to define clinically relevant trained immune states and establish reliable biomarkers for precision immune intervention in sepsis.

resumo_blocos.racional: A sepse caracteriza-se por resposta inflamatória sistêmica severa com desregulação imune complexa e elevada mortalidade mesmo sob terapias convencionais. Esta revisão narrativa examina como a imunidade treinada — memória imune inata sustentada por reprogramação metabólica e epigenética — pode explicar a disfunção imune crônica e orientar estratégias de imunoterapia de precisão.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Síntese crítica de evidências mecanísticas e translacionais sobre vias de sinalização da imunidade treinada, marcadores metabólicos e epigenéticos, biomarcadores potenciais e desafios de desenho personalizado e segurança clínica na sepse.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A revisão integra vias de reprogramação metabólica e remodelamento epigenético associadas tanto à hiperinflamação quanto à imunoparalisia pós-sepse e às sequelas inflamatórias de longo prazo. Contudo, ressalta que a evidência clínica direta ainda é limitada e que faltam biomarcadores validados para estratificar estados de imunidade treinada em pacientes sépticos antes da intervenção imune personalizada.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Malária Cerebral & Neuroinflamação' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Oferece referencial conceitual para interpretar reprogramação metabólica e epigenética de monócitos/macrófagos em quadros inflamatórios sistêmicos graves comparáveis à malária grave e à malária cerebral.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Avaliar se a exposição prévia a hemo livre ou hemozoína induz assinatura metabólica/epigenética de imunidade treinada ou tolerância em células mieloides e endotélio cerebral na infecção por Plasmodium.

43074085.titulo: Assessment of natural filariae infections in the mosquitoes of Karen state, Myanmar: a cross-sectional PCR survey in six villages
43074085.autores: Rongthong P, Kularbkeeree T, … Nosten F (8 autores)
43074085.resumo: Em seis vilas de Karen (Mianmar), 5,2% (40/772) dos mosquitos tiveram PCR positivo para filárias; W. bancrofti em metade, incluindo Anopheles barbirostris e Aedes albopictus/pseudoalbopictus; estimativa de taxa de inoculação entomológica de 0,094 picada infectante por pessoa-dia.
43074085.resumo_original:
Filarial nematodes transmitted by mosquitos cause significant burdens and important stigma in the affected communities. Focal transmission of Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi was detected incidentally during blood surveys conducted for a program of malaria elimination in Karen state, Myanmar. The objective of this study was to assess filariae infections in selected mosquito species collected in these villages striving to identify the potential vectors, characterise their biting behaviours and estimate the entomological indices of transmission.
Cross-sectional entomological surveys were conducted in September 2019 in six villages. Mosquitos were captured over 24-h diel cycles using the human-landing catch and cow-baited trap collection methods, and identified with dichotomic morphological identification keys. A subset of the specimens of potential vector species was randomly selected and tested with a filariasis PCR assay targeting the parasites 5S rRNA gene. For positive Aedes specimens, correct identification of the filariae and vector species was confirmed with DNA sequencing of the filariasis and mosquito cytochrome c oxidase subunit 1 PCR products.
Overall 5.2% (40/772) mosquito specimens had a positive filariasis PCR result. W. bancrofti DNA was found in half of the positive specimens. Three other zoonotic Brugia and Dirofilaria filariae species were also identified. W. bancrofti DNA was detected in known vector species including Anopheles barbirostris, An. hyrcanus, Downsiomyia harinasutai, Finlaya poicilia and Culex sitiens. Furthermore, it was also found in Aedes albopictus/pseudoalbopictus and Armigeres flavus. W. bancrofti entomological inoculation rate estimate was 0.094 infective bites/person-day (95%CI 0.049 to 0.164). Only 7.5% (3/40) of the positive specimens were captured indoors with the human-landing catch collection method between 9 PM and 5 AM. Specimens infected with zoonotic filariae were captured with the human-landing catch collection method highlighting the potential for zoonotic filariasis transmission in this area. Furthermore, infected specimens were collected in the cow-baited trap suggesting veterinary-based vector control interventions targeting livestock could be used to tackle filariasis transmission in this setting.
This study identified potential vectors of Wuchereria bancrofti and three zoonotic filariae species in Karen state. Mosquito bed nets may have only a limited efficacy against filariasis vectors in this area. Trials of vector control interventions preventing outdoor and early transmission are warranted.

43068115.titulo: From reactive control to precision environmental health: a One Health-based scoping review of vector management strategies in China
43068115.autores: Guo X, Lin Q, … Guo L (8 autores)
43068115.resumo: Revisão de escopo One Health sobre manejo de vetores, do controle reativo à saúde ambiental de precisão (Sci One Health).
43068115.resumo_original: Climate change, urbanization, and global travel have accelerated the resurgence of Aedes-borne diseases, posing growing public health threats. Conventional vector control remains largely reactive and chemical-dependent and is increasingly challenged by climate-driven changes in vector habitats. Using China as a case study, this scoping review examines the shift toward precision environmental health under a One Health framework. We trace surveillance advances from manual vector indices to artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled ecological sensing and examine multisource early-warning approaches integrating meteorological, biological, and human-related data for dynamic risk classification. We also consider how technological interventions, including drone-assisted precision control and biological control, can be integrated with social governance to support climate-resilient health systems. Drawing on these experiences, we propose a Layered Technology framework intended to support adaptable, environmentally sustainable vector management in resource-constrained settings, particularly in the Global South. Finally, we call for coordinated international data sharing and collaboration to address cross-border environmental and public health threats.

43081668.titulo: Epigenetic Crosstalk Between BCG-Infected Macrophages and Naïve Monocytes: Potential Role of the Extracellular Vesicles.
43081668.autores: Ellinger L, Alipoor SD, … Lerm M (6 autores)
43081668.resumo: Fatores solúveis e vesículas extracelulares de macrófagos infectados com BCG alteram a metilação de DNA de monócitos naive, com tendência a menor carga de Mtb.
43081668.resumo_original: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of death from infectious disease. Infected cells secrete extracellular vesicles (EVs), nanosized membrane-bound particles containing bioactive molecules known to mediate intercellular communication and may contribute to immune regulation during infection. We hypothesized that factors released by Mycobacterium bovis Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG)-infected macrophages (MΦs), including EVs, could contribute to epigenetic remodeling of naïve monocytes and influence their response to subsequent Mtb infection. A transwell co-culture system enabled communication via soluble factors and EVs between BCG-infected MΦs and naïve monocytes undergoing differentiation into recipient MΦs. The recipient MΦs exhibited altered DNA methylation patterns compared to those co-cultured with untreated, Staphylococcus aureus-infected or hydrogen peroxide-exposed MΦs. These DNA methylation changes were accompanied by a trend toward lower GFP-based Mtb burden in vitro. BCG-infected MΦs released EVs with a distinct proteomic profile enriched in tuberculosis-related pathways. Exploratory integration of the EV proteomic and DNA methylation datasets from the recipient MΦs identified potential molecular associations, including a TNF-centered network enriched in phagosome and tuberculosis pathways. These findings indicate that exposure to the intercellular environment generated by BCG-infected MΦs, including EVs and soluble factors, is associated with DNA methylation changes and modulation of antimycobacterial responses in recipient cells. Further studies using purified EVs and targeted mechanistic approaches are required to define the relative roles of EVs and other soluble mediators.

43078098.titulo: Flashing light modulates insect behavior in a species-specific manner.
43078098.autores: Ali MS, Luo X, … Holmes TC (4 autores)
43078098.resumo: Luz intermitente modula o comportamento de insetos de modo espécie-específico (Curr Biol). Só título e metadados lidos; abstract não consultado.
43078098.resumo_original: Light is a powerful tool to study animal behavior.1-3 In contrast to natural light, almost all artificial light exhibits flicker, but most work on insect behavioral responses to light flicker focuses on flicker perceptual detection. We tested photopreference light-choice behavior across a wide range of Drosophila species in response to rhythmically flickering light using custom FLASH (flickering light of actuatable spectral hues) instrumentation and find species-specific behavioral responses and altered time-of-day-ordered behaviors that are evoked by light frequencies far beyond perceptual flicker frequency. Mutant analysis shows that behavioral responses to FLASH rely on all known classes of phototransduction, including Cryptochrome and Rhodopsin-7 expressed directly in brain neurons and the eyes. FLASH behavioral responses are abolished following ablation of the pigment-dispersing factor (PDF)-positive lateral ventral neuron circadian light input hub and in circadian mutants. These results suggest means for designing ecologically friendly light devices for species-specific insect behavioral control.

resumo_blocos.racional: Diferentemente da luz solar natural, fontes artificiais exibem cintilação (flicker) rítmica, mas a resposta comportamental dos insetos além da frequência perceptiva de fusão permanecia pouco explorada. Os autores investigaram como luz cintilante espectralmente modulada altera a fotopreferência e ritmos comportamentais em múltiplas espécies de Drosophila.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Ensaios comportamentais de escolha luminosa em painel de espécies de Drosophila utilizando instrumentação customizada FLASH (flickering light of actuatable spectral hues), combinados a análise de mutantes de fotorrecepção (incluindo Cryptochrome e Rhodopsin-7) e ablação genética do centro circadiano de neurônios ventrais laterais positivos para PDF.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A luz cintilante evocou respostas de fotopreferência espécie-específicas e alterou comportamentos ordenados por hora do dia mesmo em frequências muito superiores ao limiar perceptivo de cintilação. Análise com mutantes mostrou dependência de todas as classes conhecidas de fototransdução — incluindo Cryptochrome e Rhodopsin-7 expressos em neurônios cerebrais e olhos — e abolição completa da resposta após ablação do hub circadiano PDF+ ou em mutantes circadianos.

43069404.titulo: Antimicrobial peptides are differentially regulated in blood and visceral adipose tissue in obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction and linked to NLRP3-related signaling
43069404.autores: Casado M, Gómez-Ambrosi J, … Catalán V (13 autores)
43069404.resumo: Em 108 participantes, obesidade se associa a perfil circulante de peptídeos antimicrobianos (catelicidina, calprotectina, entre outros); adipócitos viscerais humanos e macrófagos THP-1 ligam esses peptídeos à sinalização de NLRP3.
43069404.resumo_original: Obesity is characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation in which visceral adipose tissue (VAT) plays a central immunometabolic role. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) integrate host defense and inflammatory signaling, but their regulation across metabolic compartments in human obesity remains incompletely defined. We evaluated circulating AMP concentrations and gene expression levels in VAT and circulating leukocytes from 108 participants classified according to obesity and glycemic status. These analyses were complemented with mechanistic studies in human visceral adipocytes evaluating inflammatory and microbiota-related stimuli, effects of NLR family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3)related modulation, and crosstalk with PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Obesity was associated with a selective circulating AMP profile characterized by higher cathelicidin, calprotectin, lipocalin-2 and neutrophil elastase together with lower α-defensin 6 and β-defensin 1. In VAT, obesity was accompanied by increased expression of several inflammatory AMP-related genes together with higher NLRP3 and NLRP6 expression and reduced DEFB1, with additional differences emerging across glycemic groups. Circulating leukocytes displayed a partially overlapping but distinct transcriptional profile, consistent with compartment-specific regulation rather than a generalized AMP response. In vitro, visceral adipocytes showed gene- and stimulus-dependent AMP responses to inflammatory and microbiota-related signals. NLRP3 silencing attenuated selected LPS-induced inflammatory and antimicrobial responses, whereas the glucose-lowering medication glibenclamide promoted complementary stimulus-dependent effects. Adipocyte-conditioned medium modified AMP expression in PMA-differentiated THP-1 macrophage-like cells. Collectively, these findings identify a selective, compartment-dependent remodeling of antimicrobial pathways in obesity and obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction, with NLRP3-related mechanisms emerging as a potential contributor to the regulation of selected antimicrobial responses in visceral adipocytes.

43074418.titulo: Itaconate: An Emerging Metabolic Regulator Linking Immunity and Ferroptosis
43074418.autores: Li S, Chen Y, … Nan Y (8 autores)
43074418.resumo: Revisão crítica do itaconato (ACOD1/IRG1) na ligação entre imunometabolismo, sinalização redox e ferroptose; aponta confusão frequente entre itaconato endógeno e derivados administrados (4-octil e dimetil itaconato).
43074418.resumo_original:
Itaconate, generated in activated myeloid cells by aconitate decarboxylase 1 (historically termed immune-responsive gene 1), coordinates immunometabolism, redox signalling and regulated cell death. Emerging evidence links this pathway to ferroptosis; however, interpretation is complicated by the frequent conflation of endogenous itaconate with exogenously administered native itaconate and electrophilic derivatives such as 4-octyl itaconate and dimethyl itaconate.
This review critically integrates the biosynthesis, transport and intercellular signalling of itaconate with its effects on ferroptosis. Evidence is examined across solute carrier family 7 member 11-dependent cystine uptake, glutathione supply, glutathione peroxidase 4 expression, stability and catalytic activity, iron-sulfur clusters, ferritinophagy, phospholipid remodelling, mitochondrial redox signalling and selective autophagy, distinguishing cell-autonomous effects in myeloid cells from cell-nonautonomous transfer to parenchymal and tumour cells.
The available evidence supports a context-dependent model: itaconate-related signalling can suppress ferroptosis and limit acute tissue injury, but may also preserve immunosuppressive myeloid populations or confer ferroptosis resistance on tumours; at high pharmacological exposures, selected compounds can instead promote ferritinophagy-dependent ferroptosis.
Clinical translation requires compound-resolved terminology, validated ferroptosis endpoints, cell-specific delivery, quantitative exposure and target-engagement biomarkers and careful assessment of infection- and tumour-related risks.

resumo_blocos.racional: O itaconato, sintetizado em células mieloides ativadas pela enzima aconitato descarboxilase 1 (ACOD1/IRG1), conecta reprogramação imunometabólica, sinalização redox e ferroptose. Contudo, a literatura recente confunde efeitos do itaconato endógeno com derivados eletrofílicos exógenos como 4-octil-itaconato (4-OI) e dimetil-itaconato (DMI).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão mecanística crítica que disseca comparativamente a biossíntese, o transporte e a sinalização intercelular do itaconato nativo versus seus derivados alquilados/eletrofílicos sobre os eixos centrais da ferroptose: captação de cistina dependente de SLC7A11, síntese de glutationa, expressão e estabilidade catalítica de GPX4, centros ferro-enxofre, ferritinofagia, remodelamento de fosfolipídios poli-insaturados e autofagia seletiva em células mieloides e parenquimatosas.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A análise estabelece um modelo estritamente dependente de contexto e composto: em doses fisiológicas ou moderadas, o eixo do itaconato sustenta SLC7A11/GPX4 e defesas antioxidantes que suprimem a ferroptose e limitam a lesão tecidual aguda, distinguindo ações célula-autônomas em macrófagos/micróglia da transferência parácrina para células endoteliais e parenquimatosas. Em contrapartida, exposições farmacológicas elevadas a derivados eletrofílicos específicos podem inverter o fenótipo e disparar ferroptose dependente de ferritinofagia.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Dialoga diretamente com duas frentes centrais do LUCHM: a ferroptose microvascular endotelial e ativação microglial na malária cerebral (PbA/C57BL/6J) e a peroxidação lipídica induzida por ferro/hemo livre, alertando para não extrapolar ensaios com 4-octil-itaconato como equivalentes diretos do itaconato endógeno.

43075943.titulo: Applying functional MRI analysis techniques to whole-brain calcium-imaging data to investigate structural and functional relationships in Drosophila melanogaster
43075943.autores: Okuno T, Woodward A, … Hata J (4 autores)
43075943.resumo: Aplica pré-processamento de fMRI a dados de cálcio de cérebro inteiro de Drosophila e os cruza com conectomas FlyEM/FlyWire; a correlação conectividade funcional × estrutural cai com o número de regiões e neurônios com sinapses não segregadas contribuem mais para a conectividade funcional.
43075943.resumo_original: Clarifying the relationship between structure and function is important for understanding the brain. In Drosophila melanogaster, FlyEM and FlyWire electron microscopy-based connectome data, and whole-brain calcium-imaging data are available. We applied pre-processing methods from functional magnetic resonance imaging to whole-brain calcium-imaging data and comprehensively investigated the optimal parameters. Then, we found that the FC-SC (functional and structural connectivity) correlation decreased linearly with region of interest count, and this trend was the same in flies and humans. We also developed a new, more robust method to quantify the degree of pre- and post-synaptic segregation, and investigated this in the fly whole-brain. This revealed that many neurons have unsegregated synapses. We extracted highly unsegregated synapses and compared them with random-extracted null SC matrices. Their FC-SC correlation was significantly higher, indicating that these synapses contribute to FC well. Conversely, highly segregated synapses showed significantly lower FC-SC correlation and contribute less to FC. Neurons with unsegregated synapses, like non-spiking neurons, are spread throughout the whole-brain, and they are thought to have a significant influence on FC.

43081641.titulo: Dietary Hercynine Protects Intestinal Stem Cell Function During Epithelial Repair and Aging Through Insulin Signaling.
43081641.autores: Zhang Q, Fu F, … Chen H (10 autores)
43081641.resumo: A hercinina protege células-tronco intestinais de Drosophila no reparo e no envelhecimento via sinalização de insulina; a microbiota remodelada parece resposta acompanhante, não causa.
43081641.resumo_original: Intestinal stem cell (ISC) dysfunction compromises epithelial repair and contributes to intestinal aging, yet naturally derived metabolites that preserve ISC homeostasis remain incompletely defined. Through metabolomic profiling of a standardized edible mushroom extract, we identified hercynine (HER) as the most abundant detected metabolite and investigated its role in intestinal repair and aging. In Drosophila, HER accelerated post-injury epithelial repair by promoting timely restoration of ISC/progenitor dynamics and epithelial differentiation. During physiological aging, mid-life HER supplementation preferentially attenuated age-associated ISC/progenitor dysfunction, accompanied by improved intestinal homeostasis, enhanced organismal fitness, and extended lifespan. Mechanistically, HER shifted aged ISC/progenitor transcriptomes toward a more youth-associated state, with genetic and pharmacological pathway-perturbation experiments supporting the functional involvement of insulin signaling in HER-mediated improvements in aged ISC/progenitor homeostasis. HER was also associated with remodeling of the gut microbiota during injury repair and aging; microbiota perturbation experiments suggested that this remodeling represented an accompanying response to HER treatment rather than the primary driver of ISC protection. In aged human small intestinal organoids, HER improved budding capacity, ISC/progenitor-associated activity, and epithelial differentiation, while reducing p-AKT levels, supporting a conserved epithelial response in a mammalian model. Together, these findings identify HER as a mushroom-derived metabolite that supports ISC-centered intestinal epithelial repair and mitigates intestinal aging, highlighting dietary metabolites as potential modulators of stem cell-associated epithelial homeostasis during tissue repair and aging.

43077227.titulo: Krüppel regulates cell cycle exit and limits adult neurogenesis of mushroom body neural progenitors in Drosophila.
43077227.autores: Chen D, Man J, … Kimata Y (7 autores)
43077227.resumo: Em Drosophila, Krüppel regula a saída do ciclo celular e a eliminação dos neuroblastos do corpo pedunculado; sua depleção prolonga a vida dos neuroblastos e permite neurogênese adulta, via Imp, com Kr-h1 antagonizando Kr.
43077227.resumo_original: Neural progenitors typically exit the cell cycle during development, limiting adult neurogenesis. Here, we identify Krüppel (Kr) as a regulator of cell cycle exit and elimination of mushroom body neuroblasts (MBNBs) in Drosophila. Neuroblast (NB)-specific Kr RNAi and the Irregular facet (KrIf-1) mutation prolong MBNB lifespan and enable continued adult neurogenesis. Despite low post-embryonic expression, pupal stage-specific Kr depletion or misexpression causes MBNB retention, revealing a role distinct from its established embryonic function. Persistent MBNBs retain the early temporal factor IGF2 mRNA-binding protein (Imp) and fail to fully induce the late temporal factors Syncrip (Syp) and Eip93F (E93). Imp co-depletion suppresses MBNB retention following Kr depletion, identifying Imp as a key downstream effector. Krüppel homolog 1 (Kr-h1), a hormone-responsive transcription factor, functionally antagonises Kr by suppressing E93 expression. Kr-h1 knockdown partially rescues MBNB retention caused by Kr depletion, whereas its overexpression drives tumour-like NB overgrowth. Together, these findings identify Kr as a lineage-specific regulator coordinating the Imp/Syp transition and E93 expression to promote timely MBNB termination. This work reveals how temporal regulators control neural progenitor lifespan and restrict adult neurogenesis, linking intrinsic developmental programmes with hormone-responsive pathways in the Drosophila brain.

resumo_blocos.racional: Progenitores neurais tipicamente encerram o ciclo celular durante o desenvolvimento para restringir a neurogênese adulta. Os autores investigaram como o fator transcricional Krüppel (Kr) coordena a saída do ciclo celular e a eliminação programada dos neuroblastos do corpo cogumelar (MBNBs) no cérebro de Drosophila.

resumo_blocos.resultados: A perda de função de Kr (por RNAi, mutação KrIf-1 ou depleção pupal — distinta da função embrionária) prolongou a sobrevida dos MBNBs e manteve neurogênese adulta contínua. Neuroblastos persistentes retiveram o fator temporal precoce Imp (IGF2 mRNA-binding protein) e falharam em induzir plenamente os fatores tardios Syp e E93; a co-depleção de Imp suprimiu essa retenção. Além disso, Kr-h1 antagonizou funcionalmente Kr ao reprimir E93, sendo que o knockdown de Kr-h1 resgatou parcialmente a retenção de MBNBs enquanto sua superexpressão promoveu hiperproliferação tumoral.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Esclarece a integração entre fatores temporais intrínsecos (Imp/Syp/E93) e sinalização hormonal (Kr-h1) na plasticidade neural de dípteros, relevante para compreensão do neurodesenvolvimento e remodelamento cerebral de vetores.

43073441.titulo: Helical repeat protein mRSiC is required for rRNA fragment accumulation in T. gondii mitochondria.
43073441.autores: Drakoulis N, Maschmann S, … Tetzlaff S (12 autores)
43073441.resumo: A proteína de repetição helicoidal mRSiC é necessária para o acúmulo de fragmentos de rRNA na mitocôndria de Toxoplasma gondii (EMBO Rep).
43073441.resumo_original: Myzozoans, including apicomplexan parasites Plasmodium falciparum and Toxoplasma gondii, possess unusual mitochondrial genomes that only encode two to three respiratory chain subunits and extensively fragmented rRNAs forming a divergent mitoribosome. Heptatricopeptide repeat (HPR) proteins are expanded in myzozoans, with some functioning as mitoribosomal constituents. Additional HPR proteins have been proposed to function in post-transcriptional mitochondrial gene expression, though their specific roles remain unexplored. We present a phylogenetic analysis of HPR proteins that reveals extensive lineage-specific expansions, consistent with diversifications of mitochondrial gene expression systems within myzozoans. We further characterize mRSiC, a HPR found in T. gondii and its closest relatives. Using sRNA sequencing and RNA gel blot analyses, we show that mRSiC is required for the stabilization of two lineage-specific mitochondrial sRNAs, RNA33 and RNA42. Loss of mRSiC causes rapid depletion of these RNAs, followed by secondary reductions of rRNA fragments, defects in the respiratory chain, and impaired parasite proliferation. Together, these findings highlight the importance of HPRs in apicomplexan mitochondrial gene expression and illustrate how lineage-specific RNA-binding factors support highly derived mitochondrial expression systems.

resumo_blocos.racional: Parasitos apicomplexos como Plasmodium falciparum e Toxoplasma gondii mantêm genomas mitocondriais minimalistas que codificam apenas duas a três subunidades da cadeia respiratória e rRNAs extensivamente fragmentados montados em um mitorribossomo divergente. O trabalho investigou como proteínas com repetições heptatricopeptídicas (HPR) expandidas em myzozoários sustentam essa expressão gênica mitocondrial pós-transcricional.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Análise filogenômica comparativa de proteínas HPR em myzozoários seguida de caracterização funcional da proteína mRSiC em Toxoplasma gondii por sequenciamento de pequenos RNAs (sRNA-seq), Northern/gel blot de RNA, ensaios de cadeia respiratória e proliferação parasitária.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A filogenia revelou expansões linhagem-específicas de proteínas HPR acompanhando a diversificação dos sistemas de expressão mitocondrial em myzozoários. Em T. gondii, a perda de mRSiC provocou rápida depleção de dois pequenos RNAs mitocondriais linhagem-específicos (RNA33 e RNA42), seguida por redução secundária dos fragmentos de rRNA, defeitos na cadeia respiratória e comprometimento severo da proliferação do parasito.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Ilustra mecanismos altamente divergentes de estabilização de sRNAs e rRNAs fragmentados mitocondriais em apicomplexos, apontando vulnerabilidades moleculares conservadas em família HPR também expandida em Plasmodium.

43065052.titulo: Advancing a tool for Aedes aegypti breeding-site surveillance: validation of manual identification of trash and tires on unmanned aerial imaging
43065052.autores: Woo KE, Tarpenning MS, … Rosser JI (13 autores)
43065052.resumo: Validação de identificação manual de lixo e criadouros para vigilância de Aedes aegypti.
43065052.resumo_original:
Trash accumulations and discarded tires can retain water and may provide habitat for Aedes aegypti, but the reproducibility of identifying and classifying these features from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery has not been established.
We evaluated manual trash mapping in two Kenyan settings, Ukunda and Kisumu. Raters delineated visible trash polygons on high-resolution UAV orthomosaics and assigned categories using a seven-category scheme and a collapsed three-group scheme (low-risk trash, high-risk trash, and tires). Classification agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha. Spatial inter-rater and intra-rater consistency were evaluated from polygon overlap and unique area metrics.
Pairwise inter-rater agreement for classification was strong (mean unweighted Cohen's kappa = 0.80, 95% CI 0.75-0.86; mean weighted kappa = 0.80, 95% CI 0.61-0.97). Three-rater Fleiss' kappa was 0.80 (95% CI 0.77-0.83) and increased to 0.90 (95% CI 0.87-0.93) for the collapsed risk groups. Standard and fuzzy Krippendorff's alpha values were 0.76 (95% CI 0.71-0.81) and 0.94 (95% CI 0.91-0.96), respectively. Spatial analyses showed overlap in major trash areas but meaningful differences in detection and boundary placement. Intra-rater feature-specific unique area ranged from 4.7 to 18.5%; pooled across all seven features, unique area was 31.1% (95% CI 29.8-32.4).
Manual interpretation of UAV imagery is reproducible for image-based identification and classification of visible trash and tires, particularly for visually distinctive features such as tires. The method measures potential habitat proxies rather than confirmed Aedes aegypti breeding productivity; entomological ground validation remains necessary. Standardized annotations may also support future automated image classification approaches.

43083739.titulo: Transcriptomic and Metabolomic Remodeling of the Cockroach Brain Following Envenomation by Parasitoid Wasp Ampulex compressa.
43083739.autores: Miroliubov A, Lianguzova A, … Libersat F (6 autores)
43083739.resumo: Transcriptoma e metabolômica do cérebro de Periplaneta americana 24 h após envenenamento por Ampulex compressa: 331 genes diferenciais, sinalização aminérgica alterada e aumento de ácido fumárico e sorbitol.
43083739.resumo_original: The parasitoid jewel wasp Ampulex compressa induces prolonged hypokinesia in its cockroach host, Periplaneta americana, by injecting venom into the central nervous system. Although acute behavioral effects are well characterized, molecular processes associated with persistent hypokinesia remain poorly understood. We combined transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics to characterize brain changes 24 h after envenomation. RNA-seq of the central brain region containing the central complex and adjacent tissue identified 331 differentially expressed genes: 267 upregulated and 64 downregulated. Increased expression of tyrosine decarboxylase-like and arrestin-domain genes, together with reduced expression of a putative tyramine/octopamine receptor, suggests altered regulation of aminergic signaling. Changes in synaptic vesicle and innexin transcripts further implicate chemical and electrical synaptic function. Immune, detoxification, and extracellular-matrix genes were also affected. Independent metabolomic analyses revealed significant increases in fumaric acid and sorbitol, consistent with altered energy metabolism. Tyramine, octopamine, glutamate, and GABA showed no significant differences after multiple-testing correction, although several showed greater inter-individual variation in stung cockroaches. Together, these findings identify changes in neuromodulatory signaling, synaptic organization, and metabolic support as candidate processes associated with persistent hypokinesia. Their contributions to behavioral suppression remain to be distinguished from downstream responses to reduced neural activity and tissue stress.

43078171.titulo: Beyond taste: internal nutrient sensing and endocrine roles of selected insect gustatory receptors.
43078171.autores: Zhang W, Sun J, Mang D (3 autores)
43078171.resumo: Revisão das funções fisiológicas de receptores gustativos em sensoriamento interno de nutrientes, como Gr43a em Drosophila e BmGr9 em Bombyx, incluindo sinalização endócrina e proliferação hematopoiética.
43078171.resumo_original: Gustatory receptors (GRs) are best known for detecting chemicals that influence insect feeding and behavior. Studies of selected receptors, predominantly sugar-responsive GRs, have also established roles in internal nutrient sensing and physiological regulation. Fructose-responsive receptors such as Drosophila melanogaster Gr43a and Bombyx mori BmGr9 illustrate how internal carbohydrate availability can influence feeding, endocrine signaling, and hematopoietic proliferation. Other sugar-responsive GRs have been implicated in gut peptide hormone signaling and metabolic regulation. Here, we examine the experimental evidence for these functions and distinguish established receptor-specific mechanisms from broader hypotheses concerning the GR family. We discuss how structural biology, single-cell approaches, and comparative functional studies can define the distribution and mechanisms of physiological GR functions. These findings motivate a framework connecting chemical sensing with internal physiological state, while their generality across GR lineages and contribution to ecological adaptation remain open questions.

43072727.titulo: Malaria and the Coagulation System: A Narrative Review
43072727.autores: Rolling T, Langer F, … Rolling CC (4 autores)
43072727.resumo: Revisão sobre hemostasia na malária grave: citoaderência de PfEMP1 a CD36, ICAM-1, trombomodulina e EPCR, liberação de fator de von Willebrand com déficit relativo de ADAMTS13, papel dúbio das plaquetas (lesão vascular e morte parasitária via PF4) e fator tecidual. Não recomenda anticoagulação adjuvante de rotina.
43072727.resumo_original: Malaria is a major global infectious disease, with Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) accounting for most severe and fatal cases. Severe malaria is also a disorder of the microvasculature in which parasite sequestration, endothelial activation, platelet responses, and coagulation pathways interact. During the erythrocytic stage, infected red blood cells express P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1, enabling cytoadherence to endothelial receptors such as CD36, ICAM-1, thrombomodulin, and the endothelial protein C receptor. This promotes microvascular sequestration, tissue hypoxia, and organ dysfunction, including cerebral and placental malaria. Endothelial activation is accompanied by marked release of von Willebrand factor and relative deficiency of ADAMTS13 activity, leading to accumulation of ultra-large von Willebrand factor multimers that support platelet adhesion, infected erythrocyte bridging, and microvascular obstruction. Platelets have context-dependent roles: they contribute to thrombocytopenia, vascular plugging, and cerebral pathology, but may also mediate antiparasitic immunity through platelet factor 4-dependent parasite killing. More recently, anti-platelet factor 4/polyanion antibodies and antiphospholipid antibodies have been implicated in malaria-associated platelet activation, anemia, and potentially microthrombosis. Tissue factor expression by endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, and infected placental tissue further links inflammation to fibrin deposition and severe organ manifestations. Clinically, this manifests as thrombocytopenia, prolonged coagulation profiles, and potential disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Because routine adjunctive anticoagulation is not recommended, management remains strictly focused on rapid antiparasitic therapy and supportive care. This review summarizes current concepts of hemostatic dysfunction in malaria and highlights unresolved questions regarding targeted modulation of coagulation pathways.

resumo_blocos.racional: A malária grave por Plasmodium falciparum constitui simultaneamente uma patologia microvascular e tromboinflamatória em que o sequestro eritrocitário, a ativação endotelial, a resposta plaquetária e a cascata de coagulação se retroalimentam na gênese da malária cerebral e placentária.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão narrativa mecanística integrando dados clínicos e experimentais sobre citoaderência mediada por PfEMP1 a receptores endoteliais (CD36, ICAM-1, trombomodulina e receptor endotelial de proteína C/EPCR), cinética de multímeros ultragrandes do fator de von Willebrand (UL-vWF) frente à protease ADAMTS13, expressão de fator tecidual, função dual de plaquetas via fator plaquetário 4 (PF4) e anticorpos anti-PF4/poliânions.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A ocupação de EPCR e trombomodulina por eritrócitos infectados compromete a via anticoagulante da proteína C ativada, enquanto a liberação endotelial maciça de vWF somada à deficiência relativa de ADAMTS13 acumula multímeros UL-vWF que ancoram plaquetas e eritrócitos parasitados, obstruindo capilares cerebrais. Paralelamente, anticorpos dirigidos contra complexos PF4/poliânions e fosfolipídios amplificam a ativação plaquetária, trombocitopenia e deposição de fibrina induzida por fator tecidual, explicando por que anticoagulantes clássicos inespecíficos falham clinicamente devido ao risco hemorrágico.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Cria uma ponte conceitual imediata entre os programas de Malária Cerebral e de Polifosfato Inorgânico do LUCHM: como o polifosfato liberado por parasitos e plaquetas é um poliânion fisiológico potente que interage com PF4, fator XII e vWF, esse eixo pode modular diretamente a microtrombose na BHE.

43076420.titulo: Advances in Chikungunya Fever Prevention and Control: Antiviral Therapeutics, Vaccine Development and Integrated Intervention Strategies
43076420.autores: Yu Y, Li J, … Shen C (9 autores)
43076420.resumo: Revisão sobre prevenção e controle de chikungunya: antivirais, vacinas e estratégias integradas de intervenção.
43076420.resumo_original: Chikungunya fever (CHIKF) is an acute mosquito-borne disease caused by chikungunya virus (CHIKV). Driven by globalization, climate change and expanding vector habitats, its geographic range continues to widen; in 2025 it produced the largest outbreak ever recorded in China, with more than 25,800 locally transmitted cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities of Guangdong. Beyond acute fever, rash and arthralgia, a substantial proportion of patients develop chronic arthritis, which accounts for much of the disease burden. This review summarizes the etiological features, life cycle, epidemiology and ongoing evolution of CHIKV, and critically evaluates progress in antiviral drugs and vaccines, together with vector control, microbiome-based approaches and One Health governance. No specific antiviral has yet been approved: compounds targeting viral entry, RNA capping, protease activity and genome replication inhibit CHIKV selectively in cell culture but remain at preclinical or early clinical stages, and host-directed agents are further constrained by host toxicity. Two vaccines are now licensed-the live-attenuated vaccine Ixchiq, whose use has been progressively restricted following post-marketing safety signals, and the virus-like particle vaccine Vimkunya-while inactivated, chimeric, viral-vectored and mRNA candidates remain earlier in development. For all countermeasures, whether the envelope substitutions carried by recently emerged strains, including E2-L210Q and E2-I211 T within the immunodominant domain B, will erode protection remains experimentally unresolved. Collectively, CHIKV control still faces the absence of approved antivirals, incompletely defined long-term vaccine safety and breadth, and ongoing vector population expansion. Future work should prioritize broad-spectrum antivirals and next-generation vaccines, promote multidisciplinary collaboration, and strengthen integrated governance under the One Health framework.Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT07555392..Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06669208..

resumo_blocos.racional: Impulsionado pela expansão geográfica de mosquitos Aedes e mudanças climáticas, o vírus Chikungunya (CHIKV) protagonizou em 2025 o maior surto já registrado na China (> 25.800 casos autóctones em Guangdong), mantendo elevada carga de artrite crônica sem antivirais específicos aprovados.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Revisão crítica abrangendo epidemiologia molecular recente do CHIKV, candidatos antivirais pré-clínicos e clínicos (inibidores de entrada, capeamento de RNA, protease nsP2, replicação genômica e fatores do hospedeiro), desempenho e segurança pós-comercialização das vacinas licenciadas (atenuada Ixchiq e VLP Vimkunya), mutações emergentes no envelope E2 e estratégias integradas baseadas em microbioma vetorial.

43066962.titulo: Estimating Culex species (Diptera: Culicidae) flight range: meta-analysis
43066962.autores: Moore TC, Sedda L, … Brown HE (4 autores)
43066962.resumo: Metanálise de 206 experimentos (57 estudos) sobre distância média de voo de Culex: Cx. tarsalis 1.404 m; Cx. tritaeniorhynchus 347 m; Cx. quinquefasciatus 302 m; Cx. pipiens 283 m.
43066962.resumo_original: Mosquitoes of the genus Culex transmit arboviruses of public health importance, including West Nile and Japanese encephalitis viruses. Dispersal, commonly measured as mean distance traveled (MDT), influences transmission dynamics and spatially targeted surveillance and control. However, Culex flight-distance estimates vary substantially because of differences in study design, environmental context, and analytical methods. We systematically synthesized empirical flight data and evaluated environmental and methodological factors associated with MDT across Culex species. A systematic literature review through December 2025 identified 206 experiments from 57 studies spanning 15 countries. MDT was estimated using nonweighted, capture-weighted, and inverse-variance weighted approaches. Multivariable generalized linear and mixed-effects models were applied to Culex tarsalis Coquillett, Cx. quinquefasciatus Say, Cx. pipiens L., and Cx. tritaeniorhynchus Giles, adjusting for study designs. Of 206 experiments, 119 were included in species-specific MDT estimations. Capture-weighted MDT was greatest for Cx. tarsalis (1,404 m; 95% CI: 865-2,281), followed by Cx. tritaeniorhynchus (347 m), Cx. quinquefasciatus (302 m), and Cx. pipiens (283 m). Study area radius was most consistently associated with estimation of the MDT, whereas recapture efficiency was inversely associated with the MDT. Environmental and methodological factors, including mosquito origin, release timing, temperature, and infrastructure, showed species-specific effects. Capture-weighted models produced more precise and stable estimates than inverse-variance approaches. These findings indicated that ecological and methodological factors influenced estimated Culex dispersal and emphasized the importance of accounting for study design when interpreting MDT. Species-specific estimates can improve spatial targeting of vector surveillance and control and inform arbovirus transmission models.

43066963.titulo: Field video recording reveals how temperature and season influence Culex quinquefasciatus (Diptera: Culicidae) oviposition activity
43066963.autores: Méndez-Cardona S, Schluep S, … Thongsripong P (4 autores)
43066963.resumo: Gravação de vídeo em campo de Culex quinquefasciatus mostra efeito de temperatura e estação sobre o comportamento.
43066963.resumo_original: Understanding vector behaviors under natural field conditions is essential for refining targeted control strategies. Culex quinquefasciatus Say is an important vector of West Nile virus, yet fine-scale field oviposition dynamics across changing temperatures and seasons remain understudied, partly due to a lack of field monitoring tools. In this study, we developed an infrared video monitoring method that can be paired with oviposition traps. We deployed this monitoring system during summer and fall in coastal Florida to quantify the timing and duration of individual oviposition events relative to sunset and ambient temperature. Egg rafts were collected and reared to confirm species identity. Culex quinquefasciatus oviposition activity was concentrated within the early scotophase in both seasons. However, temporal patterns differed between sampling periods: summer oviposition was broadly dispersed across multiple hours of the night, whereas oviposition during the cooler fall occurred within a narrower window following dusk. Temperature was associated with oviposition behavior, with higher temperatures significantly associated with a greater frequency of observed oviposition events and shorter oviposition durations. Our findings demonstrate that the infrared video monitoring system can detect natural oviposition events in nighttime field conditions. We also found that oviposition dynamics vary with seasonal changes in temperature and sunset timing under natural field conditions. By identifying periods when gravid females are most actively visiting oviposition sites, these findings may help inform the timing of surveillance and targeted vector control activities such as adulticide applications during high-risk arboviral transmission periods.

43065368.titulo: The chromosomal genome sequence of the malaria mosquito, Anopheles oryzalimnetes Wilkerson & Motoki, 2009
43065368.autores: Sallum MAM, Bergo ES, … Lawniczak MKN (10 autores)
43065368.resumo: Genoma cromossômico de Anopheles oryzalimnetes (178,36 Mb, 3 pseudomoléculas) do Anopheles Reference Genomes Project.
43065368.resumo_original: We present a genome assembly from an individual female Anopheles oryzalimnetes (Arthropoda; Insecta; Diptera; Culicidae). The primary assembly has a total length of 178.36 megabases. Most of the primary assembly (99.39%) is scaffolded into 3 chromosomal pseudomolecules, including the X sex chromosome. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled, with a length of 15.42 kilobases. This assembly was generated as part of the Anopheles Reference Genomes Project.

43074439.titulo: Environmental Factors Display Multiple Associations with West Nile Virus Risk Modeling in Kansas
43074439.autores: Hinojosa I, Smith E, … Mulcahy ER (5 autores)
43074439.resumo: No Kansas, sete anos de casos humanos e equinos de WNV foram integrados a vigilância de Culex, cobertura do solo e índices climáticos; a abundância de Culex teve associação monotônica com casos em defasagem de 3 semanas, sem relação linear nos modelos de regressão.
43074439.resumo_original:
West Nile virus (WNV) persists as a significant vector-borne disease in the United States, yet risk prediction frameworks vary widely across the Midwest and often rely on sparse case data or limited mosquito surveillance. These challenges are amplified by the asymptomatic nature of WNV infection. Incorporating publicly available environmental and landscape variables-such as temperature, precipitation, drought indices, and land cover-may offer a more robust and scalable foundation for regional WNV risk assessment.
Seven years of human and equine WNV case data were integrated with Culex mosquito surveillance records, county-level land cover, and weekly temperature, precipitation, and drought indices for the state of Kansas. Mosquito abundance from 26 unique trapping sites was assessed using annual regression models, and case occurrence was evaluated using zero-inflated negative binomial models. Site-level trend assessments examined ecological patterns in relation to precipitation, drought, and habitat composition.
Lagged temperature and drought severity were the most stable environmental indicators of case occurrence, supported by trend-level contrasts between drought and nondrought seasons. Landscape composition shaped mosquito responses to precipitation and moisture availability. Although Culex abundance showed a significant monotonic association with WNV cases at a 3-week lag, regression models did not detect a linear relationship.
Publicly available, routinely updated, and geographically resolved environmental indicators can support a scalable WNV risk assessment framework. This study represents the first integration of these environmental, landscape, and surveillance factors for Kansas and provides a foundation for future work incorporating viral testing of mosquito pools, finer-scale land use data, and more consistent trap placement to strengthen predictive capacity.
