43083678.titulo: Hybrid Epidemiological-Neural Modelling of Dengue Under Climate-Socioeconomic Influence.
43083678.autores: Adeniji A, Mahmood A, … He Z (4 autores)
43083678.resumo: Modelagem híbrida epidemiológico-neural de dengue sob influência climática e socioeconômica.
43083678.resumo_original: Dengue transmission in climate-sensitive and socioeconomically heterogeneous settings arises from nonlinear interactions between environmental suitability, mosquito ecology, and human behaviour. Classical SEIR-type models offer mechanistic interpretability but are often constrained by observational noise and incomplete data, while purely data-driven approaches typically fail to respect underlying transmission dynamics. In this study, we introduce a hybrid epidemiological framework that embeds a temperature-unemployment driven SEIR-SEI model within a Physics-Informed Neural Network (SEIR-PINN). Using weekly dengue incidence data from Medellín, Colombia, we incorporate unemployment as a socioeconomic proxy that modulates transmission alongside climatic suitability. The Model performance was evaluated in two ways; the prediction of observed incidence, the SEIR-PINN achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 15.05 and R2 of 0.975, compared with MAE of 43.57 and R2 of 0.870 for a mechanistic SEIR-SEI baseline fitted under identical climatic and socioeconomic assumptions. Shuffled five-fold cross-validation provided held-out prediction of observed incidence within the 2009-2011 period, with mean MAE of 14.87 and mean R2 of 0.977 (out-of-fold MAE 14.89, R2 0.978). These held-out results interpolate within the observed epidemic and are not an assessment of prospective forecasting performance Importantly, the SEIR-PINN reconstructs latent human and mosquito compartments that remain biologically consistent across epidemic phases. By fusing mechanistic structure with data-adaptive flexibility, the proposed SEIR-PINN provides an interpretable framework for analysing the joint climatic and socioeconomic modulation of dengue transmission in an urban endemic setting. Although using Medellín as a single-city methodological case study, application of this framework to other dengue endemic settings requires external validation using additional locations, longer time periods, and independent datasets. The results therefore support the potential use of physics-informed hybrid models as interpretable tools for dengue surveillance and transmission-dynamics research, while recognising the need for further external validation across longer time periods and additional geographical regions.

43077045.titulo: Mosquito Population Dynamics Across Successive Gonotrophic Cycles: A Structured Multiscale Mathematical Approach.
43077045.autores: Nforba GDY, Teboh-Ewungkem MI, Ngwa GA (3 autores)
43077045.resumo: Modelo multiescala estruturado da dinâmica populacional de mosquitos ao longo de ciclos gonotróficos sucessivos.
43077045.resumo_original: We develop a structured multiscale mathematical model for mosquito population dynamics that explicitly links gonotrophic-cycle processes to population-level demographic outcomes across multiple reproductive cycles. The model couples breeding-site movement, resting, oviposition, density-dependent recruitment, mortality, human biting, and repeated reproductive cycling, thereby quantifying contributions of mosquitoes that survive to complete multiple cycles. As a first step toward understanding the role of gonotrophic cycling in mosquito-borne disease transmission, we focus on mosquito demography, with the human population held at demographic equilibrium. We characterize the steady states of the model and their stability, derive a basic offspring number governing mosquito persistence, and investigate bifurcation behaviour and parameter sensitivity. The results show that incorporating additional gonotrophic cycles increases reproductive contributions and can qualitatively alter persistence predictions. Parameter regimes yielding extinction with one or two cycles can support persistence when a third cycle is included, while additional cycles can shift stable populations into oscillatory regimes at lower oviposition rates. Shortening the gonotrophic cycle can further promote persistence under low oviposition and modestly alter oscillation frequency and amplitude at higher oviposition. Sensitivity analysis identifies early gonotrophic-cycle processes, particularly first-cycle oviposition, successful blood feeding, and breeding-to-questing progression, as dominant regulators of the basic offspring number. More generally, oviposition, breeding-to-questing movement, biting, successful blood feeding, and return rates positively influence the basic offspring number, whereas stage-specific mortality acts negatively; the effects of later-cycle parameters are increasingly weighted by successful progression through preceding cycles. These results demonstrate that explicitly representing successive gonotrophic cycles can materially change predicted mosquito persistence, stability, and potential control targets.

43083672.titulo: Insecticide Resistance in Anopheles stephensi: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Native and Invasive Populations.
43083672.autores: Eshetu D, Gadisa E, … Yan G (10 autores)
43083672.resumo: Revisão sistemática e metanálise de resistência a inseticidas em Anopheles stephensi, em populações nativas e invasoras.
43083672.resumo_original:
The rapid spread of the invasive malaria vector Anopheles stephensi in Africa, coupled with increasing reports of insecticide resistance, presents an emerging challenge for malaria vector control. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to compare insecticide resistance profiles and underlying resistance mechanisms between native Asian and invasive African populations and assessed their implications for insecticide resistance management.
PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, WHO IRIS, and gray literature sources were searched using terms related to An. stephensi, insecticide susceptibility, and resistance mechanisms. Data were extracted into Excel, critically appraised using an adapted Joanna Briggs Institute checklist, and analyzed using Comprehensive Meta-analysis software. The protocol was registered in Prospero International Registrar for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis in April 2025 (ID: CRD420251007131).
Thirty-one studies published between 2000 and 2025 were included. Pooled mortality was lower in invasive than native populations for the pyrethroids assessed in both ranges, including deltamethrin (72.6% vs. 83.5%), permethrin (68.3% vs. 89.0%), and lambda-cyhalothrin (47.0% vs. 87.0%), as well as for DDT (36.0% vs. 47.7%). Mortality was also lower in invasive populations for bendiocarb and propoxur, although propoxur was assessed in only one native-range study. Between-study heterogeneity varied substantially. Target-site mutations were reported at low frequencies; L1014F ranged from 1.4% to 32.9% in native populations and was detected in one study in invasive-range (5.7%), while L1014S (21.4-35%) was reported only in native-range. Metabolic resistance mechanisms involved cytochrome P450s (CYP4 and CYP6 families), glutathione S-transferases (GSTe2 and GSTe4), and esterases, including esterase E4 and carboxylesterase-6. No acetylcholinesterase-1 (ace-1) mutations were reported.
Anopheles stephensi exhibits resistance to multiple insecticide classes across its native and invasive ranges, with lower pooled mortality observed in the invasive range. Available evidence indicates an important contribution of metabolic detoxification, while target-site resistance markers, including vgsc L1014F/L1014S, were detected at lower frequencies and remain poorly characterized in invasive populations. High between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation and highlights the need for standardized phenotypic and molecular surveillance to guide locally tailored insecticide resistance management as An. stephensi continues to spread in Africa.

resumo_blocos.racional: A rápida invasão urbana do vetor de malária Anopheles stephensi na África, somada a relatos crescentes de resistência a inseticidas, ameaça o controle da malária em áreas urbanas e periurbanas. Esta revisão sistemática com metanálise comparou perfis de resistência e mecanismos moleculares entre populações nativas asiáticas e populações invasoras africanas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Busca sistematizada (protocolo PROSPERO CRD420251007131) em PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, WHO IRIS e literatura cinzenta, avaliada por checklist adaptado do Joanna Briggs Institute e analisada no software Comprehensive Meta-analysis, reunindo 31 estudos publicados entre 2000 e 2025.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A mortalidade combinada foi menor nas populações invasoras africanas do que nas nativas asiáticas para deltametrina (72,6% vs. 83,5%), permetrina (68,3% vs. 89,0%), lambda-cialotrina (47,0% vs. 87,0%) e DDT (36,0% vs. 47,7%), além de bendiocarbe e propoxur, com elevada heterogeneidade entre estudos. Mutações de sítio-alvo em vgsc ocorreram em baixa frequência — L1014F variou de 1,4% a 32,9% nas nativas (5,7% em um estudo invasor) e L1014S (21,4%–35%) restringiu-se a nativas, sem relatos de mutações em ace-1 — ao passo que a resistência metabólica envolveu citocromos P450 (CYP4 e CYP6), GSTe2, GSTe4 e esterases (E4 e carboxilesterase-6).

10.64898/2026.11.24.767905.titulo: Population genomics of the Anopheles farauti complex reveals a distinct regime of malaria vector evolution in the southwest Pacific
10.64898/2026.11.24.767905.resumo: Preprint de genômica populacional do complexo Anopheles farauti, com um regime distinto de evolução de vetor de malária (não revisado por pares; só título lido).
10.64898/2026.11.24.767905.resumo_original: Abstract: The southwest Pacific has one of the highest per-capita malaria burdens outside Africa, yet how its malaria mosquitoes evolve is largely unknown. In African vectors, insecticide resistance evolves rapidly in large, connected populations carrying abundant standing variation. Southwest Pacific vectors show little to no biochemical resistance despite decades of insecticide-based control. We analyse 495 genomes from six taxa of the Anopheles farauti complex, which includes the region's major vectors. The complex radiated rapidly in the late Pleistocene concomitant to the peopling of Near Oceania. Thereafter, post-glacial sea-level rise and climate change fragmented its populations into recently colonised island isolates. Successive environmental and colonisation bottlenecks left a legacy of extraordinary inbreeding, most marked in island populations of the coastal specialist An. farauti sensu stricto, where sustained low effective population size has allowed deleterious alleles to be purged effectively; the inland generalists An. hinesorum and An. oreios retain more variation. After five decades of chemical control we recover a single resistance sweep, at Gste2, alongside recent selection at species-specific chemosensory gene repertoires. Severe inbreeding and the loss of standing variation have not prevented ecological success, challenging assumptions about how much variation and connectivity a vector population needs to thrive. This work establishes the first genomic foundation for this major vector system of endemic species through a biogeographically diverse region of the world.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora o Pacífico Sudoeste concentre algumas das maiores taxas per capita de malária fora da África, seus vetores do complexo Anopheles farauti exibiram pouca ou nenhuma resistência bioquímica após décadas de controle químico, em forte contraste com vetores africanos altamente polimórficos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Análise populacional genômica de 495 genomas abrangendo seis táxons do complexo Anopheles farauti, reconstruindo radiação biogeográfica, gargalos demográficos insulares, níveis de endogamia, purga de alelos deletérios e varreduras seletivas após cinco décadas de pressão por inseticidas.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O complexo radiou rapidamente no Pleistoceno tardio concomitantemente ao povoamento da Oceania Próxima, sofrendo fragmentação insular pela elevação pós-glacial do nível do mar. Gargalos sucessivos geraram endogamia extraordinária no especialista costeiro An. farauti s.s. — permitindo purga eficaz de alelos deletérios sob baixo tamanho populacional efetivo — enquanto os generalistas continentais An. hinesorum e An. oreios retiveram maior diversidade. Após cinco décadas de controle químico, emergiu apenas uma varredura de resistência em Gste2, ao lado de seleção recente em repertórios gênicos quimiossensoriais espécie-específicos.

43083682.titulo: Overcoming Dengue Underreporting: A Machine Learning Framework for Automated Dengue Notification Based on Electronic Medical Records.
43083682.autores: Sornsurin W, Suwannik W, … Ingsrisawang L (5 autores)
43083682.resumo: Framework de aprendizado de máquina para notificação automatizada de dengue a partir de registros eletrônicos, contra a subnotificação.
43083682.resumo_original: Hospital notification of dengue cases is frequently delayed, contributing to underreporting. At Thai provincial hospitals the bottleneck is administrative, not diagnostic: delayed discharge coding and clerical steps mean notifications are submitted late or omitted. Existing machine learning (ML) studies require clinician-annotated features absent in passive electronic medical records (EMRs). We propose a dual-pathway EMR framework for ML-based pre-population of surveillance reports. We analyzed 1031 dengue-suspected encounters (508 notifiable) from Surin Hospital, Thailand (2019-2022). Pathway A combines EMR data with manually documented clinical features; Pathway B uses only passive EMR data. Using an 80/20 stratified split, we tested 7 ML methods across 11 feature sets (77 combinations) with SHAP-guided feature elimination and 10-fold cross-validation. On the primary split, Pathway A (CatBoost) achieved an F1 score of 96.62%, 95.10% sensitivity, and 98.10% specificity (10-seed mean F1 95.7% ± 1.4%). Pathway B (LightGBM) achieved an F1 score of 84.42%, 94.12% sensitivity, 75.24% specificity, and a projected negative predictive value of 99.1% at 10% prevalence; 10-seed performance was lower (F1 78.5% ± 4.3%; sensitivity 89.1%). An exploratory LSTM-16 stacking model (F1 83.99%; precision 79.49%) performed best in precision and specificity among Pathway B. Test F1 SD across 10 seeds was ≤5.0% in 75 of 77 combinations. Within this cohort, passive EMR modeling achieved 91-94% sensitivity on the primary split (85-89% across seeds) without additional data collection, supporting the feasibility of ML-based notification in resource-constrained hospitals. Whether this reduces dengue underreporting must be established in prospective, multi-center studies.

10.64898/2026.11.20.768024.titulo: Needle in a haystack: Fluorescence-guided 3D targeting for FIB milling in high-pressure-frozen samples
10.64898/2026.11.20.768024.autores: Koczy O, Tollervey F, … Mattei S (6 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.20.768024.resumo: Preprint: direcionamento 3D guiado por fluorescência para FIB milling em amostras congeladas sob alta pressão.
10.64898/2026.11.20.768024.resumo_original: Rare subcellular structures are difficult to retain during lamella preparation for cryo-electron tomography, particularly in high-pressure-frozen specimens. Here we introduce two complementary workflows for three-dimensional fluorescence-guided milling on a commercial cryo-focused ion beam-scanning electron microscope with integrated fluorescence imaging. Iterative fluorescence correlation uses repeated rounds of imaging and milling to refine the target position, whereas bidirectional fluorescence correlation images a lifted-out block from two orthogonal directions. We validated both by targeting centrosomes in waffle-frozen early Caenorhabditis elegans embryos, each of which occupy approximately 0.007% of the embryo volume. We recovered recognizable centrosomes in 83% and 67% of lamellae examined by transmission electron microscopy, respectively, compared with 25% using a refined, 2D-guided high-throughput SOLIST workflow, run as a benchmark. Neither method requires hardware modification or fluorescent fiducial beads. These workflows provide accessible strategies for targeting rare subcellular structures during lamella preparation, with or without a lift-out hardware.

43063711.titulo: Advances toward high-throughput and accurate mosquito age prediction using surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) and artificial neural networks (ANNs)
43063711.autores: Gao Z, Wu X, … He L (15 autores)
43063711.resumo: Predição de idade de mosquitos por espectroscopia Raman amplificada por superfície.
43063711.resumo_original: Accurate mosquito age estimation is critical for vector surveillance and targeted disease intervention. In this study, we present a rapid, standardized sample preparation workflow combining 70% ethanol extraction, bead disruption, surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), and artificial neural networks (ANNs) for predicting mosquito age. Solvent screening on 18-day-old mosquitoes established 70% ethanol as the optimal extraction medium. Across mosquitoes aged 3, 10, and 18 days, parallel bead disruption consistently yielded higher peak prominence-to-noise ratios than sequential sonication, markedly improving spectral definition. Crucially, parallel bead homogenization processed 12 specimens in 45 s compared to 12 min with sequential sonication, a 16-fold increase in disruption throughput. Initial spectrum-level ANN classification achieved 86.0% accuracy for a 3-age Aedes aegypti dataset (Thailand-origin; TH-origin), 92.7% for a 5-age Culex tarsalis dataset, and 84.2% for a 7-age Ae. aegypti dataset (Lakewood). Corresponding regression models demonstrated high predictive accuracy, with Pearson correlation coefficients (R) of 0.95-0.99 and root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 1.60-3.58 days. Further evaluation using three ordered hold-out splits with mosquito-level majority voting confirmed robust performance across multiple age classes. This streamlined workflow supports efficient batch preparation and accurate spectroscopic age prediction, providing a foundation for future field validation.

43069879.titulo: Accurate identification of medically important Aedes mosquito species using low-cost imaging and geometric wing morphometrics
43069879.autores: Sauer FG, Jöst H, … Lühken R (8 autores)
43069879.resumo: Identificação de espécies de Aedes por imagem de baixo custo e morfometria geométrica de asa.
43069879.resumo_original: Accurate species identification is crucial to assess the medical and veterinary relevance of a mosquito specimen, but it requires high taxonomic expertise of the respective organism group and well-equipped laboratories. This study aimed to evaluate whether low-cost imaging in combination with geometric wing morphometrics can provide accurate identification of invasive, morphologically similar Aedes species. The right wings of 670 female specimens covering 184 Ae. aegypti, 156 Ae. albopictus, 166 Ae. j. japonicus and 164 Ae. koreicus, were dissected, mounted and photographed using a professional stereomicroscope (Olympus SZ61; Olympus, Tokyo, Japan) with a macro lens (Apexel-24XMH; Apexel, Shenzhen, China) attached to a smartphone (iPhone SE 3rd Generation; Apple Inc., Cupertino, CA, USA). The coordinates of 18 landmarks on the right wings were digitalized by a single observer for each image. In addition, the landmarks of 20 randomly selected specimens per species and imaging device were digitalized by six different observers to assess the degree of the observer error. The superimposed shape variables were used to compare the species classification accuracy of linear discriminant analysis (LDA), support vector machine (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and XGBoost. In the single-observer landmark data, the LDA achieved the best classification results with a mean accuracy of 95% for landmarks from microscope images and 92% for those obtained from smartphone images. In the multi-observer landmark data, the reduction in the accuracy was more pronounced for smartphone images than for microscope images. This pattern was associated with a higher degree of observer error for smartphone images, as confirmed by a landmark-wise comparison across all landmarks. Geometric wing morphometrics provides a reliable method to distinguish the most common invasive Aedes species in Europe. Thereby, smartphones equipped with a macro lens provide adequate image quality and represents a cost-effective alternative to professional microscopes. However, due to the greater degree of observer variation for smartphone images, landmark coordinates for such images should ideally be collected by a single observer.

10.64898/2026.11.18.767690.titulo: Genomic Epidemiology of Dengue Virus in Ivory Coast Reveals Five Decades of Viral Circulation with Repeated Introductions from Burkina Faso
10.64898/2026.11.18.767690.autores: Tao X, Kadjo HA, … Trovao NS (7 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.18.767690.resumo: Preprint: epidemiologia genômica do dengue na Costa do Marfim, cinco décadas de circulação.
10.64898/2026.11.18.767690.resumo_original: Dengue fever is a rapidly emerging mosquito-borne disease in Africa, yet the continent remains critically underrepresented in genomic surveillance efforts. This disparity is especially pronounced in West Africa, despite phylogenetic studies being concentrated in only a few countries, such as Burkina Faso. Within this broader regional gap, researchers have yet to systematically characterize the dengue virus (DENV) lineages circulating in the Ivory Coast. In this study, we present 24 newly sequenced DENV genomes from Ivory Coast, spanning serotypes DENV-1, DENV-2, and DENV-3, collected between 2017 and 2023. Combined with publicly available sequences, we assembled the most comprehensive dataset to date for the country. We performed maximum-likelihood and Bayesian phylogeographic analyses using global background datasets and reconstructed the spatial and temporal dynamics of dengue virus circulation in Ivory Coast. Our findings reveal multiple independent introductions of DENV into Ivory Coast, predominantly from neighboring Burkina Faso. We identify five introductions of DENV-1 between 2017 and 2019 and four introductions of DENV-2 between 2015 and 2016. DENV-3 showed two separate introductions, one in 2015 and another in 2018. Notably, we also identified an early DENV-1 introduction from India around 1977, suggesting long-distance historical viral movement likely linked to colonial and post-colonial military presence. These results underscore the need for sustained genomic surveillance to monitor viral evolution and inform regional public health responses aimed at controlling dengue outbreaks in West Africa.

10.64898/2026.11.19.767973.titulo: Origin tracing and detection lag in the first Aedes albopictus invasion of mainland Australia and a long-term genomic dataset of mosquito incursions
10.64898/2026.11.19.767973.autores: Schmidt T, Muzari O, … Ehlers G (6 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.19.767973.resumo: Preprint: rastreamento de origem e lag de detecção da primeira invasão de Aedes albopictus na Austrália continental.
10.64898/2026.11.19.767973.resumo_original: Proactive management of invasive species aims to prevent and eradicate new incursions before they establish. Genomic data can assist proactive management around how to deploy resources and when to change strategies, and has been used effectively in managing Aedes albopictus (Asian tiger mosquito) in the Australian Northern Peninsula Area over the past decade. This study characterises the first major incursion of Ae. albopictus on the Australian mainland, and contrasts this with long-term genomic monitoring of this species within the Torres Strait Islands (TSI). First, we genomically traced the mainland incursion, which was detected in Cape York, Queensland, to the nearest infested island, Muralug (Prince of Wales). Strong genetic drift patterns in the incursion are suggestive of recent inbreeding, and point to a lag between incursion and detection of at least two mosquito generations. This stands in stark contrast with incursions within the TSI, which showed no evidence of inbreeding, suggesting no detection lag in the TSI. We genomically traced n=63 incursions detected in the TSI between 2019-2026, including n=44 newly sequenced samples; this used an expanded reference databank containing samples from one island, Muralug, that had not been available in previous tracing. Including Muralug greatly improved tracing success from ~50% to 77.8-92.1%. We observed no reduction in tracing success when whole genome and reduced representation sequencing datasets were combined in analysis, indicating composite approaches are viable. Together these findings demonstrate the value of genomic databanks for long-term incursion monitoring, provided these capture a sufficient proportion of genetic variation.

43069037.titulo: Chikungunya virus dynamics and persistence in body fluids-Nanning, Guangxi Province, China, 2025
43069037.autores: Chen Y, Liang C, … Xu B (7 autores)
43069037.resumo: CHIKV em 506 amostras de 53 pacientes de Nanning (2025): soro 81,2% positivo, saliva 11,0%; positividade na saliva cai de 52,2% (dia 1) a 0,7% (dia 7).
43069037.resumo_original:
In 2025, China experienced its largest outbreak of Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), an acute infectious disease transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. This study aims to analyze the dynamic changes, developmental trends, and persistence of CHIKV in body fluids, based on infection data collected from Nanning, China.
A total of 506 specimens were longitudinally obtained from 53 hospitalized patients in Nanning, China. Positivity rates among different specimen types were compared using the Chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, while the Kruskal-Wallis test was applied to evaluate differences in cycle threshold (Ct) values. To estimate the probability of viral detection, generalized estimating equations (GEE) were employed, and parametric survival analysis was conducted to examine the duration of viral persistence in human body fluids.
Serum had the highest positivity rate (81.20%), followed by plasma (72.50%), while urine (4.73%) and saliva (11.03%) were much lower. In the first four days following the onset of symptoms, the median Ct values for serum and plasma were lower compared to those for saliva and urine. According to GEE analysis, saliva showed the quickest decline in the likelihood of a positive test result, decreasing from 52.2% on day 1 to just 0.7% by day 7. Serum and plasma followed, with positivity rates dropping from over 85% on day 3 to around 30% by day 7. Urine consistently had low positivity rates and did not show a statistically significant relationship with the number of days since symptoms began. Parametric survival analysis indicated similar median durations of serum (5.8 days, 95% CI: 4.8-6.9) and plasma (5.8 days, 95% CI: 4.7-7.1), while saliva had a shorter median duration of 3.5 days (95% CI: 3.0-4.1). Urine was not included in this analysis due to an insufficient number of positive samples.
Blood is the preferred sample for detecting the chikungunya virus and accurately assessing the duration of the virus in the body; additionally, compared to urine, saliva is more sensitive for detecting the virus during the acute phase of the disease, which is important for subsequent transmission and public health control measures.

43065791.titulo: The critical role of N-glycosylation in mediating arbovirus-host interactions
43065791.autores: Wang L, Zhou H, … Zhao L (12 autores)
43065791.resumo: Revisão do papel da N-glicosilação de proteínas virais na replicação, tropismo, competência vetorial e escape imune de arbovírus (ZIKV, DENV, WNV, JEV).
43065791.resumo_original: Glycosylation is a major post-translational modification that regulates protein folding, stability, trafficking, and recognition in biological systems. During viral replication, many viruses exploit host glycosylation machinery to modify their own proteins and thereby shape virus-host interactions. Among the major forms of protein glycosylation, N-linked glycosylation has a particularly important role in viral glycoprotein folding, virion assembly, receptor engagement, membrane fusion, tissue tropism, vector competence, and immune evasion. Current studies have revealed diverse functions of viral protein glycosylation in the infection processes of several pathogens, including Zika virus, dengue virus, West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, duck Tembusu virus, tick-borne encephalitis virus, and other medically or veterinary important arboviruses. Here, we review the biological significance of N-glycosylation in mediating interactions between arboviruses and their hosts, with emphasis on conserved mechanisms, virus-specific glycosylation sites and their contributions to viral replication, pathogenesis, host adaptation and immune escape. We also discuss unresolved questions and potential applications of glycosylation-targeted strategies in antiviral research and vaccine development.

10.64898/2026.11.18.767689.titulo: CsrA-dependent RNA accessibility landscapes prioritize new mRNA and sRNA targets and link CsrA to polyphosphate homeostasis
10.64898/2026.11.18.767689.autores: Buchser R, Taylor K, … Contreras LM (8 autores)
10.64898/2026.11.18.767689.resumo: Preprint: CsrA e paisagens de acessibilidade de RNA ligam CsrA ao metabolismo de polifosfato em bactéria (avaliado só pelo título).
10.64898/2026.11.18.767689.resumo_original: The global RNA-binding protein CsrA (Carbon Storage Regulatory Protein A) regulates diverse physiological processes in Gammaproteobacteria, but the full set of RNAs through which it actuates and how they intersect with small RNA (sRNA) regulation and stress physiology remain incompletely defined. We asked how CsrA shapes RNA accessibility across 431 untranslated mRNA regions and 87 sRNAs in Escherichia coli. Using a previously published RNA accessibility profiling method (INTERFACE), we compared wild type and CsrA mutant (csrA::kan) strains. Permissive screening for accessibility peaks at GGA/AGA motifs nominated 87 5'UTRs, 32 3'UTRs and 28 sRNAs as candidate responsive RNAs but did not pass a permutation null (p=0.43), however it can be used to guide selection of candidates for validation. Eleven 5'UTRs had no prior experimental evidence, and all 3'UTRs and most sRNAs were nominated manually because of limited probe numbers in these targets. In reporter assays, six of nine RNAs tested showed CsrA-dependent expression (mdtE, ribB, patA, metC, ppk and proS) including three candidate activated-targets, although only two of five reporters from the primary candidate list responded. CsrA bound the sRNAs SsrA and RalA in vitro, and reporter assays suggested CsrA-dependent modulation of previously identified ArrS-ribB and GcvB-crp interactions. Mutating sequence elements in the ppk 5' UTR altered CsrA-dependent expression, and loss of CsrA-activity was associated with reduced polyphosphate and fewer Hfq-containing HP-bodies during nitrogen starvation. Together, these findings expand the CsrA regulon and its overlap with sRNA networks, and support accessibility profiling to prioritize RNA-binding protein targets for follow-up characterization.

43083857.titulo: Oropouche fever in a changing tropical world: emergence, diagnostics and surveillance preparedness for India.
43083857.resumo: Febre Oropouche num mundo tropical em mudança: emergência, diagnóstico e preparo de vigilância na Índia.
43083857.resumo_original: Oropouche virus (OROV) is an emerging arthropod-borne virus causing Oropouche fever. OROV is transmitted predominantly by the biting midge Culicoides paraensis. Although historically confined to South America, imported cases have been reported, highlighting its expanding geographic range and global public health relevance. Currently, there are no commercially available diagnostic assays for laboratory confirmation of OROV infection. In addition, no specific antiviral therapy or licensed vaccine is available. The recent emergence of cases outside traditional endemic areas further emphasizes the urgent need to address critical knowledge gaps. This review critically synthesizes current evidence on OROV virology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum and diagnostic challenges. We further contextualize OROV within the Indian setting, where competent Culicoides vectors are present, and discuss the importance of incorporating OROV into targeted surveillance and travel-related screening frameworks to facilitate early detection, reduce diagnostic misclassification and strengthen one-health preparedness in regions currently considered non-endemic.

43078151.titulo: An Anti-diabetic drug Liraglutide inhibits Zika Virus Infection by Suppressing AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis.
43078151.autores: Chiu TJ, Lu TW, … Lee JC (8 autores)
43078151.resumo: A liraglutida inibiu ZIKV em cultura (IC50 5,5 ± 0,6 µM), prolongou a vida de camundongos AG129 e reduziu a viremia cerca de 15 vezes, via AMPK/TORC2 e redução de enzimas gliconeogênicas.
43078151.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection is a global health-threatening illness that causes severe neurological complications, including microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome. Currently, no approved antiviral therapeutics or vaccines are available for treating ZIKV infections. Using cell-based and mouse experiments, we evaluated the antiviral efficacy of liraglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist clinically used to treat diabetes by reducing hepatic glucose production, on viral replication, cell viability, and host metabolic signaling pathways. We found that liraglutide exhibited significant antiviral activity in a dose-dependent manner, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 5.5 ± 0.6 μM for viral RNA replication suppression, without cytotoxicity at the effective concentration. Furthermore, liraglutide treatment extended the lifespan of ZIKV-infected AG129 mice and achieved an approximately 15-fold reduction in viremia. Mechanistically, liraglutide enhanced 5' adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation and then increased the phosphorylation of transducer of regulated CREB activity protein 2 (TORC2), thereby downregulating expression of rate-limiting gluconeogenic enzymes, specifically phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase and glucose-6-phosphatase. The antiviral activity of liraglutide was attenuated by both AMPK inhibitor Compound C and siRNA-mediated AMPK knockdown, supporting the claim that AMPK/TORC2-mediated gluconeogenesis contributes to liraglutide's anti-ZIKV activity. Given its clinical availability, liraglutide represents a promising therapeutic option for immediate repurposing for managing patients infected with ZIKV.

43082073.titulo: Cyclotides Enable the Oral Activity of Neuroactive Peptides against Lepidopteran Pests.
43082073.autores: Huang YH, Wang CK, … Craik DJ (23 autores)
43082073.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082073.resumo: Os ciclotídeos kalata B1 e B2 aumentaram de 2 a 3 vezes, de forma sinérgica, a eficácia oral de neurotoxinas de veneno contra lepidópteros; o mecanismo proposto é a ruptura seletiva da barreira do intestino médio, confirmada por microscopia.
43082073.resumo_original: Farmers face shrinking crop-protection options due to climate change, resistance, regulations, and demand for residue-free food. Peptides and proteins are attractive solutions because they are potent, specific, and degrade into harmless amino acids. Venom-derived peptide neurotoxins show strong potential as bioinsecticides, but their poor oral activity limits use in sprayable formulations. We show that plant cyclotides, kalata B1 and B2, dramatically enhance the oral efficacy of venom-derived neurotoxins against major lepidopteran pests. Their effects are synergistic, increasing activity by two to 3-fold beyond additivity, and in some cases, enabling complete mortality at doses where either component alone is ineffective. The proposed mechanism involves cyclotides selectively disrupt the lepidopteran midgut barrier, allowing neurotoxins to cross into the hemocoel and act on the nervous system. Microscopy confirms midgut damage, and the D-form of kalata B1 retains activity, indicating an achiral, lipid-mediated interaction. These results establish cyclotides as enablers of peptide-based bioinsecticides against selected important crop pests.

43064347.titulo: The Immune-Architectural Construction of Symbiont Niches in Insects
43064347.resumo: Revisão de Lemaitre e Li: a imunidade localizada constrói ativamente nichos de simbiontes (lúmen, criptas, bacterioma), incluindo mosquitos; três módulos: regulação imune, propriedades físico-químicas do nicho e coconstrução pelo simbionte.
43064347.resumo_original: Insects commonly harbor bacterial symbionts within diverse anatomical niches, including the gut lumen, midgut crypts, bacteriomes, and cuticular reservoirs. These specialized structures have long been viewed as passive containers, whereas immunity has been considered as means for host tolerance but not as a way of actively controlling symbiont populations. Here, we review studies on insect symbiont-niche formation, arguing that host anatomy and localized immunity are functionally inseparable components of a unified process of constructing a niche for symbionts. Drawing on comparative evidence from diverse insect systems -including flies, mosquitoes, tsetse flies, aphids, weevils, stinkbugs, bees, beetles, wasps, and others-, we present a framework integrating three primary modules: immune regulation and buffering, physicochemical niche properties, and symbiont-driven co-construction of the niche.

43068725.titulo: Beyond urban ecology and evolution: socio-eco-evolutionary dynamics in insects and the importance of scales
43068725.autores: Boullauazan Y, Govaert L, … Brans KI (4 autores)
43068725.resumo: Dinâmica socioecoevolutiva de insetos em ambientes urbanos e a importância das escalas (Curr Opin Insect Sci).
43068725.resumo_original: Urbanization drives rapid ecological and evolutionary change, creating opportunities for reciprocal feedback among insect phenotypes, ecological processes, and human societies. Yet, despite growing evidence for urban adaptation, empirical demonstrations of urban eco-evolutionary feedback remain rare, and their integration with societal processes is even less developed. Here, we review urban insect ecology and evolution through a socio-eco-evolutionary lens, focusing on pollinators, mosquitoes, and other indoor pests as particularly promising systems. Across these groups, urban environmental change can alter phenotypes through plasticity and evolution, with potential consequences for ecosystem services and disservices including pollination, biological control, pest outbreaks, and disease transmission. We propose a multiscale framework that separates but integrates biological organization, spatiotemporal extent, and urban scales. Phenotypic and evolutionary change can alter ecological processes and societal outcomes beyond the biological, urban, or spatiotemporal scale at which it arises, with resulting feedback propagating, dissipating, or being counteracted across scales. We introduce the concept of socio-eco-evolutionary hotspots, where phenotypic or evolutionary change meaningfully modifies ecological-societal feedback, and coldspots, where these feedback remain weak or fail to propagate. Linking urban insect eco-evolutionary dynamics to their societal consequences and governance scales provides a basis for identifying where biodiversity conservation, urban planning, pest management, and public-health interventions can most effectively shape urban socio-ecological outcomes.

43072147.titulo: Development of a novel osteotropic bone morphogenetic protein-2 carrier based on a polyphosphate diester
43072147.autores: Hirai H, Kaito T, … Iwasaki Y (10 autores)
43072147.resumo: Carreador de BMP-2 baseado em um polifosfodiéster sintético, poli(etileno fosfato de sódio) conjugado a colesterol, com afinidade por osso; inibe osteoclastogênese e favorece genes osteogênicos em células mesenquimais; fusão espinhal em 12 de 12 lados avaliados em seis ratos.
43072147.resumo_original: Autologous bone grafting remains the clinical gold standard for bone regeneration but is limited by donor site morbidity and reduced availability and quality in elderly patients. Recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) provides strong osteoinduction; however, its conventional collagen sponge carrier allows rapid release, resulting in dose-dependent adverse effects and high costs. To address these limitations, we developed a bone-targeted delivery system using cholesterol-conjugated poly (ethylene sodium phosphate) (CH-PEP·Na), a polyphosphate diester with high bone affinity and dual biological activity that suppresses osteoclastogenesis and enhances early osteogenic gene expression. CH-PEP·Na formed stable complexes with BMP-2 (CHP-BMP-2) that were resistant to proteolytic degradation and exhibited sustained adsorption to hydroxyapatite. In vitro, CHP-BMP-2 enhanced osteogenic gene expression and matrix mineralization in bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, while CH-PEP·Na inhibited osteoclast differentiation and showed reduced ERK phosphorylation in a single immunoblot experiment. In vivo, CHP-BMP-2 combined with allograft bone demonstrated prolonged fluorescence retention of labeled BMP-2, reduced bone resorption, and enhanced new bone formation compared with BMP-2 alone in a rat subfascial implantation model. Notably, in a posterolateral spinal fusion model, CHP-BMP-2-containing allografts achieved 100% fusion rates (12/12 evaluated sides in six rats) and generated high-density, trabecular-rich bone, whereas collagen sponge carriers produced bone of inferior structural quality. These findings demonstrate that CHP-BMP-2 enables spatially controlled delivery of BMP-2 via direct binding to bone graft surfaces. Clinically, this strategy may allow small amounts of autologous bone obtained during decompression procedures to function as a scaffold and growth factor depot, reducing BMP-2 dose, minimizing adverse effects and costs, and improving outcomes in spinal fusion and large-defect bone regeneration.

43082071.titulo: Trypsin-Mediated Control of Metabolic Flux Sustains Detoxification and Reproduction under Chronic Thermal Stress.
43082071.autores: Miao X, Chen B, … You S (6 autores)
43082071.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082071.resumo: Em Plutella xylostella, tripsinas do intestino médio, via CRISPR, são essenciais sob estresse térmico crônico: sustentam detoxificação e reprodução ao suprir aminoácidos.
43082071.resumo_original: Global warming and intensive insecticide use impose concurrent demands on pests, yet mechanisms coordinating resource allocation between stress responses and life-history traits remain poorly understood. We identify midgut trypsins as key regulators of this coordination in the diamondback moth, Plutella xylostella. Using CRISPR/Cas9, we show that two trypsin genes, PxTryCFT1-like and PxTry-like, are dispensable for acute thermal tolerance but essential under chronic stress. Mutant lines exhibit severe reproductive failure under prolonged high temperatures and display broad-spectrum hypersensitivity (2- to 22-fold) to multiple insecticides. Mechanistically, trypsin loss disrupts amino acid supply, suppressing major detoxification systems including cytochrome P450s, glutathione S-transferases, and carboxylesterases. By elucidating the noncanonical role of midgut trypsins in modulating trade-offs between growth and stress defense, we demonstrate how nutrient acquisition fuels stress-response networks.

43082084.titulo: FTZ-F1 Homologue Silencing Reveals Endocrine and Xenobiotic-Response Vulnerabilities Associated with RNAi-Insect Growth Regulator Co-Treatment in Heortia vitessoides.
43082084.autores: Wang H, Liu N, … Lin T (5 autores)
43082084.revista: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
43082084.resumo: Em Heortia vitessoides, o silenciamento de dois homólogos de FTZ-F1 prejudicou ecdise, pupação e emergência; um se associou a menos triglicerídeo no corpo gorduroso, o outro a ruptura do epitélio do intestino médio. dsRNA em quitosana combinado a reguladores de crescimento reduziu a sobrevivência em algumas combinações.
43082084.resumo_original: Insect growth regulators disrupt endocrine signaling, but the molecular vulnerabilities underlying their effects remain incompletely understood. Here, two FTZ-F1 homologues in Heortia vitessoides were characterized and functionally analyzed. RNAi-mediated knockdown of either homologue impaired ecdysis, pupation, and adult emergence. HvFTZ-F1-1 knockdown was more strongly associated with reduced fat-body triglyceride content and lipid-metabolism-related transcription, whereas HvFTZ-F1-2 knockdown was more strongly associated with midgut epithelial disruption, reduced ELISA-derived 20E immunoreactive levels, and broader transcriptomic perturbation. Pyriproxyfen and tebufenozide induced opposite transcriptional responses of the two homologues. Chitosan-dsRNA cotreatment produced combination-dependent survival responses, with CS-dsF1+Teb and CS-dsF2+PPF showing reduced survival relative to the corresponding pesticide-control groups. These findings identify homologue-biased developmental vulnerabilities and support a laboratory framework for RNAi-insect growth regulator cotreatment in H. vitessoides.

43082872.titulo: Virulence of Conidiobolus coronatus Against the Fall Webworm, Hyphantria cunea, and the Effect of Silencing a Host Cuticular Protein Gene on Larval Susceptibility.
43082872.autores: Bai F, Yang T, … Zhou X (7 autores)
43082872.resumo: Conidiobolus coronatus (LC50 204 conídios/mm²) contra Hyphantria cunea; o silenciamento de um gene de proteína cuticular por dsRNA oral reduziu a muda e acelerou a mortalidade após exposição ao fungo.
43082872.resumo_original: Conidiobolus coronatus is an entomopathogenic fungus with a broad insect host range. We examined the virulence of strain 20220622F, isolated from a naturally infected gall midge, against the invasive forest pest Hyphantria cunea (fall webworm). Bioassays against final-instar larvae yielded a median lethal concentration (LC50) of 204 conidia/mm2 at 96 h post-inoculation, with cumulative mortality reaching 75% at the highest inoculum density tested (351.3 conidia/mm2). Infected larvae showed transient changes in polyphenol oxidase and catalase activities, reactive oxygen species levels, and circulating hemocyte counts, together with apoptosis-related fluorescence at 24 h. Transcriptomic analysis identified differentially expressed genes associated with immune and cuticle-related functions. In third-instar larvae, feeding on dsRNA targeting the cuticular protein gene Hc.10517 reduced its expression by approximately 55% at 48 and 72 h, and this silencing was associated with developmental abnormalities and reduced moulting success. Following inoculation with 150 conidia/mm2, the dsHc.10517 group reached 100% mortality within 60 h, with a median survival time of 42 h (95% CI, 36-48 h). These laboratory results identify strain 20220622F as a candidate for the biological control of H. cunea and indicate that silencing Hc.10517 is associated with faster mortality following fungal exposure.

43081080.titulo: A larval salivary effector from a parasitoid wasp hijacks bacteria to kill host hemocytes.
43081080.autores: Song J, Yan Z, … Ye G (11 autores)
43081080.resumo: Uma proteína flagelar de origem bacteriana, transferida horizontalmente para vespas calcidoides, é expressa na saliva larval de Nasonia vitripennis, altera a microbiota do hospedeiro e, com Enterococcus faecalis, induz morte de hemócitos por perturbação do metabolismo da dopamina.
43081080.resumo_original: Salivary proteins are well characterized in herbivorous and blood-feeding insects but remain largely unexplored in parasitoid wasps. Here, we show that FlhE, a bacterial flagellar protein gene, was horizontally transferred from Herbaspirillum to chalcidoid wasps. The single-copy Nasonia vitripennis larval salivary flagellar protein FlhE (NvLSFlhE) is highly expressed in larval salivary glands and important for wasp development. Furthermore, we found that NvLSFlhE modulated the microbiota of host fly Sarcophaga peregrina, increased microbial diversity and specifically interacted with inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase (IMPDH) from Enterococcus faecalis (E. faecalis). This cooperative effect of NvLSFlhE and E. faecalis induced host hemocyte death by perturbing dopamine metabolism, with decreased cellular adenosine triphosphate levels and accumulation of cytotoxic 7-ketolithocholic acid. These findings reveal how a parasitoid larval salivary effector remodels host microbiota and shapes parasitoid-microbe-host interactions.

43080506.titulo: Host Availability and Host Contacts of Mosquitoes Using Environmental DNA.
43080506.autores: Balvers C, Visser TM, … Koenraadt CJM (7 autores)
43080506.resumo: Combina DNA do repasto, eDNA em pernas e eDNA do ar para estimar disponibilidade e contato de hospedeiros por mosquitos; Culex pipiens pipiens se alimentou mais em aves que as demais espécies.
43080506.resumo_original: Host availability is an important parameter when studying vector-borne diseases, especially in the case of opportunistic mosquito vectors. To study host feeding patterns of mosquitoes in the field, we integrated three sources of information: (1) host feeding, by identifying the origin of DNA in bloodmeals; (2) host contact, inferred from eDNA detected on mosquito legs; and (3) host availability, estimated via airborne eDNA using the frequency of host detection via airborne eDNA as a proxy for their relative abundance. At four field locations, we deployed Burkard 7-day spore traps next to BG-sentinel 2 traps to capture airborne eDNA and blood-fed mosquitoes, respectively. We found that mosquitoes caught on dairy farms fed most on the animal species that were most frequently detected by airborne eDNA. However, Culex pipiens pipiens fed significantly more on birds compared to Cx. p. molestus, Anopheles daciae, An. messeae and Culiseta annulata (p < 0.01), which fed more on mammals. Animal DNA on mosquito legs via direct contact could be detected, but results were inconsistent and prone to contamination, thereby limiting the use of mosquito legs to study host contacts. This study shows that airborne eDNA is a promising method to assess the presence, and to a certain extent also the relative abundance of vertebrate animal species as potential available hosts for mosquitoes. This method could ultimately provide better insights into the context dependency of host preference of opportunistic mosquito vectors.

43057226.titulo: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
43057226.autores: Wang G, Sun P, … Wang S (18 autores)
43057226.resumo: Em colônia de An. stephensi mantida a temperatura alta por 3 anos, surgiu uma deleção de 5 kb em timeless (tim-5kb). Machos heterozigotos mantêm period estável no calor, expressam mais AKH1 (mobilização de energia, voo) e FAR3/FAR5 (feromônio heptacosano) e ganham no acasalamento; fêmeas heterozigotas ficam mais suscetíveis a Plasmodium.
43057226.resumo_original: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim-5kb) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim+/-5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

resumo_blocos.racional: O mosquito transmissor de malária Anopheles stephensi invadiu a África e tem se adaptado rapidamente às altas temperaturas de ambientes urbanos, mas a base genética e fisiológica dessa termoadaptação e seu impacto sobre a transmissão parasitária permanecem pouco esclarecidos.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores identificaram e caracterizaram uma variante natural com deleção de 5 kb no gene do relógio circadiano timeless (tim-5kb), cuja frequência aumentou após três anos de manutenção de colônias em altas temperaturas de laboratório. Avaliaram-se a expressão do gene period em machos heterozigotos tim+/-5kb sob estresse térmico, a vantagem competitiva no acasalamento, a expressão do hormônio adipocinético (AKH1), a atividade de voo, a regulação de redutases de acil-CoA graxo (FAR3 e FAR5) na síntese do feromônio heptacosano e a susceptibilidade de fêmeas heterozigotas à infecção por Plasmodium.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Machos heterozigotos tim+/-5kb mantiveram expressão estável do gene period em temperaturas elevadas e conquistaram vantagem competitiva no acasalamento, mediada pela maior expressão de AKH1 — promovendo mobilização energética e atividade de voo — e pela ativação de FAR3 e FAR5, que elevaram a produção do feromônio heptacosano. Em paralelo, fêmeas heterozigotas apresentaram maior susceptibilidade à infecção por Plasmodium, ampliando o potencial de transmissão da malária.

43044585.titulo: Innate immune memory of past hepatic injury promotes ischemic cardiac inflammation.
43044585.autores: Zhang S, Zhang Y, … Zhan Z (13 autores)
43044585.resumo: Lesão hepática antiga reprograma de forma duradoura o sistema imune inato, desvia a diferenciação de células-tronco hematopoéticas para a linhagem mieloide e agrava a inflamação no infarto do miocárdio; a memória é transferível por transplante de medula e parabiose. O ácido palmítico do fígado lesado rearranja o metabolismo dos macrófagos cardíacos e fixa marcas epigenéticas em genes com motivo AP-1 (assinatura HepMem).
43044585.resumo_original: Hepatic disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular diseases, leading to worsened prognosis. However, the mechanisms of inter-organ communication and the impact of historical hepatic injury await elucidation. Here, we report that the historical liver damage triggers long-term reprogramming of the innate immune system, biases hematopoietic stem cells differentiation toward myeloid fate, and aggravates inflammatory injury during myocardial infarction (MI). This immune memory is transmissible in bone marrow transplantation and parabiosis models. Injured liver-derived palmitic acid is responsible for the metabolic rewiring of cardiac macrophages during memory formation and establishes persistent epigenetic signatures in the transcriptional regulatory regions of hepatic injury-associated memory ("HepMem") genes containing the activator protein-1 motif. The HepMem monocyte/macrophages are expanded in liver-injured mice and potentiate the post-MI inflammatory cascades and adverse cardiac remodeling. Therefore, the innate immune memory links the past hepatic injury with MI, guiding the promising therapeutic approaches for the inflammatory cardiac comorbidities.

43039802.titulo: Life-history trade-offs: the constraints underlying mosquito-borne pathogen transmission.
43039802.autores: Johnson B, Jacobs GR, … Murdock C (4 autores)
43039802.resumo: Perspectiva que propõe que sobrevivência, reprodução e imunidade do mosquito covariam por restrição de recursos (trade-offs), e que modelos de transmissão que tratam esses traços como independentes perdem previsões não intuitivas; a variação ambiental muda a alocação de recursos e, com ela, o potencial de transmissão.
43039802.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne pathogen transmission models typically assume that vector life-history traits vary independently. While survival, reproduction, and immunity are shaped by evolutionary forces to maximize fitness, life-history theory predicts that resource and physiological constraints create trade-offs among these traits. These trade-offs can shape pathogen development and transmission in nonintuitive ways. We argue that incorporating trade-offs into epidemiological and ecological modeling could improve predictive capacity for disease establishment and spread. Environmental variation alters resource allocation and, thus, trait covariation, so environmental variability may have cascading effects on transmission potential. This perspective unifies infection biology, local adaptation, vector-pathogen coevolution, invasion dynamics, and vector control under a common mechanistic framework to improve predictions of disease risk in a rapidly changing world.

43040049.titulo: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity.
43040049.autores: Michieletto MF, Jimenez MT, … Henao-Mejia J (33 autores)
43040049.resumo: Em camundongos, dieta hiperlipídica na gestação ou no início da vida pós-natal, mas não na vida adulta, remodela o perfil epigenético e transcricional de células T CD4 virgens e prejudica sua diferenciação em Tfh e a reação de centro germinativo após vacinas de mRNA e de proteína. O mecanismo central é a repressão epigenética de A20 (Tnfaip3); pacientes pediátricos com haploinsuficiência de A20 têm menos células T circulantes.
43040049.resumo_original: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

43044588.titulo: Microglial SUCNR1 senses metabolic state to regulate whole-body homeostasis.
43044588.autores: Repollés-de-Dalmau M, Asimakidou E, … Fernández-Veledo S (31 autores)
43044588.resumo: O succinato do líquor, dissociado do plasma, reflete o estado metabólico sistêmico, e a microglia é seu alvo principal no SNC via SUCNR1. A deleção de Sucnr1 na microglia deu resistência ao estresse metabólico por dieta rica em gordura e alterou a resposta à leptina e o comportamento de jejum/realimentação.
43044588.resumo_original: Peripheral metabolic cues influence central energy control through incompletely understood pathways. Succinate, a Krebs cycle-derived metabolite elevated during nutrient excess and inflammation, signals via the G protein-coupled receptor SUCNR1; however, its central nervous system (CNS) role remains poorly defined. Using integrated mouse, human, and cellular approaches, we investigated how the succinate-SUCNR1 axis regulates peripheral energy balance in normal and high-fat diet states. Cerebrospinal fluid succinate dynamics were dissociated from plasma levels yet reflected systemic metabolic status, supporting a distinct central succinate compartment dynamically associated with peripheral metabolic state. Multi-omic and functional analyses identified microglia as the principal CNS targets of succinate, characterized by high SUCNR1 expression and functional dependence on this signaling pathway. Microglial Sucnr1 deletion altered peripheral energy regulation, conferring resistance to diet-induced metabolic stress while disrupting physiological energy balance, including leptin responsiveness and fasting-refeeding behavior. These findings establish the microglial succinate-SUCNR1 axis as a key immuno-metabolic mechanism linking systemic metabolic signals to the hypothalamic control of energy homeostasis.

43043974.titulo: The effects of environmental temperature on the extrinsic incubation period of arboviruses in their mosquito vectors: A systematic review
43043974.autores: Hartner AM, Herath T, … Irrgang C (8 autores)
43043974.resumo: Primeira revisão sistemática de estudos de laboratório sobre temperatura e período de incubação extrínseco (EIP): 53 estudos, 17 arbovírus. Zika e vírus do Nilo Ocidental mostram maior eficiência de transmissão e EIP mais curto em temperaturas altas; para Sindbis e chikungunya não há tendência clara, por dados escassos, e vetores do mesmo vírus divergem muito, em parte por desenhos experimentais inconsistentes.
43043974.resumo_original:
Arboviruses are an increasing global public health concern, driven by both human and environmental factors. A key parameter shaping vectorial capacity for transmission is the extrinsic incubation period (EIP), the time required for a mosquito that has ingested an infectious blood meal to become capable of transmitting the virus via its saliva, which is strongly influenced by temperature. However, the temperature-EIP relationship remains poorly characterized across arboviruses and mosquito species.
We conducted the first systematic review of laboratory studies evaluating temperature effects on EIP across all reported mosquito-arbovirus pairings identifiable in the literature. We searched three databases and extracted data on infection and transmission efficiency (TE), applying a binomial generalized linear mixed-effects model to estimate the median extrinsic incubation period, the time post-infection at which 50% of infected mosquitoes become infectious.
Our synthesis included 53 studies covering 17 arboviruses. We found substantial heterogeneity in temperature effects on TE. Zika and West Nile viruses generally showed increased TE and shorter EIP at higher temperatures. However, similar trends based on published data were not clear for many viruses, such as Sindbis and chikungunya viruses, because of limited data granularity and small sample sizes. Even across different vectors of the same virus, findings varied widely, reflecting both biological differences and inconsistent experimental designs.
The findings revealed gaps in the understanding of the temperature effects on the EIP of arboviruses in mosquito vectors. Standardisation of reporting in vector competence experiments and expanded research on neglected viruses are urgently needed. Real-world environmental conditions should also be incorporated to improve modelling and support robust vector control and public health planning under changing climatic conditions.

43058765.titulo: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations.
43058765.autores: Piccinno R, Madec Y, … Malacrida AR (11 autores)
43058765.resumo: Populações de Ae. albopictus do Mediterrâneo têm ancestralidade heterogênea (introduções descontínuas e miscigenação). Essa ancestralidade explica diferenças de competência para CHIKV e DENV: populações vizinhas com ancestrais distintos diferem muito; populações distantes com mesma ancestralidade se parecem.
43058765.resumo_original:
Aedes albopictus is one of the world's most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. This study investigates whether and how the complex dynamics of these diverse genetic backgrounds have shaped variations in vector competence for CHIKV, DENV, and Zika (ZIKV) viruses.
Using highly polymorphic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers, we genotyped Ae. Albopictus samples from an ancestral population (Guangzhou, China) and ten adventive populations across five Mediterranean regions (Southern Switzerland, Northern/Central Italy, the Balkans, and Greece). Genetic ancestry and demographic histories were inferred using Bayesian STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) and DIYABC-RF. The association between population ancestry and vector competence for CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1, and ZIKV (PE243) was assessed using infection rate, dissemination efficiency, and transmission efficiency indices, analyzed via univariate and multivariate models.
Combining historical records with demographic models revealed that the establishment of Ae. Albopictus in the Mediterranean was driven by chaotic, discontinuous lineage introductions and admixture events, resulting in high spatial and ancestry heterogeneity. Notably, this genetic heterogeneity significantly influences vector competence, in particular for CHIKV and DENV. Interestingly, populations in neighboring geographical areas with distinct ancestries exhibited drastically different competence profiles, whereas geographically distant populations sharing genetic ancestry displayed similar vector competence for CHIKV and DENV.
Our findings demonstrate that the complex population dynamics and colonization history of Ae. Albopictus contributes to variation in vector competence, altering the geographical landscape of arboviral risk. These results underscore the urgent need for localized, geographically tailored vector control strategies in Europe, a region facing a rising trend of both imported and autochthonous arboviral infections.

resumo_blocos.racional: A invasão de Aedes albopictus na bacia do Mediterrâneo desde os anos 1980 envolveu múltiplas introduções descontínuas e mistura genômica entre linhagens. O estudo investigou se essa heterogeneidade de ancestralidade genética explica variações locais na competência vetorial para os vírus Chikungunya (CHIKV), Dengue (DENV) e Zika (ZIKV).
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Populações de Ae. albopictus de referência ancestral (Guangzhou, China) e de dez localidades adventícias em cinco regiões mediterrâneas (Sul da Suíça, Norte e Centro da Itália, Bálcãs e Grécia) foram genotipadas por marcadores microssatélites (SSR), inferindo-se ancestralidade e demografia via STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) e DIYABC-RF. A competência vetorial para CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1 e ZIKV (PE243) foi avaliada por taxas de infecção, eficiência de disseminação e eficiência de transmissão em modelos univariados e multivariados.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A reconstrução demográfica revelou colonização mediterrânea caótica e descontínua com intensa mistura gênica, gerando acentuado mosaico espacial de ancestralidade. Essa heterogeneidade genética modulou significativamente a competência vetorial sobretudo para CHIKV e DENV: populações geograficamente próximas com ancestralidades distintas diferiram fortemente em competência, enquanto populações distantes de ancestralidade compartilhada exibiram perfis semelhantes para CHIKV e DENV.

43021904.titulo: Optimized protocol for single-cell and bulk transcriptomic profiling of stabilized hemocytes frommosquitoes
43021904.autores: Saha B, McNinch CM, … Barillas-Mury C (3 autores)
43021904.resumo: Protocolo para estabilizar hemócitos de mosquito logo após a perfusão e sequenciá-los em célula única (10X) ou em bulk. A estabilização preserva o transcriptoma, permite guardar as amostras por até quatro semanas e recupera mais hemócitos, inclusive populações raras, que os métodos anteriores; prohemócitos menores que 5 μm ainda saem mal.
43021904.resumo_original:
Insect hemocytes play a crucial role in the innate immune response against pathogens. However, transcriptomic profiling and analysis of hemocytes in insect vectors, such as Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes, are challenging due to their small size, low RNA content, limited numbers, and highly reactive nature.
To address these challenges, we developed a protocol for single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing of stabilized hemocytes from adult female An. gambiae mosquitoes. Immediate stabilization of hemocytes following perfusion prevents transcriptional changes during sample collection and RNA degradation, thereby minimizing technical artifacts. After stabilization, hemocytes are filtered to remove contaminating tissue and ambient RNA introduced by tissue injury during sample collection, enriching for hemocyte-specific transcripts. The stabilized hemocytes can be stored for up to four weeks, allowing for convenient sample storage, transportation, and simultaneous processing of multiple samples, which reduces costs and minimizes batch effects.
Our single-cell RNA sequencing stabilization and processing protocol is compatible with the 10X Genomics platform, yielding high-quality and reproducible data. We demonstrate higher hemocyte recovery compared to other contemporary methods, enabling the identification of rare hemocyte populations. However, this protocol requires further optimization to increase the recovery of small-sized prohemocytes (< 5 μm in diameter). Our bulk mRNA stabilization and hemocyte enrichment protocol yields high-quality, intact RNA, and Illumina bulk mRNA sequencing libraries enable an in-depth investigation of gene expression changes in hemocytes. These protocols significantly improve transcriptomic analysis of hemocytes, which is critical for advancing discoveries in vector biology and disease control. Moreover, the protocol can be applied to other mosquito species and likely many other insects with only minor optimizations.

resumo_blocos.racional: Hemócitos circulantes de mosquitos vetores são efetores centrais da imunidade inata contra Plasmodium e arbovírus, mas sua análise transcriptômica enfrenta gargalos críticos: tamanho celular reduzido, baixíssimo conteúdo de RNA, número limitado de células por inseto e ativação transcricional instantânea durante o estresse da dissecção/perfusão.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Os autores padronizaram um protocolo de estabilização química imediata de hemócitos logo após a perfusão de fêmeas adultas de Anopheles gambiae, seguido de filtração seletiva para remover fragmentos teciduais e RNA ambiente decorrentes da injúria de coleta. As suspensões estabilizadas foram armazenadas por até quatro semanas antes do processamento em célula única (10X Genomics) ou em bibliotecas Illumina de RNA total (bulk mRNA-seq).
resumo_blocos.resultados: A estabilização imediata bloqueou alterações transcricionais induzidas pela coleta e degradacão de RNA, permitindo estocagem e transporte de lotes por até quatro semanas com redução de efeitos de lote. Na plataforma 10X Genomics, o fluxo recuperou mais hemócitos e subpopulações raras do que protocolos convencionais, mantendo como principal limitação a sub-representação de pró-hemócitos com diâmetro inferior a 5 μm.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Representa um ganho operacional imediato para o insetário do LUCHM ao viabilizar a coleta seriada de hemolinfa e hemócitos estabilizados de Aedes aegypti ou Anopheles após infecção ou repasto HFHS em dias distintos, enviando lotes consolidados para sequenciamento.

43008729.titulo: Plasmodium falciparum Hsp90 supports DNA replication
43008729.autores: Ibrasheva G, Chen Y, … Derbyshire ER (6 autores)
43008729.resumo: Dois inibidores de PfHsp90 quimicamente distintos reduziram 131 proteínas em comum no estágio sanguíneo de P. falciparum; 40% delas co-imunoprecipitam com PfHsp90 e a replicação de DNA foi a via mais enriquecida. A inibição reduz o conteúdo de DNA e a síntese de DNA nascente nos estágios sanguíneo e hepático e é sinérgica com inibidores de replicação.
43008729.resumo_original: Plasmodium falciparum heat shock protein 90 (PfHsp90) is an attractive antimalarial target, but the molecular pathways dependent on its activity remain poorly understood. Here, we use two chemically distinct Hsp90 inhibitors, geldanamycin and XL888, to profile the PfHsp90-dependent proteome during the blood stage. We identify 131 proteins reduced in abundance following both treatments, 40% of which co-immunoprecipitate with PfHsp90. DNA replication emerges as the most enriched pathway, and PfHsp90 inhibition reduces parasite DNA content and nascent DNA synthesis during blood- and liver-stage development. Combining Hsp90 inhibition with inhibitors of DNA replication further produces synergistic antiparasitic activity. Together, these findings establish a functional connection between PfHsp90 and parasite DNA replication and define a network of conserved and Plasmodium-specific proteins dependent on Hsp90 activity.

resumo_blocos.racional: A chaperona PfHsp90 de Plasmodium falciparum é um alvo antimalárico validado, mas faltava mapear quais complexos moleculares dependem diretamente de sua atividade nos estágios sanguíneo e hepático.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Proteômica quantitativa no estágio sanguíneo sob dois inibidores químicos distintos de Hsp90 (geldanamicina e XL888), co-imunoprecipitação (Co-IP) de clientes e ensaios de síntese nascente de DNA em fases eritrocítica e hepática.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Identificadas 131 proteínas depletadas por ambos os inibidores (40% co-imunoprecipitadas com PfHsp90), com forte enriquecimento em replicação de DNA; inibir PfHsp90 reduziu conteúdo de DNA, bloqueou síntese nascente e gerou sinergismo com inibidores de replicação.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Abre estratégia sinérgica para bloquear proliferação de Plasmodium combinando moduladores de proteostase (PfHsp90) e estresse replicativo em modelos celulares e murinos do LUCHM.

43036147.titulo: Temperature-dependent bloodmeal retention is associated with altered midgut ROS homeostasis in Aedes aegypti.
43036147.autores: Ferreira PG, Profeta CA, … Mendes TAO (9 autores)
43036147.resumo: Em Aedes aegypti mantidas a 20, 28 e 36 °C, a 20 °C a digestão do repasto é mais lenta e o sangue fica retido por mais tempo no intestino médio, com acúmulo sustentado de peróxidos solúveis e óxido nítrico e maior expressão de genes antioxidantes.
43036147.resumo_original: Temperature is a key environmental factor influencing mosquito physiology and vector competence, yet the mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly understood. Previous transcriptomic analyses of the midgut of Aedes aegypti maintained at different temperatures revealed differential expression of genes associated with blood digestion. Here, we investigated whether these transcriptional changes are accompanied by alterations in digestive enzyme activity, bloodmeal digestion kinetics, bloodmeal retention and midgut reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis. Mosquitoes maintained at 20°C exhibited delayed bloodmeal digestion and prolonged bloodmeal retention compared with those maintained at 28 and 36°C. Delayed bloodmeal digestion at 20°C was accompanied by sustained accumulation of soluble peroxides and nitric oxide, together with increased expression of antioxidant genes, indicating prolonged, temperature-dependent oxidative stress in the mosquito midgut. These findings suggest that cooler temperatures extend bloodmeal retention and prolong oxidative stress in the midgut, providing a physiological link between environmental temperature, digestive dynamics and redox homeostasis that may ultimately influence vector competence.

43038290.titulo: NF-κB/Dif-driven miR-1000 feedback restrains toll signaling via targeting Myd88 to restore Drosophila immune homeostasis
43038290.autores: Jia C, Li J, … Jin P (8 autores)
43038290.resumo: Em Drosophila, Dif (NF-κB) ativa miR-1000 após infecção por bactéria Gram-positiva, e miR-1000 degrada o mRNA de Myd88, fechando uma alça que encerra a sinalização Toll; no corpo gorduroso, romper o eixo prolonga a ativação de Toll e reduz a aptidão do hospedeiro na infecção.
43038290.resumo_original: Innate immune homeostasis is vital for animal survival and requires precise control of both the intensity and duration of immune signaling. Although microRNAs (miRNAs) are known to fine-tune immune responses, their transcriptional regulation mechanisms during infection remain poorly characterized. Here, we identify an NF-κB-dependent miRNA feedback loop essential for Drosophila Toll pathway. Through dynamic expression profiling and functional genetics, we demonstrate that the NF-κB transcription factor Dif directly activates miR-1000 transcription upon Gram-positive bacterial infection, while miR-1000 in turn targets the adaptor Myd88 mRNA for degradation. Moreover, we show that upon immune challenge, miR-1000 is significantly induced in the fat body, and fat body-specific manipulations confirm that Dif activates miR-1000 transcription and miR-1000 directly targets Myd88 in this key immune tissue. This dual function of Dif, concurrently inducing immune effectors (e.g., Drosomycin) and their suppressor miR-1000, establishes a self-limiting circuit: Dif/miR-1000/Myd88 axis. Crucially, miR-1000-mediated suppression of Myd88, the hub of Toll pathway, constrains signal transduction and enables timely termination. Disruption of this axis prolongs Toll pathway activation and compromises host fitness during infection. Furthermore, this miRNA-adaptor regulatory paradigm is evolutionarily conserved, as miRNAs targeting MyD88 (such as miR-155) also inhibit TLR signaling in mammals. Our work reveals a transcriptionally connected feedback mechanism that dynamically restores animal innate immune homeostasis by targeting a central signaling adaptor.
