43038963.titulo: Rapid spread of nutritional Wolbachia symbionts across and within solitary bee species
43038963.autores: Preuß L, Tischer M, … Gerth M (7 autores)
43038963.resumo: Wolbachia ocorre em até 60% das espécies de abelhas solitárias e o sucesso está associado a um cassete gênico de síntese de biotina (vitamina B7), raro em outras linhagens e comum nas de abelhas; linhagens com o elemento se espalharam de forma independente e recente por vários hospedeiros.
43038963.resumo_original: Maternally inherited, intracellular bacteria of the genus Wolbachia are extremely widespread among arthropods. Their evolutionary success is owed to frequent host shifts and rapid subsequent spread within host populations, often facilitated by Wolbachia-induced reproductive manipulations. Theory suggests that often, Wolbachia spread may also be explained by fitness benefits, the nature of which have remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that Wolbachia's success in many solitary bee species is strongly associated with the presence of a gene cassette enabling Wolbachia to synthesize biotin (vitamin B7). This ability is absent from almost all other Wolbachia strains but common among bee-associated strains. We show that Wolbachia occurs in up to 60% of all bee species and that strains carrying this rare genomic element have independently spread into numerous bee hosts recently. We further demonstrate that the presence of the biotin operon is associated with specialized diets in several bee species, suggesting a previously overlooked nutritional role of Wolbachia in this group of important pollinators. Overall, our results suggest that nutritional benefits provided by symbionts may represent a more widespread and important mechanism by which reproductive manipulators spread into new host species than previously appreciated.

10.64898/2026.11.13.766388.titulo: Improved long-read sequencing technology reveals full genome architecture of Malian Plasmodium falciparum field isolates
10.64898/2026.11.13.766388.resumo: Preprint: sequenciamento de leitura longa revela a arquitetura genômica completa de Plasmodium maliano. Só título e bloco lidos.
10.64898/2026.11.13.766388.resumo_original: Understanding genome plasticity in malaria parasites and the diversity of their repetitive gene families requires high-quality reference genomes derived from parasites recently isolated from patients. However, generating such genomes in Plasmodium falciparum remains challenging owing to the parasite's extreme AT content, extensive repetitive regions, and the frequent occurrence of multiclonal infections in endemic settings. As a result, most available reference genomes are derived from laboratory-adapted strains, that have experienced prolonged in vitro maintenance, and that incompletely represent natural parasite diversity. We developed and optimized a de novo assembly strategy based on PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and applied it to eight recently-isolated and cloned P. falciparum parasites from Mali. HiFi sequencing enabled highly accurate genome reconstruction, yielding assemblies with a mean of 18 contigs, 301 pseudogenes, and a frameshift rate of 0.04% following Liftoff annotation. Assemblies showed high structural integrity and near-complete chromosomes, including improved recovery of subtelomeric regions and multigene families, without requiring short-read correction. Despite overall conservation of chromosome organization, substantial variation was observed in chromosome-end architecture, subtelomeric structure, and telomeric repeat content among parasite genomes. Our approach simplifies the generation of high-quality P. falciparum genomes and reduces sequencing requirements fourfold. The resulting assemblies enabled characterization of natural variation in telomere plasticity and multicopy gene family diversity in field isolates. These findings establish PacBio HiFi sequencing as an effective and scalable strategy for producing highly contiguous and accurate de novo assemblies of P. falciparum, supporting the development of geographically-diverse, field-relevant malaria parasite reference genomes.

43033420.titulo: Genomic epidemiology of CHIKV during the largest outbreak in Mainland China - implication for CHIKV intervention.
43033420.autores: Yi L, Xiang S, … Lu J (13 autores)
43033420.resumo: Epidemiologia genômica de CHIKV no maior surto da China continental.
43033420.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) has caused recurrent epidemics across tropical and subtropical regions globally. In 2025, Guangdong, China, experienced the largest documented CHIKV outbreak in mainland China, with 23,464 reported cases across all 21 prefecture-level cities. We conducted integrated epidemiological, genomic, and phylodynamic analyses to investigate the outbreak's origins, transmission dynamics, and CHIKV lineage evolution. The Guangdong strain belongs to the East/Central/South African (ECSA) genotype, Middle African lineage (ECSA-MAL) - one of several CHIKV lineages co-circulating globally in 2025; a long internal branch separates ECSA-MAL from previously sequenced relatives, indicating substantial surveillance gaps in endemic regions. Phylodynamic analysis using a local molecular clock model estimated that the viral introduction occurred within a narrow window in early April 2025 (95% HPD: March 26-April 12), suggesting a 2.5-month period of cryptic transmission prior to detection. The prolonged silent phase aligns with vector dynamics: the Mosquito Ovitrap Index in the outbreak town of Beijiao, Foshan, stayed low in April (3.0) before surging to 9.0 through July - consistent with suppressed early transmission followed by seasonal amplification. Human migration from the two epidemic epicenters was moderately associated with the spatial distribution of cases (Spearman ρ around 0.5), while mosquito ecology may constrain spatial spread. Phylowave analysis on global circulating strains identified 33 lineage-defining mutations across 14 sublineages, concentrated in NSP3, E1 and E2. Four of these have been experimentally validated as adaptive mutations. This study demonstrates the critical need for enhanced genomic surveillance during pre-peak months and underscores the importance of monitoring adaptive mutations across diverse ecological regions.

43049708.titulo: Basophil FcεR1γ signaling regulates gut barrier integrity and systemic antibacterial immunity during malaria with a sex bias
43049708.autores: Céspedes N, Fellows AM, … Luckhart S (11 autores)
43049708.resumo: Camundongos com deleção de FcεR1γ em basófilos, infectados com a cepa 17XNL de Plasmodium, não mudam a parasitemia, mas as fêmeas têm mais permeabilidade intestinal no dia 6, menos bacteremia no dia 10, mais IL-6 e CCL4 no íleo e mais CCL3 e CCL5 no plasma.
43049708.resumo_original: Malaria predisposes individuals to concurrent bacteremia, a complication associated with increased intestinal permeability and mast cell (MC) activation. These effects correlate with elevated type-2 cytokines, including interleukin (IL)-3, IL-4, and IL-10. We previously demonstrated that basophils regulate MC activation and protect intestinal barrier integrity during malaria. Because FcεR1γ signaling is required for basophil IL-4 production, we monitored parasitemia, barrier integrity, bacteremia, and cytokine and chemokine profiles in male and female mice with basophil-specific deletion of FcεR1γ [baso Fcer1g (-)], generated by crossing Mcpt8-Cre and Fcer1gflox/flox mice. Baso Fcer1g (-) mice retain IL-3 responsiveness but fail to produce IL-4 upon activation. Mice were infected with Plasmodium yoelii 17XNL to assess the role of basophil FcεR1γ signaling during infection. Basophil FcεR1γ deficiency had no effect on parasitemia. However, female baso Fcer1g (-) mice exhibited significantly increased intestinal permeability by day 6 post-infection (PI) compared to genotype controls. Despite this enhanced barrier disruption, bacterial 16S levels in blood were reduced in female baso Fcer1g (-) mice by day 10 PI relative to female controls and mutant males. Increased permeability was associated with elevated ileal IL-6 and CCL4, and increased plasma CCL3 and CCL5 at day 6 PI. At day 10 PI, reduced bacteremia correlated with increased systemic IL-17A and GM-CSF, and reduced IL-10 and Mcpt1, indicating reduced MC activation. These findings demonstrate that basophil FcεR1γ signaling shapes female-biased mucosal and systemic immune responses during malaria, extending our understanding of sex-specific gut-systemic immune crosstalk during infection.

43053495.titulo: A short embedding protocol for diagnostic electron microscopy: long-term implementation and diagnostic outcomes in a high-volume clinical series.
43053495.resumo: Reduzir só a polimerização da resina epóxi para 40 min a 120 °C, mantendo o processamento anterior, preservou a qualidade diagnóstica: em mais de 30.000 casos consecutivos não houve inadequação ligada à inclusão, e a espessura da membrana basal glomerular diferiu 12,7 nm (cerca de 4%) entre métodos. Os autores exigem validação local conforme a resina e o forno.
43053495.resumo_original: Epoxy resin polymerization is a lengthy step in tissue preparation for transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We evaluated whether reducing the polymerization step alone to 40 minutes at 120 °C, with upstream processing unchanged, could maintain diagnostic quality. The protocol has been the sole routine method in a high-volume, accredited clinical TEM laboratory for more than 10 years. Among more than 30,000 consecutive cases, no embedding-related diagnostic inadequacy was identified in consultant pathologist sign-out records. In a prospective, blinded, split-specimen comparison of renal biopsies, both pathologists scored 4 or 5 on every feature for both methods. Nearly all scores were at the upper end of the scale, indicating comparable performance but not establishing statistical equivalence. Glomerular basement membrane thickness was closely similar (mean difference -12.7 nm, ~4%), within measurement variability and below diagnostic detection thresholds. Because curing behavior depends on the resin formulation and oven conditions, local validation is required before implementation.

43058170.titulo: MitoEM 2.0: A Benchmark for Challenging 3D Mitochondria Instance Segmentation from EM Images.
43058170.autores: Liu P, Shen B, … Wei D (9 autores)
43058170.resumo: MitoEM 2.0: benchmark de segmentação 3D de instâncias de mitocôndrias em microscopia eletrônica de volume (FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM, ssSEM) com rótulos verificados, formatos nnU-Net e OME-Zarr e scripts de base. Relevante para a análise da MET de volume da glândula salivar de Anopheles.
43058170.resumo_original: We present MitoEM 2.0, a difficulty-aware extension of the original MitoEM benchmark for training and evaluating three-dimensional (3D) mitochondria instance segmentation in volume electron microscopy. The collection assembles multiscale vEM datasets (FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM, ssSEM) spanning diverse tissues and species, with expert-verified instance labels emphasizing biologically difficult scenarios, including dense mitochondrial packing, hyperfused networks, and thin filamentous connections with ambiguous boundaries. All releases include native-resolution volumes and standardized processed versions, per-volume metadata (voxel size, modality, tissue, splits), and official train/validation/test partitions to enable reproducible benchmarking. Annotations follow a consistent protocol with quality checks and instance reindexing. Data are provided in NIfTI with nnU-Net-compatible layout and OME-Zarr for cloud-aware workflows, alongside machine-readable split files and checksums. Baseline scripts support common training pipelines and size-stratified evaluation. By consolidating challenging volumes and harmonized labels, MitoEM 2.0 facilitates robust model development and fair comparison across methods while supporting reuse in bioimage analysis, algorithm benchmarking, and teaching.

resumo_blocos.racional: Algoritmos de segmentação de instâncias mitocondriais em 3D por microscopia eletrônica de volume (vEM) perdem acurácia em cenários ultracompactos, redes hiperfusionadas e conexões filamentosas delgadas de contorno ambíguo devido à falta de benchmarks multiescala padronizados.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: O MitoEM 2.0 estende o benchmark MitoEM reunindo volumes multiescala de vEM adquiridos por FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM e ssSEM em diferentes tecidos e espécies, com segmentação de instâncias verificada por especialistas e submetida a controle de qualidade e reindexação. Os dados são disponibilizados em resoluções nativas e processadas, nos formatos NIfTI (compatível com nnU-Net) e OME-Zarr para fluxos em nuvem, acompanhados de metadados por volume (tamanho de voxel, modalidade, tecido, partições oficiais de treino/validação/teste), somas de verificação e scripts de linha de base.
resumo_blocos.resultados: O conjunto consolidado oferece volumes anotados especificamente calibrados para situações biologicamente difíceis — empacotamento mitocondrial denso, redes fusionadas e túbulos finos — com partições reproduzíveis e métricas estratificadas por tamanho que permitem treinamento robusto e comparação justa entre métodos de segmentação 3D.
resumo_blocos.ancoragem_luchm: Articulado diretamente ao programa 'Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume & Bioimagem' do LUCHM.
resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Recurso técnico de alto valor imediato para a frente de Microscopia Eletrônica de Volume no CENABIO/UFRJ (FIB-SEM e SBF-SEM), acelerando pipelines de segmentação mitocondrial em NIfTI/nnU-Net e OME-Zarr para reconstruções 3D de protozoários e células de vetores.
resumo_blocos.faisca_lateral: 💡 Treinar ou calibrar modelos nnU-Net a partir dos pesos e partições do MitoEM 2.0 sobre tomogramas FIB-SEM do CENABIO para segmentar mitocôndrias e mapear sítios de contato com acidocalcisomos e gotas lipídicas.

10.64898/2026.09.13.751325.titulo: Thermodynamic, Kinetic, and Structural Basis of Polyspecificity in the Malaria Sugar Transporter PfHT1
10.64898/2026.09.13.751325.resumo: Preprint de biofísica do transportador de hexoses PfHT1 de P. falciparum; versão listada em 18/11 de DOI de setembro. Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
10.64898/2026.09.13.751325.resumo_original: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum relies on the polyspecific sugar transporter PfHT1 for survival in diverse nutrient environments, making the molecular basis of its polyspecificity a potential avenue for antimalarial drug discovery. However, the structural, thermodynamic and kinetic basis of the emergence of polyspecificity in membrane transporters are not established in literature. Despite advances in AI for protein engineering, the design of selective/promiscuous membrane transporter proteins remains challenging as it requires connecting substrate recognition to the energetics of the transport cycle. Here, we examine the molecular origins of polyspecificity in PfHT1 transporter using molecular dynamics simulations of substrate transport and experimental validation of the key residues that tune specificity. From a structural viewpoint, we hypothesize that polyspecific membrane transporter contains flexible structural elements that could reshape the binding pocket in a substrate-dependent manner. For PfHT1, the cracking of the extracellular helix TM7b allows flexible reshaping of the binding pocket similar to the promiscuous enzymes. The thermodynamic signature of polyspecificity emerges in the form of the substrate dependent stabilization of transport-competent states. From a kinetic perspective, this stabilization asymmetrically alters transition kinetics and channels the flux through diverse conformational pathways that facilitate the conformational transitions from outward to inward facing states. To investigate the contribution of the underlying interaction network to sugar specificity, we used graph-attention learning to prioritize mutant transporters with distinct substrate preferences. Distinct glucose- and fructose-dependent growth phenotypes identify positions with differential effects on sugar utilization, providing functional evidence relevant to substrate specificity within the polyspecific transporter. Together, these findings support a mechanism in which structural, thermodynamic and kinetics observables connect polyspecificity to conformational energetics, kinetics, and structural plasticity.

resumo_blocos.racional: O transportador de açúcares PfHT1 é indispensável para a captação de hexoses por Plasmodium falciparum em nichos nutricionais variáveis, mas as bases estruturais, termodinâmicas e cinéticas que permitem sua poliespecificidade — e como explorá-las para inibidores seletivos — permaneciam mal definidas.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Simulações de dinâmica molecular do ciclo completo de transporte de substratos em PfHT1 integradas à validação experimental por mutagênese dirigida de resíduos-chave que calibram a especificidade do bolsão de ligação.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A flexibilidade local derivada da quebra parcial (cracking) da hélice extracelular TM7b remodela dinamicamente o sítio de ligação de PfHT1 de modo dependente do substrato, fornecendo a assinatura estrutural e energética que sustenta sua promiscuidade funcional semelhante à de enzimas poliespecíficas.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Relevante para a frente de metabolismo energético de Plasmodium no LUCHM, conectando biologia estrutural de transportadores de membrana à vulnerabilidade metabólica do parasito frente a variações glicêmicas do hospedeiro.

43044821.titulo: The heteromeric Plasmodium falciparum pantothenate kinase has only one active site and does not require Pf14-3-3I for activity.
43044821.autores: Liu X, Spry C, Saliba KJ (3 autores)
43044821.resumo: Pantotenato quinase heteromérica de P. falciparum tem um único sítio ativo e dispensa uma proteína acessória (JBC). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43044821.resumo_original: Coenzyme A (CoA) is an essential molecule for the intraerythrocytic stage of Plasmodium falciparum. Pantothenate kinase (PanK) catalyses the first step of the CoA biosynthesis pathway and functions as a homodimer in most organisms investigated thus far. P. falciparum possesses a novel heteromeric PanK complex composed of PfPanK1, PfPanK2 and Pf14-3-3I. Using a mutagenesis approach, we generated 10 PfPanK mutants and demonstrate that the PfPanK complex has only one functional active site, with both PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 required for activity by the complex. We also show that PfPanK2 is essential for normal intraerythrocytic parasite proliferation using a conditional knockdown system. 14-3-3 binding motifs generally contain a phosphoserine/threonine residue. Mass spectrometry analyses of phospho-peptide enriched, immunoprecipitated PfPanK samples revealed phosphorylation sites in both PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 that were additional to the previously reported sites. To investigate the role of specific sites in PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 that may be involved in Pf14-3-3I binding, five additional mutants were generated. Mutagenesis of four predicted Pf14-3-3I binding sites in PfPanK1 resulted in a significant reduction in the amount of Pf14-3-3I bound to the PfPanK complex. Heterologous expression of the PfPanK complex in an insect cell system yielded a small amount of soluble protein that assembled in situ into a functional complex. Combined results from heterologous expression and P. falciparum mutagenesis suggest that Pf14-3-3I may not be essential for PfPanK activity but may be important for stabilising the PfPanK complex.

resumo_blocos.racional: A pantotenato quinase (PanK) inicia a síntese de coenzima A (CoA) essencial para a sobrevivência intraeritrocítica de Plasmodium falciparum, mas ao contrário dos homodímeros típicos de outros organismos, o parasito monta um complexo heteromérico peculiar composto por PfPanK1, PfPanK2 e Pf14-3-3I cujo papel catalítico e regulatório de cada subunidade era incerto.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Mutagênese dirigida gerando 10 mutantes de PfPanK, sistema de knockdown condicional para testar essencialidade de PfPanK2 na proliferação sanguínea e imunoprecipitação seguida de espectrometria de massas enriquecida para fosfopeptídeos, complementada por cinco mutantes adicionais nos sítios preditos de ligação a Pf14-3-3I.
resumo_blocos.resultados: Os autores demonstraram que o complexo heteromérico PfPanK possui apenas um sítio ativo funcional, exigindo simultaneamente PfPanK1 e PfPanK2 para atividade catalítica, e que PfPanK2 é essencial para a proliferação intraeritrocítica normal. A fosfoproteômica identificou novos sítios de fosforilação em ambas as subunidades e a mutação de quatro motivos em PfPanK1 dissociou a ligação de Pf14-3-3I sem abolir a atividade enzimática.

resumo_blocos.implicacoes: Conecta-se diretamente ao eixo de pantotenato/CoA e pantazinas discutido na edição de 13/11 (PMID 43019082), explicando a arquitetura estrutural assimétrica da PanK do parasito frente à PanK do mosquito vetor.

43052706.titulo: Genome-wide identification and analysis of RNA secondary structures in response to glucose in Plasmodium falciparum.
43052706.autores: Zhang Y, Zheng G, … Qi Y (8 autores)
43052706.resumo: Em P. falciparum, a restrição curta de glicose alterou a estrutura secundária de RNA (icSHAPE) de mais de 2.721 transcritos no trofozoíto, com mais mudança em 3'UTR do que em 5'UTR e correlação positiva entre flexibilidade e abundância do mRNA. Propõem motivos de RNA responsivos à glicose como elementos reguladores.
43052706.resumo_original:
Food intake has a significant effect on systemic physiology. The growth, development and transmission of malaria-causing Plasmodium parasites rely on carbohydrate utilization, and parasites must rapidly adapt to fluctuating host glucose concentrations throughout their life cycle. However, the precise process by which Plasmodium parasites quickly react and adapt to glucose stress, in general, remains elusive. The goal of this investigation was to determine whether glucose starvation affects the RNA secondary structure of parasites.
In this study, we applied different short-term glucose stresses on parasites to determine the effect of host-derived glucose nutrients on the dynamics of parasite development and RNA secondary structures. We found that the S-type rRNA expression level in the low glucose-treated group was higher than that in the 2 mg/mL control group. The RNA-seq results indicated that glucose significantly affects the expression of genes involved in RNA-related processes, antigenic variation, transport processes, stimulus response, and DNA-related activities. Metabolomics studies also revealed that several types of sugar compounds exhibit a decrease in metabolic activity when subjected to a reduction in glucose supply. Via analysis of three glucose conditions, we identified the RNA secondary structures of more than 2,721 transcripts throughout the intraerythrocytic trophozoite stage. We discovered a positive correlation between mRNA structural flexibility (icSHAPE scores) and transcript abundance (RPKM values), demonstrating a direct association between RNA structural openness and steady-state mRNA levels. Our results revealed structural alterations in the entire transcriptome, including glucose transporters, metabolic enzymes, and the erythrocyte invasion protein family. These genes were mainly enriched in response to stimuli or preferential biological processes. The total number of genes with changes in icSHAPE scores in the UTRs was significantly greater for the 3' UTRs than the 5' UTRs. Furthermore, by comparing icSHAPE reactivity profiles across glucose conditions, we identified candidate cis-acting RNA motifs predominantly located within UTRs, whose structural flexibility changed rapidly in response to glucose fluctuation. We term these glucose-responsive RNA motifs, as they constitute promising regulatory elements for future research into post-transcriptional glucose sensing mechanisms.
Our findings clarify glucose stress-triggered remodeling of in vivo RNA secondary structure during the P. falciparum intraerythrocytic stage, reveal the functional relevance of structural dynamics in parasite environmental adaptation, and lay a foundational resource for future nutrient stress and post-transcriptional regulatory research. These findings show that glucose, the primary carbon source for parasite survival, modulates RNA secondary structural dynamics via nutrient-sensing cascades to modulate parasite proliferation and adaptive development, which offers clues for developing novel antimalarial therapies.

43014996.titulo: Seasonal variation of immature mosquitoes in rice fields and their association with water quality and crop growth stages in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam
43014996.autores: Duong CV, Ngo QKT, Nguyen VV (3 autores)
43014996.resumo: Em arrozal periurbano de Hanói, 3.196 imaturos de seis espécies em duas safras; abundância maior na primavera e no estágio vegetativo; Cx. tritaeniorhynchus associado a profundidade, pH e oxigênio dissolvido, Cx. quinquefasciatus a condutividade e An. barbirostris negativamente a temperatura e condutividade.
43014996.resumo_original: Rice agroecosystems are among the most productive mosquito habitats in Asia, but the ways in which crop phenology and urbanisation-driven environmental changes shape immature mosquito vector populations remain poorly understood. We quantified mosquito larvae and pupae dynamics across two crop seasons in a rice field located in a peri-urban area of Hanoi, Vietnam, using generalised linear models with appropriate error distributions. A total of 3196 immature mosquitoes representing six species were collected. Overall mosquito abundance was significantly higher in spring than in autumn and peaked during the vegetative stage. Species richness did not vary between seasons but declined significantly at later crop stages. Larval-stage structure varied with both season and crop phenology. Early instars were more prevalent in spring and during the reproductive stage, whereas late instars dominated in autumn and declined during the ripening stage. The proportion of pupae decreased during the reproductive stage. Among dominant taxa, Culex tritaeniorhynchus and Anopheles barbirostris showed strong seasonal responses, whereas Cx. quinquefasciatus exhibited no significant temporal variation. Environmental drivers differed among species. Culex tritaeniorhynchus was positively associated with water depth, pH and dissolved oxygen, but negatively associated with conductivity. In contrast, Cx. quinquefasciatus was strongly associated with higher conductivity, while An. barbirostris showed negative associations with temperature and conductivity. These findings indicate that mosquito development in rice fields is jointly structured by crop seasonality and agronomic water management, with early crop stages creating favourable conditions for larval proliferation. The dominance of vector species of epidemiological concern underscores the need to integrate phenology-based habitat management into nuisance and mosquito vector control strategies in Hanoi and similar peri-urban rice-growing landscapes.

43015931.titulo: Risk indicators and composite index for imported malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China: a 10-year study integrating case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data
43015931.autores: Liao Q, Wang J, … Wu Z (5 autores)
43015931.resumo: Índice mensal exploratório de cinco indicadores binários (caso importado, atraso diagnóstico, presença e alta densidade de Anopheles, meteorologia favorável) em Fuzhou, 2016–2025: 663 casos importados (92,2% da África) e cinco meses de alto risco, todos em maio ou junho. Em 37 meses pareados, a densidade de Anopheles correlacionou com precipitação (ρ=0,360) e negativamente com temperatura dois meses antes (ρ=−0,504); o índice não foi validado contra transmissão local.
43015931.resumo_original:
Following China's malaria-free certification in 2021, imported malaria infections and the continued presence of Anopheles mosquitoes pose challenges for preventing local transmission in post-elimination settings. We integrated case, vector, and meteorological surveillance data to describe potential conditions for malaria re-establishment in Fuzhou, China.
We analyzed imported malaria cases reported during 2016-2025, vector surveillance records, and corresponding meteorological data. Five binary indicators-imported case presence, diagnostic delay, Anopheles presence, high Anopheles density, and favorable meteorological conditions-were combined into an exploratory monthly index. Risk scores were tabulated for the 60 months in the May-October surveillance seasons using the available routine surveillance information.
A total of 663 imported malaria cases were reported, of which 611 (92.2%) originated from Africa. In the 37 months with matched vector and meteorological records, concurrent precipitation was positively associated with Anopheles density (Spearman's ρ = 0.360, P = 0.031), whereas mean temperature and dew point temperature 2 months earlier were negatively associated with density (ρ = - 0.504, P = 0.002; and ρ = - 0.578, P < 0.001, respectively). Of the 60 seasonal months, 28 (46.7%) were assigned low-risk scores, 27 (45.0%) moderate-risk scores, and 5 (8.3%) high-risk scores. All five high-risk months occurred in May or June.
The exploratory index identified seasonal variation in the concurrence of routinely monitored indicators, with high-risk scores observed in May and June. Year-round case surveillance and timely diagnosis remain important, alongside vector monitoring during the surveillance season. Uneven monitoring coverage and the lack of validation against local transmission events limit interpretation of the resulting risk categories.

43019102.titulo: Complex non-transmission and widespread insecticide resistance sustain hyperendemic malaria in Penka-Michel, a focus of the Cameroon highlands
43019102.autores: Kiam BC, Ibrahima I, … Nsango SE (15 autores)
43019102.resumo: Malária hiperendêmica mantida por transmissão complexa e resistência a inseticidas generalizada.
43019102.resumo_original:
A 12-month longitudinal entomological study (September 2023-August 2024) in the Western Highlands of Cameroon (Penka-Michel) investigated malaria transmission dynamics and insecticide resistance markers, including target-site resistance (L1014F, N1575Y, G119S-Ace1) and metabolic resistance (E205D-CYP6P3, L119F-GSTe2, CYP6P9a/b) mutations. Malaria transmission was driven by the coexistence of three species: Anopheles funestus (43.7%), Anopheles gambiae (42.9%), and Anopheles ziemanni (13.5%). The study site was hyperendemic with an annual Entomological Inoculation Rate (EIR) of 839.5 infective-bites/human/year. Plasmodium falciparum predominated at 51.9% (68/131), though a significant non-falciparum burden was observed (P. malariae: 14.5%, 19/131; P. ovale: 15.3%, 20/131), including mixed infections (18.3%, 24/131). Anopheles funestus was the principal driver (Infection Rate, IR, of 7.8%) for P. falciparum and P. ovale curtisi, which peaked in the later rainy season (November). Anopheles gambiae (IR=5.4%) primarily vectored P. malariae, maintaining a sustained peak during the dry season (January). Widespread insecticide resistance was marked by high frequencies of target-site and metabolic resistance markers. Possible associations were observed between L119F-GSTe2 mutations with P. ovale curtisi transmission (IRR=1.15, p=0.03), and L1014F-kdr mutation with P. malariae (IRR=2.2, p=0.04). These dynamics underscore the intricate nature of a multifaceted, species-diverse system, where seasonal vector efficiency and insecticide resistance perpetuate the hyperendemicity of the frequently disregarded non-falciparum malaria species.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-026-69358-w.

resumo_blocos.racional: Regiões africanas de altitude com controle vetorial intenso continuam sustentando transmissão hiperendêmica de malária por múltiplos vetores simpátricos e espécies negligenciadas além de Plasmodium falciparum, exigindo vigilância longitudinal de marcadores moleculares de resistência.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Estudo entomológico longitudinal de 12 meses (setembro/2023 a agosto/2024) nas Terras Altas Ocidentais de Camarões (Penka-Michel), identificando fauna anofelina (Anopheles funestus 43,7%, An. gambiae 42,9%, An. ziemanni 13,5%), taxa de inoculação entomológica (EIR), detecção de espécies de Plasmodium e genotipagem de mutações alvo-sítio (L1014F, N1575Y, G119S-Ace1) e metabólicas (E205D-CYP6P3, L119F-GSTe2, CYP6P9a/b).
resumo_blocos.resultados: A área apresentou EIR anual extrema de 839,5 picadas infectantes/pessoa/ano, com P. falciparum em 51,9% das amostras, mas expressiva circulação de P. ovale (15,3%), P. malariae (14,5%) e coinfecções (18,3%). An. funestus dirigiu P. falciparum e P. ovale curtisi na estação chuvosa, enquanto An. gambiae manteve P. malariae na estação seca; detectou-se associação significativa entre L119F-GSTe2 e P. ovale curtisi (IRR=1,15) e entre L1014F-kdr e P. malariae (IRR=2,2).

43031714.titulo: Urbanization development characteristics coincide with elevated Anopheles stephensi habitat suitability.
43031714.autores: Sun Y, Liu W, … Liu Q (9 autores)
43031714.resumo: Modelo de adequabilidade de habitat de Anopheles stephensi ao longo do gradiente de urbanização; atividades de construção ligam urbanização a criadouros artificiais.
43031714.resumo_original: The invasion of Anopheles stephensi into Africa is increasing risks in urban areas, posing challenges to global malaria elimination. Unlike most malaria vectors, Anopheles stephensi is well adapted to urban environments, thereby imposing a substantial burden on urban malaria transmission. Here, we quantify the influence of urbanization on Anopheles stephensi habitat suitability and examine potential underlying mechanisms. Habitat suitability increases along the urbanization gradient, with the highest suitability observed in high-density urban regions. Urbanization increases the habitat suitability, particularly in Africa, with the transition from urban to high-density urban areas showing the greatest increase in suitability. Moreover, we identify construction-related activities as a key pathway linking urbanization to habitat suitability, consistent with the proliferation of artificial larval habitats in built environments. These findings provide a mechanistic understanding of urban-associated risk, inform large-scale malaria predictions to support the integration of vector surveillance with urban planning.

43037378.titulo: Spatial and Spatiotemporal Clustering of Dengue in Jambi Municipality, Indonesia, 2010-2024.
43037378.autores: Syukri M, Salim M, … Billardi A (4 autores)
43037378.resumo: Agrupamento espacial e espaço-temporal de dengue em Jambi, Indonésia (só título e resumo curto lidos).
43037378.resumo_original:
Dengue is a public health problem in Indonesia, particularly in urbanising cities where transmission patterns are spatially heterogeneous and seasonally dynamic. This study aimed to identify the spatial and spatiotemporal clusters of dengue cases in Jambi Municipality, Indonesia. A retrospective ecological study was conducted using dengue surveillance data aggregated across 62 urban villages.
Monthly counts of clinically diagnosed dengue cases reported through routine surveillance between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2024 were obtained from the Jambi Municipality Health Office. Population data were obtained from the Central Bureau of Statistics and cases were analysed at the urban-village level to support local surveillance. Retrospective spatial and space-time cluster analyses were carried out using SaTScan TM with a discrete Poisson model. Monte Carlo hypothesis testing was used to assess statistical significance, and the clusters were visualised with Quantum GIS.
A total of 7,099 clinically diagnosed dengue cases were reported. Purely spatial and space-time analyses identified 24 and 39 significant clusters, respectively. Recurrent high-risk clusters were concentrated mainly in the central and southern parts of the municipality, although their locations varied by year. Among the 39 space-time clusters, 37 were in a minimum of one rainy-season month (October-April), and the other two secondary clusters were limited to the dry season (August 2011 and June 2023.
Dengue showed recurrent small-area clustering and significant overlap with rainy-season months over 15 years, suggesting the need for fine-scale surveillance and spatially targeted vector control.

43037875.titulo: Molecular screening of arboviruses in asymptomatic blood donors from Northern Brazil.
43037875.autores: Calazans AR, da Costa VD, … Alvarez P (20 autores)
43037875.resumo: Em 5.954 pools de seis amostras de doadores do HEMOAM (Amazonas), testados por RT-qPCR ao longo de 18 semanas epidemiológicas, houve 11 pools positivos para CHIKV, 4 para DENV e nenhum para ZIKV, em doadores assintomáticos na estação chuvosa. A positividade é por pool, não por doador.
43037875.resumo_original:
Asymptomatic infections caused by the arboviruses dengue virus (DENV), zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) pose a hidden risk to blood safety, as viremic donors may contribute to transfusion-transmitted infections with severe outcomes.
Viral RNA from 5,954 pools (each pool contains six samples) was extracted using the Chemagic™ Prime™ platform, as part of the Brazilian NAT PLUS system from pooled plasma samples collected at Amazonas Hematology and Hemotherapy Hospital Foundation (HEMOAM) and analyzed by RT-qPCR using the ZC D-Tipagem molecular assay (Bio-Manguinhos).
Over eighteen consecutive epidemiological weeks, 11 CHIKV-positive cases were identified, 4 DENV-positive cases, and no ZIKV-positive detections on the blood bags samples analyzed.
The detection of asymptomatic arboviral infections during the rainy season, when environmental conditions favor mosquito proliferation and arbovirus transmission, suggests ongoing silent viral circulation in the region and reinforces the importance of blood donor surveillance.

43041224.titulo: Exploring the nexus of climate-socioeconomic drivers of dengue transmission: a covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI mechanistic model
43041224.autores: Adeniji A, Miller J, … He Z (4 autores)
43041224.resumo: Modelo determinístico SEIR-SEI com covariáveis de clima e socioeconômicas, simulado com dados de Medellín (Colômbia): aprendizado de máquina ranqueia preditores socioeconômicos, com a população desempregada como principal, e a simulação indica que o desemprego soma-se à temperatura, eleva a transmissão e antecipa o pico.
43041224.resumo_original: A deterministic covariate-augmented SEIR-SEI model is developed and used to gain insight into the nexus between climate and socioeconomic parameters and the transmission dynamics of dengue. The model developed a framework that incorporates two external influences: climate and socioeconomic factors. The model is rigorously analyzed, with disease-free and endemic equilibria investigated, and is simulated using data relevant to Medellín, Colombia. We then employ machine learning algorithms as an empirical feature-selection step to identify and rank socioeconomic predictors of dengue incidence, revealing that the unemployed population is the dominant socioeconomic driver. This finding motivates the selection of unemployment as the socioeconomic covariate in the mechanistic model. From our numerical simulation, we computed using temperature only and combined [temperature + socioeconomic (unemployment)] parameters to determine how their influences drive the epidemic spread. Our model suggests that socioeconomic influence can act as a driver alongside temperature, increasing the transmission rate and leading to an earlier peak. The framework is appropriate for endemic settings where socioeconomic and climatic factors are the primary drivers of transmission dynamics. The approach demonstrates how empirical machine-learning insights can inform covariate selection in mechanistic epidemiological models, thereby strengthening interpretation of how socioeconomic and climatic conditions interact to shape epidemic potential.

10.64898/2026.05.14.722605.titulo: AIedes: a neural-network framework for modelling the distribution and abundance of Aedes albopictus in Europe
10.64898/2026.05.14.722605.resumo: Preprint de rede neural para distribuição e abundância de Ae. albopictus na Europa; versão listada em 18/11 de DOI de maio. Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
10.64898/2026.05.14.722605.resumo_original: Modelling the distribution and abundance of invasive species requires the integration of heterogeneous ecological surveillance data with environmental covariates and reproducible computational workflows. Aedes albopictus is an invasive mosquito species whose ongoing geographical expansion across Europe, driven by climate change, trade, human mobility and urbanisation, is increasing both ecological and public-health concerns. Accurate mapping of its distribution and abundance is therefore essential for monitoring, forecasting and targeted vector-control strategies. Here we present AIedes, a neural-network framework that predicts both the presence and weekly egg abundance of Ae. albopictus across Europe using climate variables and harmonised surveillance data. The model reproduces the large-scale spatial distribution of the species and captures fine-grained spatiotemporal variation in egg-laying activity. To support reproducible evaluation, the framework is trained and validated on newly harmonised, large-scale surveillance and climate datasets, which are publicly available together with the model implementation and code. These resources provide a consistent benchmark for comparing vector distribution and abundance models and offer an extensible workflow for ecological forecasting of invasive mosquito species in other regions where comparable data are available.

43049855.titulo: Climatic Suitability and Disease Burden Divergence in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region.
43049855.resumo: Adequação climática e carga de doença na região do Mediterrâneo Oriental (EcoHealth). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43049855.resumo_original: This study investigates whether climate suitability predicts malaria and leishmaniasis burden in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean countries (2000-2023). Multi-linear regressions models. Climate suitability models were developed using ERA5 reanalysis data and ecological thresholds. Reported malaria and leishmaniasis cases were analysed alongside conflict intensity, health expenditure, and governance indicators. Panel regression and sensitivity analyses assessed explanatory power. Climate suitability showed weak or negative correlations with reported cases, whereas conflict intensity and governance indicators demonstrated substantially stronger statistical associations and explained up to four times more variance in reported disease burden. In Syria, leishmaniasis incidence rose >15-fold during the civil war despite minimal climatic change. Surveillance disruptions in conflict-affected settings may contribute to underreporting, although the magnitude of this effect could not be directly quantified. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the study's main conclusions remained robust across a range of plausible underreporting assumptions. Climate appears to define ecological boundaries of transmission, whereas socio-political fragility is more strongly associated with variation in reported disease burden across countries and over time. Climate-only models are insufficient in fragile states; vulnerability and stability metrics must complement climate indicators in policy frameworks.

43051866.titulo: Temporal analysis using machine learning of morbidity and mortality from vector-borne diseases in Brazilian municipalities.
43051866.autores: Nicomedes NP, Costa AS, … Silva DCDCE (5 autores)
43051866.resumo: Análise de 1999 a 2022 de dengue, febre amarela, leishmaniose e malária em municípios brasileiros: malária caiu em morbidade e mortalidade e a mortalidade por dengue subiu de forma monotônica. Os random forests tiveram desempenho preditivo desprezível (R² fora da amostra de -0,03 a 0,08), então a importância das variáveis (urbanização primeiro) é só descritiva.
43051866.resumo_original: This study examined morbidity and mortality from four vector-borne diseases-dengue, yellow fever, leishmaniasis, and malaria-in Brazilian municipalities from 1999 to 2022. Rates were compared between eight triennia (Kruskal-Wallis, Dunn post-hoc) and tested for monotonic trend (Mann-Kendall, Theil-Sen) at national and municipal levels. Because the four diseases differ in vector and transmission ecology, a separate Random Forest was estimated for each disease-outcome combination on the full 1999-2022 municipality-year panel, under a common covariate set, with calendar year as a categorical split variable and covariates standardized within each year; importance uncertainty was estimated by resampling municipalities as clusters. Temporal patterns were heterogeneous, malaria declined consistently in both morbidity and mortality, dengue mortality increased monotonically, dengue morbidity rose in 16.5% of municipalities without a monotonic national trend, yellow fever was confined to the 2017-2018 sylvatic epidemic, and leishmaniasis showed no trend. Municipalities with extreme rates were concentrated in the North, Northeast, and Central-West, regions combining rapid urban growth, social vulnerability, and environmental degradation. Predictive performance was negligible, out-of-bag R2 ranged from -0.03 to 0.08 and fell to -0.05 to 0.02 under cross-validation grouped by municipality, so variable importance is reported as a ranking within low-performing models, not as evidence of prediction or causation. On that basis, the urbanization index was the covariate most frequently ranked first, followed by population density and CO2 emissions. The framework provides a descriptive basis for targeting surveillance under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 3, 10, and 13).

43051869.titulo: Spatiotemporal modeling of climatic effects on dengue transmission across Mexican municipalities.
43051869.autores: Babasola O, Peter OJ, … Oshinubi K (4 autores)
43051869.resumo: Modelagem espaço-temporal de efeitos climáticos na transmissão de dengue em municípios do México (Spatial Spatiotemporal Epidemiol). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.
43051869.resumo_original: Dengue remains one of the fastest expanding mosquito borne viral diseases, with transmission strongly influenced by climatic conditions. In Mexico, recurrent dengue outbreaks show substantial geographic variation across municipalities, yet the extent to which climatic variability and spatial dependence contribute to this heterogeneity remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the spatiotemporal distribution of dengue incidence across Mexican municipalities and quantified associations with climatic variability and spatial dependence using a hierarchical spatial model. Municipality level surveillance data were compiled into a weekly panel of confirmed dengue cases and linked with gridded temperature, rainfall, and relative humidity data. Temporal relationships were assessed using weekly national time series and lagged correlation analysis, while spatial dependence was evaluated using Moran's I statistics. A negative binomial regression model with conditional autoregressive spatial random effects was used to estimate associations between dengue incidence and contemporaneous climatic conditions, with additional adjustment for population density. The results showed pronounced seasonal and interannual variation in dengue incidence, with climatic variables exhibiting distinct temporal associations with dengue activity. Significant positive spatial autocorrelation was observed throughout the study period, with elevated dengue burden concentrated primarily along the Gulf of Mexico, the Yucatán Peninsula, and parts of the Pacific coast. The spatial model showed positive associations of temperature and population density with dengue incidence, while substantial residual spatial variation remained after adjustment for the measured covariates. These findings indicate that climatic, demographic, and spatial processes contribute to geographic variation in dengue transmission across Mexico and support spatially explicit approaches for targeted surveillance and prevention.

43061609.titulo: Spatio-Temporal Modeling of Malaria Occurrence Probability Using Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing and Machine Learning.
43061609.autores: Hassanpour G, Youssefi F, … Hanafi-Bojd AA (5 autores)
43061609.resumo: Modelagem espaço-temporal da probabilidade de malária com sensoriamento remoto multissensor e aprendizado de máquina.
43061609.resumo_original:
Reliable mapping of malaria occurrence requires validation across environmentally distinct years and careful separation of model-derived probability from transmission intensity. This study developed a multi-sensor remote sensing and machine-learning framework for mapping annual malaria case occurrence in southeastern Iran.
Annual median composites of Soil Water Index (SWI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Land Surface Temperature (LST) were generated from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 at 30m resolution. After quality control, 82, 168, 775 and 483 malaria case locations were retained for the Solar Hijri years 1400-1403 (2021-2025). Five spatially balanced pseudo-absence realizations were generated annually at a 1:1 ratio with a 300m exclusion buffer. Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated through complete four-fold leave-one-year-out validation with nested tuning. Performance, bootstrap confidence intervals, uncertainty, Getis-Ord Gi* clusters and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) were assessed.
Across 20 outer evaluations, RF achieved ROC-AUC 0.685±0.045, PR-AUC 0.693±0.040, balanced accuracy 0.624±0.026 and Brier score 0.230±0.015. XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC 0.687±0.044, PR-AUC 0.691±0.043, balanced accuracy 0.625±0.033 and Brier score 0.231±0.015. Year-specific ROC-AUC ranged from 0.624 to 0.726. LST was the dominant predictor (48.27%), followed by NDVI (37.04%) and SWI (14.69%). Only 3.46-6.10% of pixels exceeded probability 0.70. Mean uncertainty was low (0.030-0.032) but spatially heterogeneous.
Both algorithms showed moderate, comparable performance with year-dependent variation. Maps provide relative probabilities for prioritizing field surveillance, not transmission estimates.

43061606.titulo: Integrating Local Occurrence Records and Monthly Spatiotemporal Thermal Analysis to Predict Current and Future High-Risk Areas of Aedes albopictus in Guilan Province, Iran.
43061606.autores: Karimi S, Jamshidi E, … Hanafi-Bojd AA (7 autores)
43061606.resumo: Registros locais de ocorrência e análise térmica mensal para prever distribuição atual e futura de vetor (J Arthropod Borne Dis); método de modelagem de distribuição.
43061606.resumo_original:
Aedes albopictus, a key vector of arboviral diseases, has already been detected in Guilan Province, Iran, and is emerging as a public health concern in the country. This study aimed to identify monthly high-risk areas of Ae. albopictus and predict its distribution in Guilan Province using ecological niche modeling under current and projected climate scenarios. Guilan Province, with its high annual influx of travellers and active maritime ports, represents a strategic area for monitoring Ae. albopictus establishment.
A total of 200 occurrence points were obtained from local entomological surveys and health authorities. Four MaxEnt models were developed: current baseline (bioclimatic variables + elevation); current enhanced (bioclimatic variables + elevation + LST, NDVI, NDWI and population); and two future scenarios (SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5, year 2030, CMIP6). Model performance was excellent, with AUC values of 0.909 and 0.908 for the baseline and enhanced models, respectively. Monthly thermal suitability maps were generated based on 2024 meteorological data using the optimal temperature range of 15-35 °C.
Under the SSP5-8.5 scenario, risk areas expanded, and the monthly analysis indicated that nearly the entire Guilan Province exhibited suitable conditions for seven months of the year. The warm months showed the highest probability of Ae. albopictus presence across the province.
These findings provide critical insights for targeted vector surveillance and control strategies in the region.

43059927.titulo: Neighborhood-scale modeling of Culex tarsalis abundance and West Nile virus infection prevalence.
43059927.autores: Wong TS, Brooks W, … Barker CM (7 autores)
43059927.resumo: Preprint: modelagem em escala de bairro da abundância de Culex tarsalis e da prevalência de infecção por vírus do Nilo Ocidental; relevante para desenho de coleta de Culex.
43059927.resumo_original: Prevention of West Nile virus (WNV) transmission relies heavily on vector surveillance and control. Current methods of population reduction are often reactive, guided by field surveillance. Vector control measures would benefit from neighborhood-scale, spatiotemporal predictions of WNV risk that could facilitate proactive, targeted surveillance to locations and times where vector and virus activity is expected to be highest. To determine the potential of predictions at this spatial scale, we approached model development in two phases: (1) inferential generalized additive models were developed using high-density mosquito data collected across Davis, CA that identified causal associations between neighborhood-scale spatial features and relative abundance or WNV infection prevalence in Culex tarsalis; (2) Bayesian predictive models for Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence were constructed by incorporating neighborhood-scale spatial variables with temporal and climatic predictors, using historical vector surveillance data from Davis between 2006 - 2024. Inferential analyses revealed significant, time-dependent effects of nearby rice fields and distance from urban edge on Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence. Final predictive models included terms for spatial, meteorologic, and temporal variables, and performed well for Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence when challenged with novel data from Davis or the neighboring town of Woodland, CA. Results support the potential of neighborhood-scale models to predict WNV vector activity and inform vector control efforts, including routine operational control and placement of field trials.

43058501.titulo: Early detection of dengue outbreaks from routine primary health care records: evaluation by an extended version of the Mixed Model of Artificial Intelligence and Next-Generation (MMAING).
43058501.autores: Borges DGF, Coutinho ER, … Andrade RFS (13 autores)
43058501.resumo: Detecção precoce de surtos de dengue a partir de registros de atenção primária, com versão estendida de um método de detecção; alinhado à frente de vigilância em alta resolução.
43058501.resumo_original:
A recently proposed surveillance framework is used to detect arbovirus outbreaks. It mixes traditional compartmental models with artificial intelligence techniques applied to large volumes of unconventional data on syndromic events, environment, and social information, and its performance is evaluated in the early identification of dengue epidemic events in Brazil at municipal level.
We evaluated an extended version of the MMAING model, referred to as MMAING-Arbo, developed to enable the early detection of dengue outbreaks based on primary health care (PHC) encounters associated with specific arboviral syndromes at the municipal level in Brazil. The analysis covered the period from January 1, 2023, to July 1, 2024, encompassing 2,767 municipalities (49.68% of all municipalities in the country) and identifying a total of 3,478 epidemic events of varying duration observed in the PHC data.
The results obtained with MMAING-Arbo indicate that the proposed approach consistently issues early warning signals (EWS) for a high proportion of identified dengue outbreaks. The comparative evaluation with EARS demonstrated that MMAING-Arbo performs comparably to or outperforms the EARS variants (C1, C2, and C3) across different epidemiological contexts, with performances varying according to municipal population size. In particular, MMAING-Arbo showed a lower alarm burden per outbreak in larger municipalities, while the EARS-C2 variant achieved higher sensitivity and timeliness in smaller ones.
The analysis of PHC data for multiple mosquito-borne diseases using MMAING-Arbo yields promising results and indicates it might be a valuable tool to issue EWS of emerging outbreaks in real-life conditions. These findings reinforce the importance that future surveillance systems include data-driven approaches that benefit from the integration of multiple models, strengthening sensitivity, specificity, and timeliness of EWS.

43059460.titulo: Autochthonous dengue outbreak spreading from a holiday site to visitors' places of residence, Tuscany, Italy, August to October 2026.
43059460.autores: Sacco C, Cosma C, … Pezzotti P (44 autores)
43059460.revista: Euro surveillance : bulletin Europeen sur les maladies transmissibles = European communicable disease bulletin
43059460.resumo: Surto autóctone de dengue partindo de um sítio de férias na Toscana, Itália, com dispersão para locais de residência dos visitantes (Euro Surveill).
43059460.resumo_original: Between August and October 2026, 49 autochthonous dengue cases were notified in Italy. Of these, 42 were exposed at a Tuscan coastal holiday site, and diagnosed after returning home, in 14 municipalities across seven provinces. Seven additional cases were identified, six in two areas where viraemic cases returned home and one near the holiday site. Dengue virus serotype 2, lineage 2II_F.1.1.5, was identified. When exposure occurs at holiday destinations, investigation and vector control should extend to places where cases reside.

43058881.titulo: Bacterial and fungal diversity in Anopheles larval habitats with different productivities.
43058881.autores: Forson AO, Afrane YA, … Hurwitz I (7 autores)
43058881.resumo: Comunidades bacterianas (16S) e fúngicas (ITS) em criadouros de Anopheles no sul de Gana distinguem habitats de alta, baixa e nenhuma produtividade larval (Paraclostridium bifermentans e Bacillus em alta; Acinetobacter variabilis e Lactococcus garvieae em baixa). Microbiota larval, sem desfecho de competência.
43058881.resumo_original:
Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes develop in diverse aquatic habitats, where microbial communities influence oviposition, larval growth, and survival. This study characterized bacterial and fungal communities across Anopheles larval habitats of differing productivity in southern Ghana.
Larval densities were monitored bi-weekly over 6 months. Water and larval samples were collected for bacterial (16S rRNA gene) and fungal (ITS) amplicon sequencing. Based on the consistency of Anopheles larval presence throughout the monitoring period, habitats were classified as high-productive (larvae present at every visit), low-productive (intermittent larval presence), or non-productive (larvae consistently absent).
The study revealed that distinct microbial signatures were associated with habitat productivity. Linear discriminant analysis identified Paraclostridium bifermentans and Bacillus spp. as indicator taxa for high-productive habitats, while Acinetobacter variabilis and Lactococcus garvieae were associated with low-productive habitats. For fungi, Cladosporium halotolerans and Aspergillus penicillioides were the primary discriminant taxa associated with high-productive habitats, while Candida tropicalis and Pichia kudriavzevii characterized low-productive habitats. Beta-diversity analyses revealed significant differences in bacterial communities between productive and non-productive habitats (PERMANOVA, p = 0.006), whereas fungal communities showed no significant separation.
These findings highlight an association between microbial assemblages and larval-habitat suitability and underscore the potential of microbiota-informed strategies to enhance vector surveillance and targeted larval control.

resumo_blocos.racional: Comunidades microbianas de criadouros aquáticos influenciam oviposição, desenvolvimento e sobrevivência de larvas de Anopheles gambiae, mas a contribuição relativa de bactérias e fungos para distinguir habitats de alta e baixa produtividade larval ainda precisava ser caracterizada.
resumo_blocos.metodologia: Criadores naturais de Anopheles no sul de Gana foram monitorados quinzenalmente por 6 meses e classificados em alta produtividade (larvas presentes em todas as visitas), baixa produtividade (presença intermitente) ou não produtivos (ausência constante). Amostras de água e larvas passaram por sequenciamento de amplicons bacterianos (16S rRNA) e fúngicos (ITS), com análise de diversidade beta (PERMANOVA) e análise discriminante linear.
resumo_blocos.resultados: A diversidade beta bacteriana diferiu significativamente entre criadouros produtivos e não produtivos (PERMANOVA, p = 0,006), ao passo que as comunidades fúngicas não mostraram separação global significativa. Como táxons indicadores de alta produtividade destacaram-se as bactérias Paraclostridium bifermentans e Bacillus spp. e os fungos Cladosporium halotolerans e Aspergillus penicillioides, enquanto Acinetobacter variabilis, Lactococcus garvieae, Candida tropicalis e Pichia kudriavzevii associaram-se a habitats de baixa produtividade.

43014904.titulo: Immune impairments in the offspring following parental cadmium exposure in Drosophila melanogaster
43014904.autores: Shaikh FH, D'Souza LC, … Sharma A (5 autores)
43014904.resumo: Prole não exposta de Drosophila cujos pais receberam cádmio por 20 dias tem menos hemócitos, acúmulo de progenitores na glândula linfática, fagocitose menor, coagulação mais lenta e queda de Toll-9, PGRP-LC e peptídeos antimicrobianos.
43014904.resumo_original: Chronic exposure to environmental toxicants, such as cadmium (Cd), poses significant health risks that may extend across generations. However, studies demonstrating immune dysregulation following parental exposure to Cd are limited. Hence, this study aimed to investigate the intergenerational impact of chronic parental Cd exposure on immune homeostasis using Drosophila melanogaster as a model. Parental flies were exposed to two concentrations of cadmium chloride (2 and 20 μg/mL) for 20 days, and multiple endpoints, including the hematopoietic progenitor population, differentiated hemocytes (Drosophila immune cells), circulatory hemocytes and their function (phagocytotic and clotting time), expression of pattern recognition receptors, and antimicrobial peptides, were assessed in their unexposed progeny. The results showed that offspring of chronically Cd-exposed parents experienced a reduced hemocyte population, exhibiting an accumulation of hemocyte progenitors in the lymph glands (Drosophila hematopoietic organs). Reduction in the total number of circulatory hemocytes, decreased phagocytic activity, prolonged clotting time, and downregulation of key pattern recognition receptors (Toll-9, Peptidoglycan Recognition Protein LC (PGRP-LC)) were also observed. Likewise, humoral immunity was also compromised, as evidenced by reduced levels of antimicrobial peptides (Diptericin, Attacin, Drosomycin). Overall, these results suggest that prolonged parental Cd exposure significantly impairs the cellular and humoral immune responses of offspring, indicating its potential to induce intergenerational immune perturbations.

43049467.titulo: Fixation Matters: Multidimensional Effects of Chemical Preparation on Morphology and SEM Image Texture Features of Extremophilic Bacteria
43049467.resumo: Compara glutaraldeído 2,5% e Karnovsky, em 1, 3 e 24 h, com e sem pós-fixação com tetróxido de ósmio, em três bactérias Gram-positivas (duas poliextremófilas e uma mesófila), avaliando morfometria de célula e características de textura da imagem de MEV.
43049467.resumo_original: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is widely used to investigate bacterial morphology and surface-associated features; however, sample preparation protocols may introduce artifacts that influence the interpretation of morphometric measurements and image characteristics observed in SEM micrographs. This issue is particularly relevant for extremophilic microorganisms, whose specialized cell envelopes may respond differently to chemical fixation. In this study, we evaluated two aldehyde-based fixation protocols (2.5% glutaraldehyde and Karnovsky's solution), each tested at three fixation times (1, 3, and 24 h) and with or without osmium tetroxide (OsO4) postfixation, in three Gram-positive bacterial strains: the polyextremophiles Exiguobacterium sp. S17 and Nesterenkonia sp. Act20 and the mesophile Kocuria rosea CH-021. Morphometric responses were assessed using cell surface area and surface-to-volume ratio (S/V), together with SEM image-texture analysis using Haralick-based features. Fixation conditions produced significant strain-dependent differences in both morphometric and image-texture outcomes. The magnitude of morphometric variability differed among strains, and SEM image-texture patterns were not always paralleled by morphometric measurements. These findings indicate that bacterial responses to fixation conditions are strain-dependent and support the combined use of cellular geometry and SEM image-texture descriptors for quantitative comparison of preparation conditions within a standardized SEM workflow.

43038261.titulo: Intelligent classification of medically and veterinary important mosquito vectors using self-distillation-enhanced supervised learning.
43038261.autores: Chuwongin S, Kaewthamasorn M, … Kittichai V (8 autores)
43038261.resumo: O modelo auto-supervisionado DINOv2-L14 classificou 30 espécies de mosquito a partir de imagens (acurácia 99,2%, F1 86,1%, AUC 0,996) e superou uma ResNet101; com 20% dos dados (11 a 13 imagens por classe) igualou o baseline treinado com tudo. O conjunto é desbalanceado (15 a 124 imagens por classe).
43038261.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. In response to these challenges, this study harnesses the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to develop a robust, accessible diagnostic tool. We introduce an innovative application of the Distillation of knowledge with NO labels v2 (DINOv2-l14) algorithm, a self-supervised learning (SSL) model, for the classification of 30 distinct mosquito species from image data. A key focus was enabling the model to learn effectively from a highly imbalanced dataset, where the number of images per class ranged from 15 to 124. We also investigated the data efficiency of SSL by determining the minimum data partition required to match the performance of a conventional supervised model. Our image processing pipeline involved cropping, padding, and dividing images into 14 × 14 patches before converting them into embedded vectors for classification. The fully trained DINOv2-l14 model significantly outperformed a selected ResNet101 baseline, achieving 99.2% accuracy, 97.7% specificity, an F1 score of 86.1%, and a robust area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.996. Most notably, when fine-tuned on just 20% of the available data (averaging 11-13 images per class), the SSL model achieved performance comparable to the baseline model trained on the entire dataset, demonstrating exceptional data efficiency. Although limitations exist, including dataset imbalance and a lack of standardization for broader application, the model's high performance across five-fold cross-validation and strong Cohen's Kappa coefficients (up to 0.836) confirm its reliability. This work validates a novel, efficient, and highly accurate AI-driven approach to mosquito identification. By integrating such a model into a mobile application using an embedding AI framework, this technology holds significant promise for empowering field personnel with a practical, powerful tool to enhance vector surveillance and control programs worldwide.

43041013.titulo: Targeting the Lactate-Lactylation Axis in Cancer Immunotherapy Resistance: From Tumor Acidosis to Context-Dependent Immune Reprogramming
43041013.autores: Liang X, Lin M, … Li Y (6 autores)
43041013.resumo: Revisão que trata o lactato como regulador imunometabólico no microambiente tumoral e a lactilação de histonas e proteínas como elo entre disponibilidade de lactato e cromatina; propõe a lactilação como mediador plausível da conversão de estresse metabólico sustentado em reprogramação imune persistente e diz que persistência após a retirada do estímulo e memória celular ainda não foram demonstradas no câncer.
43041013.resumo_original: Lactate is now recognized as an active immunometabolic regulator in the tumor microenvironment (TME), not simply as a glycolytic byproduct. Its immunological effects arise through several related but distinct routes. Extracellular acidosis, glucose competition, and impaired monocarboxylate transporter-dependent flux can impair CD8+ T cells, natural killer cells, and dendritic cells. Lactate- and proton-sensing receptors can also favor suppressive myeloid and regulatory-cell programs. Histone and non-histone lactylation add another layer by linking lactate availability to chromatin regulation and protein function. During sustained or repeated metabolic stress, these processes may support regulatory T-cell fitness, suppressive programs in tumor-associated macrophages and myeloid-derived suppressor cells, checkpoint expression, and resistance to immunotherapy. Lactylation is a plausible mediator through which sustained metabolic stress may be converted into persistent immune reprogramming; however, post-withdrawal persistence and cellular memory remain to be demonstrated in cancer. We distinguish lactate-dependent regulation from acidosis and evaluate the links to immune dysfunction and treatment resistance by their temporal, causal, and clinical support. This framework defines tests of post-exposure persistence and connects mechanistic evidence and pharmacological specificity to biomarker development and mechanism-matched trial design.

43057496.titulo: Antimalarial activity of Croton caudatus Geiseler leaf extract and its ability to reduce experimental cerebral malaria pathogenesis.
43057496.autores: Chatterjee A, Singh N, … Nagaraj VA (7 autores)
43057496.resumo: Extrato de folha de Croton caudatus: atividade contra P. falciparum 3D7 (CI50 6,84 µg/mL da fração hexano), inibição de β-hematina, efeito gametocitocida e, em P. berghei ANKA, preservação da barreira hematoencefálica e menos infiltração imune no modelo de malária cerebral experimental. Mecanismo é de heme/ROS; interessa pelo painel de ECM (integridade de BHE e infiltrado) como referência de leitura.
43057496.resumo_original:
Croton caudatus Geiseler is widely used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including malaria. However, scientific evidences supporting its antimalarial activity and the associated molecular mechanisms, and its potential to reduce severe malaria complications are lacking.
The present study was aimed to evaluate the antimalarial activity of C. caudatus leaf extract and its fractions, and to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Methanolic leaf extract of C. caudatus (CcLE) was fractionated into water (CcWater), butanol (CcBut), chloroform (CcChl), and hexane (CcHex) fractions. In vitro antiplasmodial activity was assessed against two different strains of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf): Pf3D7 and PfCam3.IR539T, alongside cytotoxicity and hemolysis assays. Phytochemical profiling of the most active fraction was performed by chemical fingerprinting. Mechanistic studies included β-hematin polymerization inhibition, hemozoin quantification, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement. Acute oral toxicity and in vivo antimalarial efficacy were carried out in Plasmodium berghei (Pb) ANKA-infected BALB/c mice. Experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) studies were performed in Pb ANKA-infected C57BL/6 mice through the assessment of blood-brain barrier integrity, inflammatory marker expression, and immune cell infiltration analyses. Examining the gametocyte numbers and ex vivo exflagellation assays were carried out with Pb ANKA-infected mouse blood to assess the gametocytocidal activity.
CcHex exhibited the highest antiplasmodial activity against Pf 3D7 (IC50 = 6.84 ± 0.61 μg/mL) without detectable cytotoxic or hemolytic effects. Phytochemical analysis suggested the presence of bioactive metabolites associated with antimalarial activity. CcHex inhibited β-hematin formation in a cell-free assay and reduced hemozoin levels in Pf3D7 parasites, supporting its potential to interfere with parasite heme detoxification. It also increased intracellular ROS levels in the parasites, suggesting the disruption of heme detoxification. Further, CcHex treatment reduced gametocyte formation and impaired male gametocyte exflagellation, indicating gametocytocidal activity. Acute toxicity studies demonstrated a favourable safety profile. In Pb-infected Balb/c mice, CcHex treatment produced ∼62% parasite suppression at 1000 mg/kg/day. Importantly, CcHex treatment could protect against ECM by preserving blood-brain barrier integrity, and significantly reducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IFN-γ), chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCR3), the adhesion molecule ICAM-1, and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the brain.
The present study demonstrates that C. caudatus, a traditionally used medicinal plant, possesses significant antiplasmodial activity, exhibits protective effects against ECM, and impairs male gametocyte exflagellation. CcHex showed potent antimalarial efficacy through inhibition of parasite heme detoxification, induction of oxidative stress, and modulation of host inflammatory responses. These results support the ethnopharmacological use of C. caudatus and highlight its potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals for the development of novel antimalarials and adjunctive therapies against severe malaria.

resumo_blocos.racional: Embora Croton caudatus Geiseler seja empregado na medicina tradicional contra a malária, faltavam evidências experimentais sobre sua atividade antiplasmódica, seus alvos moleculares no parasito e sua capacidade de conter a patogênese da malária cerebral experimental (ECM).

Testaram-se ainda toxicidade oral aguda e supressão parasitária em camundongos BALB/c com Plasmodium berghei ANKA (PbA), integridade da barreira hematoencefálica, expressão de citocinas/quimiocinas e infiltrado imune cerebral em camundongos C57BL/6 com ECM, além de gametocitemia e exflagelação ex vivo.

43017141.titulo: Comparative analysis of serum antibody responses and immune landscapes in patients with acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and Chikungunya virus infections
43017141.autores: Zhang Y, Zhang S, … Wu N (13 autores)
43017141.resumo: 80 soros (DENV-1 n=29, DENV-2 n=10, CHIKV n=26, controles n=15): ativação associada a interferon e inflamação sistêmica contida nos três grupos, com perfis de mediadores distintos; associações compartilhadas envolvendo IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4 e CXCL1 após correção de Benjamini-Hochberg.
43017141.resumo_original:
Dengue virus (DENV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) are major mosquito-borne arboviruses that increasingly co-circulate in tropical and subtropical regions, including southern China. However, the extent to which these viruses induce shared or distinct host immune responses remains poorly understood. This study aimed to comparatively characterize immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections.
A total of 80 serum samples were analyzed, including 65 samples from patients with laboratory-confirmed DENV-1 (n = 29), DENV-2 (n = 10), or CHIKV (n = 26) infections and 15 healthy controls.Viral RNA was detected by real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction. Virus-specific IgM and IgG responses were measured by Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and serum cytokines were quantified using a multiplex assay. Group comparisons used nonparametric tests, and associations among antibody responses, cytokine concentrations, and viral RNA levels were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Multiple comparisons were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure.
The three infections shared features of interferon-associated immune activation and relatively restrained systemic inflammation but exhibited distinct immune mediator profiles, characterized by differential inflammatory mediator and growth factor responses. After multiple-testing correction, cytokine-cytokine correlation analysis revealed both shared and infection-specific patterns of immune mediator covariation, with shared associations involving IL-9, TNF-β, CCL4, and CXCL1 across all three infection groups. Positive associations between pathogen-specific IgM responses and Ct values were observed across the infections, although the association was not statistically significant for DENV-2 after multiple-testing correction. IgG responses showed a similar association only in DENV-1 infection. Integration of cytokine and antibody profiles further revealed distinct immune association patterns: DENV-1 showed broader associations involving viral RNA levels, inflammatory mediators, and humoral responses, whereas CHIKV displayed a more restricted pattern centered on associations between inflammatory mediators and IgM responses.
These findings reveal shared and distinct immune responses during acute DENV-1, DENV-2, and CHIKV infections and provide a comparative framework for investigating virus-associated immune regulation during acute arboviral infections.
